countries.name: Andorra
countries.summary: Andorra is an EU Annex I listed territory (pets from it enter the EU without titer test or point-of-entry check). No dedicated official import page was found; in practice pets arrive via Spain or France, so that country's EU entry rules apply (microchip, rabies vaccination, EU pet passport or EU health certificate; titer test from unlisted countries).
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid. (as required by the EU country of arrival)
countries.rabies_titer: Per EU rules of the arrival country: required only from unlisted third countries.
countries.parasite_treatment: None identified (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None identified if EU requirements are met.
countries.timeline: As for the EU arrival country: at least 4 weeks from EU/listed origin; 4+ months from unlisted origin.
countries.restricted_breeds: Not verified.
countries.private_aviation: No airport in Andorra; private jets land in Spain (e.g. Andorra-La Seu d'Urgell, Barcelona) or France (e.g. Toulouse); EU entry rules and points of entry of that country apply for third-country arrivals.
countries.export: Leaving: EU treats this territory as Annex I listed (pet passport/certificate, no titer, no point-of-entry requirement). Local export procedure not verified.
countries.authority: Government of Andorra - Ministry of Agriculture (veterinary service); not verified
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: EU pet passport (from EU) or EU animal health certificate + non-commercial declaration (from third countries), as required by the EU arrival country.

countries.name: United Arab Emirates
countries.summary: A MOCCAE import permit is required before arrival (valid 90 days), followed by a MOCCAE release permit and inspection at the port of entry. Pets from countries not on MOCCAE's low-risk list (including the USA, Canada, France, Germany and Italy per the official list) also need a rabies antibody titre test of at least 0.5 IU/ml.
countries.microchip: Mandatory permanent microchip; the chip number on the health certificate must match the implanted chip. ISO 11784/11785 is not named on the MOCCAE page but is standard.
countries.rabies_titer: High-risk origins only (any country not on MOCCAE's low-risk list): FAVN/RNATT of at least 0.5 IU/ml from a lab approved by the exporting country's authority. The sample must be at least 21 days after a first or lapsed rabies vaccination, or any time if the booster is continuous. The result is valid 365 days if the vaccination stays continuous and no booster is given; otherwise retest. Official MOCCAE low-risk list: Australia, Austria, Andorra, Bahrain, Barbados, Belgium, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Fiji, Finland, French Polynesia, Falkland Islands, Hong Kong, Iceland, Ireland, Jamaica, Japan, Kuwait, Liechtenstein, Mauritius, Malta, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Portugal, Singapore, San Marino, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom, Vanuatu, Netherlands, Bulgaria, Slovenia, Palau, Latvia, Albania, Croatia, Maldives, Spain (excluding Melilla and Ceuta), Cyprus, Korea, Montenegro, Seychelles, Suriname, Micronesia, Greece, Marshall Islands, Bahamas, Lithuania, Macedonia. Note: IATA Traveldoc's copy also lists Germany and Italy, but the MOCCAE page does not, so confirm with MOCCAE before relying on it. USDA states a titre is required for US-origin pets, with the sample no more than 12 months before travel.
countries.parasite_treatment: Preventive treatment for internal and external parasites within 14 days before shipment, recorded on the health certificate or passport. USDA suggests fipronil or permethrin for external parasites and praziquantel for internal parasites.
countries.import_permit: Required. Apply online through MOCCAE digital services before travel. Issued in about 1 working day (5 working days for service, emotional-support or medical dogs). Valid 90 days. Fees: AED 200 per head for the import permit, plus a release permit of AED 500 per dog or AED 250 per cat. Note: the USDA page (last modified Jul 2025) still says 30 days; the MOCCAE page stated 90 days at the previous check (MOCCAE site unreachable at this re-check), so plan within 30 days to be safe. Limit: maximum 2 companion animals per person per year (2 cats, 2 dogs, or 1 of each). Returning resident pets are exempt from the limit.
countries.quarantine: No routine quarantine for compliant pets. Inspection, and lab testing if required, happens on arrival at the MOCCAE port quarantine centre. Non-compliant pets are rejected (re-exported at the owner's expense) or confiscated.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2 months before travel for low-risk origins, and 3–4 months for high-risk origins needing a first titre. Steps: microchip → rabies and core vaccines (first rabies dose at 12 weeks or older) → titre test, if high-risk, at least 21 days after a first rabies dose → MOCCAE import permit (valid 90 days) → parasite treatment within 14 days of travel → official health certificate (USDA: within 10 days) → MOCCAE release permit and inspection on arrival. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~30 days from the USA (high-risk origin under MOCCAE): titer on a continuously vaccinated pet has no post-test waiting period, so the limit is lab turnaround (2-4 weeks) plus the MOCCAE permit and certificate within 10 days. From MOCCAE low-risk origins (e.g. UK, Netherlands, Spain, Portugal, Switzerland): ~14 days. France, Germany, Italy need a titer.
countries.restricted_breeds: Banned (dogs, including mixes): Staffordshire Bull Terrier, American Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, American Bully, Fila Brasileiro, Dogo Argentino, Tibetan Mastiff, Neapolitan Mastiff, Dogue de Bordeaux, Boerboel, Bullmastiff, Cane Corso, Bully Kutta (Alangu or Indian Mastiff), Perro de Presa Canario, Japanese Tosa. Exception for service, emotional-support or medical dogs under specific rules. Cats: Bengal and Serval need a fifth-generation pedigree. Minimum age at import: 12 weeks (low-risk origin) or 15 weeks (high-risk origin).
countries.private_aviation: MOCCAE says pets are shipped 'according to IATA conditions' and released at a MOCCAE quarantine centre. Release documents include a customs declaration or bill of lading. USDA states pets must travel to the UAE as manifested cargo. No official source confirms that a pet may stay in the cabin of a private jet and be cleared at an FBO without being manifested. Plan to list the pet on the aircraft's cargo manifest or air waybill and pre-arrange MOCCAE inspection through the handling agent. Relevant MOCCAE centres: Al Maktoum Airport (DWC), Dubai Airport Cargo Village, Dubai Airport Free Zone, Zayed International Airport (Abu Dhabi), and Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah airports. Confirm with MOCCAE (800 3050, info@moccae.gov.ae) and the FBO before each flight. Transit: no permit is needed for airside transit at the same airport (the pet must be isolated). A MOCCAE transit permit is needed if the pet enters UAE territory.
countries.export: Leaving the UAE requires a MOCCAE veterinary health certificate for export or re-export of live animals, issued after a physical inspection at the export point (e.g. Dubai Airport Cargo Village or Al Maktoum Airport centre). Valid 30 days. Fee AED 100 for a personal consignment of 2 or fewer pets (AED 400 standard). About 1 working day. Not required: certificate of origin or a destination import permit copy for companion animals. Bring the passport or vaccination booklet and any tests the destination requires. MOCCAE's FAQ (quoted in search results, not opened directly) says to present the pet at the export port about 48 hours before departure. Returning residents: pets must have a MOCCAE health certificate on departure and a rabies vaccination valid until return to re-enter under the resident rules.
countries.authority: Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE)
vaccinations: Rabies: valid vaccination given according to the manufacturer's instructions. The first dose may not be given before 12 weeks of age. A first or lapsed vaccination needs 21 days before the titre blood draw. No 21-day wait if the booster is continuous. USDA additionally says at least 21 days before travel.
Dogs: canine distemper (CDV), canine parvovirus, infectious canine hepatitis, leptospirosis (leptospirosis may be replaced by a lab test if the exporting country does not vaccinate).
Cats: feline panleukopenia, feline rhinotracheitis, feline calicivirus.
Vaccination record or passport must show microchip number, species, colour, sex, date of birth, vaccine name, manufacturer, batch number and date.
documents: MOCCAE import permit (valid 90 days from issue; entry with an expired permit is refused)

Official health certificate issued or endorsed by the exporting country's competent veterinary authority (USDA: valid 10 days after issuance; US certificates need original ink USDA signature and embossing)
Vaccination record or passport with microchip number
Rabies titre lab certificate (high-risk origins only; can be recorded on the health certificate)
For release at port: customs declaration or bill of lading showing delivery data
If transiting other countries: proof or attestation that the pet did not mix with other animals in transit
Bengal and Serval cats: fifth-generation pedigree certificate
Service, emotional-support or medical dogs: training certificate, owner medical report, and a non-transfer pledge (5 working days to process)

countries.name: Afghanistan
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.authority: Unknown (Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation and Livestock; current de facto administration)

countries.name: Antigua and Barbuda
countries.summary: An import license from the Veterinary & Livestock Division is required in advance. The application needs rabies and microchip certification and a FAVN titer result. Pets need parasite treatment within 7 days and an APHIS-endorsed health certificate issued within 7 days before arrival. Pit bulls are banned.
countries.microchip: Required; proof of microchipping goes with the license application.
countries.rabies_titer: Rabies FAVN result within accepted levels from an OIE/WOAH-approved lab, submitted with the license application. No waiting period is stated, so confirm with VLD.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasites treated within 7 days of export with approved products, recorded on the certificate (products and dates).
countries.import_permit: Required. Only pets with a duly issued import license are accepted. Apply to the Veterinary & Livestock Division (vld@ab.gov.ag, fax 268-460-1759).
countries.quarantine: No standard quarantine is stated. Non-compliant pets may be refused or confiscated.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2 months before travel: microchip, rabies, FAVN (lab turnaround), then the license, then parasite treatment and the health certificate within 7 days of arrival, then APHIS endorsement.
countries.restricted_breeds: Pit bull-type dogs and mixes may not land. Look-alike dogs need certification from a recognized kennel club stating they are not pit bulls.
countries.authority: Veterinary & Livestock Division, Ministry of Agriculture, Antigua and Barbuda
vaccinations: Rabies: given within 1 year of importation.
documents: Import license.
Medical history including Ehrlichia and Lyme test results (dogs); FIP, FeLV and FIV testing and vaccination history (cats).
Health certificate by a USDA-accredited vet within 7 days before arrival, endorsed by APHIS (original ink endorsement).

countries.name: Anguilla
countries.summary: Get a Government of Anguilla pet import permit and an APHIS-endorsed health certificate valid 14 days. Pets must be 13 weeks or older, ISO-microchipped, rabies-vaccinated at least 30 days before departure, and dewormed after a negative fecal test. Pit bull terriers are prohibited.
countries.microchip: ISO-compliant microchip, verified by the vet.
countries.parasite_treatment: Negative fecal flotation and internal parasite treatment within 21 days before departure. External parasite treatment within 14 days before departure; free of ticks (Amblyomma, Boophilus).
countries.import_permit: Required. Apply through gov.ai (Pet Import/Export requirements page); a fee form is provided, but the amount isn't published.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 5–6 weeks before travel: rabies at least 30 days before departure, permit application, fecal test and deworming within 21 days, health certificate and tick treatment within 14 days, APHIS endorsement.
countries.restricted_breeds: Pit bull terrier type or other 'ferocious' dogs are prohibited and will be seized, unless the Chief Veterinary Officer is satisfied otherwise.
countries.export: Leaving Anguilla: a licensed local vet issues the health certificate, endorsed by the Government Veterinarian if the destination requires it.
countries.authority: Government of Anguilla – Department of Agriculture (Chief Veterinary Officer)
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated vaccine at least 30 days before departure and within its 12- or 36-month validity. Boosters of unexpired vaccines may be under 30 days if the previous vaccination is listed.
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis (adenovirus), parvovirus, parainfluenza and leptospirosis.
Cats: rhinotracheitis, calicivirus, panleukopenia, pneumonitis and FeLV.
documents: Pet Import Permit Application (Cat & Dog), Government of Anguilla Department of Agriculture.
US Veterinary Health Certificate for Anguilla (ISO microchip number, age 13 weeks or older), APHIS-endorsed, valid 14 days after issuance.

countries.name: Albania
countries.summary: EU-style non-commercial pet certificate issued by the origin country's official/accredited vet. A rabies titer test is needed only if the pet comes from, or transits, a country not on the Annex II list. The APHIS-endorsed certificate must be issued within 10 days of travel.
countries.microchip: Required: ISO microchip, or a legible tattoo applied before 3 July 2011, per the EU-model certificate used by Albania
countries.rabies_titer: Not required if the pet travels directly from, or transits only, Annex II-listed or EU countries (the US is covered). Otherwise required per the model certificate: ≥0.5 IU/ml, sample taken ≥30 days after vaccination and ≥3 months before travel. An owner declaration covers transit through unlisted countries
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month if coming from a listed country (4+ months if a titer is needed): microchip → rabies vaccine (wait 21 days) → [titer + 3 months if unlisted origin] → health certificate within 10 days of travel
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development of Albania / National Food Authority (AKU)
vaccinations: Rabies: required. Must be current; per the EU model, given at ≥12 weeks of age, with ≥21 days after the primary vaccination before entry
Young unvaccinated pets: an owner declaration form exists (APHIS 'Pet Not Vaccinated Against Rabies'). Acceptance is not guaranteed; confirm in advance
documents: Albania health certificate for dogs, cats and ferrets (non-commercial). For US origin: issued by a USDA-accredited vet and APHIS-endorsed within 10 days of travel
Owner declaration (non-commercial movement / transit through unlisted country, where applicable)
Rabies vaccination record

countries.name: Armenia
countries.summary: EAEU member with the same rules as Russia. Up to 2 personal dogs/cats may enter on an international passport with rabies and core vaccines and a clinical-exam mark from within 14 days; otherwise an EAEU Form 15 certificate is needed. For US origin, APHIS allows up to 5 pets on Form 15 issued within 5 days of travel.
countries.microchip: Not mandated by EAEU rules; recommended
countries.rabies_titer: Not required (alternative only)
countries.import_permit: Not needed for ≤2 personal pets (EAEU); APHIS states up to 5 without special permission
countries.quarantine: None for compliant personal pets
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month: vaccines ≥20 days before → exam/certificate within 5 days
countries.authority: Food Safety Inspection Body of Armenia (EAEU common veterinary requirements)
vaccinations: Rabies: dogs/cats ≥3 months, ≥20 days before travel unless vaccinated within last 12 months (multi-year vaccine OK while valid)
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, adenovirus, leptospirosis — ≥20 days, ≤12 months before
Cats: panleukopenia — ≥20 days, ≤12 months before
documents: International pet passport with clinical exam mark ≤14 days (≤2 pets), or EAEU Form 15 certificate (APHIS: issued and endorsed within 5 days of travel)

countries.name: Angola
countries.summary: Angola requires an import permit for pets. A USDA Foreign Agricultural Service report (AO2023-0004, Nov 2023) says Angola's Veterinary Services Institute (ISV) issues 'zoosanitary licenses to import pets', and that ISV accepts health certificates issued by APHIS. Angola does not publish its detailed pet conditions (rabies timing, certificate validity), so get the ISV licence and its written conditions before booking.
countries.import_permit: Required. Per the USDA FAS FAIRS export-certificate report AO2023-0004 (29 Nov 2023), ISV (Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry) issues zoosanitary licences for importing pets under Animal Health Law 04/04 and Decree 70/08. For animals and animal products in general, the report says only ISV can issue the import permit, the original must accompany the shipment, it is valid 60 days from issue and covers a single shipment. ISV contact listed in the report: isvetangola@gmail.com.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel: request the ISV zoosanitary licence and its written conditions (processing time unknown) → vet health certificate and government endorsement as ISV instructs → travel within the licence's 60-day validity.
countries.authority: Instituto dos Serviços de Veterinária (ISV), Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, Angola
documents: ISV zoosanitary import licence (original), valid 60 days from issue per the USDA FAS report (general rule for animal import permits)
Veterinary health certificate from the country of origin. ISV accepts APHIS-issued health certificates (USDA FAS AO2023-0004). Exact pet certificate content is not published.
Proof of current rabies vaccination (APHIS general guidance for countries with unknown requirements)

countries.name: Argentina
countries.summary: Accompanied dogs and cats need an International Veterinary Certificate (CVI) issued or endorsed by the official veterinary authority of the origin country (Mercosur rules), presented to SENASA on arrival. Accompanied pets need no prior import permit.
countries.microchip: Not required by SENASA for entry (no microchip requirement on SENASA entry page). If present, record on CVI.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external broad-spectrum antiparasitic treatment within 15 days before CVI issue (or passport endorsement), with products approved in the origin country; record product, active ingredient, date.
countries.import_permit: Not required for pets accompanying their owner. Pets shipped as cargo (unaccompanied) require a prior SENASA border-intervention request at least 24 business hours in advance and pay the internment fee.
countries.quarantine: None routinely. Non-compliant animals may be retained or subjected to sanitary measures at the owner's cost.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks before travel: rabies (≥21 days if first dose) → antiparasitic treatment within 15 days of CVI → vet exam within 10 days of CVI → official CVI/endorsement in origin country → SENASA document/identity check on arrival.
countries.restricted_breeds: SENASA states no breed restrictions for dogs or cats.
countries.private_aviation: SENASA performs documentary, physical and identity checks at the point of entry; no cost for accompanied pets. Confirm SENASA availability at the arrival airport/FBO before booking.
countries.export: Leaving Argentina: SENASA issues the CVI based on destination requirements. Book a SENASA appointment online (up to 30 days ahead), bring private-vet health certificate and vaccination records (originals + copies). For Ezeiza, documents can be emailed up to 10 days before the flight. CVI validity 5/10/up to 60 days depending on destination; returning pets may re-enter Argentina within 60 days on the SENASA-issued CVI if rabies is valid.
countries.authority: SENASA (Servicio Nacional de Sanidad y Calidad Agroalimentaria)
vaccinations: Rabies: required, with a vaccine authorized in the origin country and still valid on the day of entry; a first (primary) vaccination must be given at least 21 days before entry.

Puppies/kittens under 3 months: may enter unvaccinated if the origin authority certifies age and no exposure to urban rabies in the prior 90 days. Animals from WOAH rabies-free countries/zones are exempt if stated on the CVI.
documents: Original CVI from the origin country's official veterinary authority (Spanish must be one of the languages), valid 60 calendar days from issue provided rabies vaccination remains valid
Clinical exam by a registered vet within 10 days before CVI issue (stated on the CVI)
Alternatively: a valid official pet passport endorsed by the origin's veterinary authority before shipment, containing the same health data (Spanish or English accepted)

countries.name: American Samoa
countries.summary: Dog and cat imports to American Samoa are banned by law except: (1) from Hawaii, New Zealand or Australia under Department of Agriculture conditions; (2) from the continental US, Guam or former Trust Territories, but only after mandatory quarantine in Hawaii. EU and other origins are not on the allowed list. Rabies vaccination at least 30 days before arrival. Non-compliant pets are returned at the owner's cost or destroyed.
countries.rabies_titer: Not specified in the territorial code. Pets from the US mainland must meet Hawaii's requirements (FAVN-based), since they must quarantine in Hawaii.
countries.import_permit: Entry is only under conditions set by the Director of Agriculture; get them in writing from the American Samoa Department of Agriculture before travel.
countries.quarantine: Hawaii, NZ or Australia origin: per DOA conditions. Continental US, Guam or Trust Territories origin: mandatory quarantine in Hawaii for a period set by the Department of Agriculture (A.S.A.C. 24.0317(2)).
countries.timeline: Get DOA conditions first. US mainland pets must first complete Hawaii's import programme and the required quarantine. Length is set by DOA and Hawaii rules, so no fixed lead time.
countries.restricted_breeds: Not in the code reviewed. Secondary sources report Pit Bull types and crosses are banned; confirm with DOA.
countries.private_aviation: A direct private flight from the US mainland or Europe with a pet is not allowed. US-mainland pets must quarantine in Hawaii first, and EU-origin pets are not an allowed origin. Pets arriving without full prior compliance are returned or destroyed.
countries.export: For export to New Zealand, MPI treats American Samoa as Category 2 (rabies-free); the crate needs a vet-applied seal on departure day (USDA).
countries.authority: American Samoa Department of Agriculture (Director of Agriculture)
vaccinations: Rabies: certificate from a salaried government vet (or other competent authority) that the pet was vaccinated no later than 30 days before arrival (A.S.A.C. 24.0307(d)).
documents: Government-vet rabies vaccination certificate (vaccinated at least 30 days before arrival)
Proof of compliance with Department of Agriculture entry conditions (permit/conditions set by the Director; get them before travel)
US mainland/Guam origin: proof of the mandatory Hawaii quarantine

countries.name: Austria
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
countries.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry.
countries.restricted_breeds: No federal import ban identified; several Länder (e.g. Vienna, Lower Austria, Vorarlberg) have listed-dog rules (licence/muzzle/leash) for residents - verify with the destination Land.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Airport points of entry on the list published via the European Commission (dated 2006): Vienna, Linz, Klagenfurt, Salzburg, Graz, Innsbruck. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: Federal Ministry of Social Affairs, Health, Care and Consumer Protection (BMSGPK)
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.
Young animals: this country does NOT accept unvaccinated/insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under ~15 weeks) from other EU states; never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: Australia
countries.summary: Group 1 (New Zealand, Norfolk Island, Cocos (Keeling) Islands): no quarantine. Group 2 (rabies-free) and Group 3 (approved, rabies absent or well controlled) countries need a DAFF import permit (BICON) and Post Entry Quarantine at Mickleham, arriving into Melbourne. Pets from non-approved countries must first live in an approved country.
countries.microchip: Microchip required; identity is tied to the RNAT. For Group 3, a competent-authority (official government vet) identity check before the RNAT blood draw cuts quarantine from 30 to 10 days.
countries.rabies_titer: Group 3: RNAT by FAVN or RFFIT, at least 0.5 IU/ml. Export only 180 days or more after the lab receives the sample. The RNAT is valid 12 months from sampling; a retest plus a permit variation avoids restarting the 180 days.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatments per the permit and step-by-step guide (timings not verified here).
countries.import_permit: Yes for Group 2 and 3, via BICON. Secondary sources say permits typically take 20-40 business days (sometimes much longer).
countries.quarantine: Group 2: at least 10 days. Group 3: at least 10 days only if the competent-authority identity check was done before the RNAT blood draw and at least 180 days before export; otherwise at least 30 days. All quarantine is at the Mickleham PEQ facility (Melbourne). Book only after the permit is issued, via the Post Entry Biosecurity System or by phone (1800 900 090). The facility accepts arrivals 05:00-14:30 Mon, Tue, Sat, Sun and 05:00-21:00 Wed-Fri.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 7-8 months for Group 3: identity check, RNAT blood draw, wait 180 days (meanwhile the permit takes 20-40+ business days), book Mickleham after the permit, pre-export tests, treatments and certificate, then fly into Melbourne. Group 2 is shorter (weeks to a few months). LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~210 days from the USA or most EU countries (Group 3): RNAT, then 180 days after the lab receives the sample, plus permit and PEQ booking. Not re-verified this pass (DAFF site unreachable).
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited dogs: Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa, Pit Bull Terrier/American Pit Bull Terrier, Perro de Presa Canario. Some cat hybrids (e.g. Savannah) are prohibited. Verify on DAFF.
countries.private_aviation: Allowed with conditions. Pets normally arrive as manifested cargo directly into Melbourne (no domestic transfers). For a private or chartered flight, DAFF must be told before departure: the permit must be varied (fees apply), and DAFF gives written approval after a document check before the flight leaves. Group 2/3 flights must land at a first point of entry airport in Victoria. The pet must be crated before the aircraft enters Australian territory and stay crated until it reaches PEQ. On mixed flights, Group 2 pets stay sealed the whole flight; Group 3 pets may be uncrated until Australian territory.
countries.export: Export certification is through DAFF (MICoR lists destination requirements; export health certificates are government-endorsed). Group 3 pets returning to Australia can use the identity check on their Australian export certification.
countries.authority: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF)
vaccinations: Rabies (Group 3): vaccination valid from the RNAT blood draw through export.
Other vaccines and tests per the import permit.
documents: DAFF import permit (BICON)
RNAT declaration and lab report (Group 3)
Competent-authority identity check (optional, enables 10-day quarantine)
Government-endorsed veterinary health certificate
Dogs (per USDA summary for US origin): tests for Leishmania infantum, Brucella canis (unless desexed), Leptospira Canicola (unless vaccinated)
PEQ booking confirmation

countries.name: Aruba
countries.summary: The Aruba Veterinary Service must approve the health certificate and documents BEFORE shipment. Pets need rabies vaccination at least 1 month before travel (if over 3 months old), an AVID/ISO chip, 6 months' residence in the US or Aruba, and a USDA-endorsed certificate issued within 14 days of arrival, with New World screwworm statements.
countries.microchip: AVID or ISO-compatible. With another chip type, the pet must travel with a scanner.
countries.import_permit: No separate permit is named, but the Veterinary Service of Aruba must approve the documents before shipment.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 5–6 weeks before travel: rabies at least 1 month before, health certificate within 14 days, APHIS endorsement, Aruba approval before departure.
countries.export: Return to the US: Aruba is on APHIS's screwworm-affected list, so dogs need a screwworm certificate from an official vet. Aruba is not on the CDC high-risk list.
countries.authority: Veterinary Service of Aruba (Departamento di Salubridad Publico)
vaccinations: Rabies: pets over 3 months, at least 1 month before travel; the certificate lists vaccine name, lot and expiry. Under 3 months: exempt (stated on the certificate).
documents: Health certificate by a USDA-accredited vet within 14 days of arrival, USDA-endorsed (digital via VEHCS), including NWS (screwworm) certification statements.
Prior approval from the Director of the Veterinary Service of Aruba (vetservice@dvg.aw, +297 585 0400).
Residence: in the US or Aruba continuously for 6 months before export (pets under 6 months: born in and always in the US), unless exempted in writing.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.microchip: Unverified (third-party sites only): ISO 11784/11785 microchip
countries.rabies_titer: Unverified: third-party sites say not required
countries.import_permit: Unverified: third-party sites say not required for personal pets
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2 months and confirm with the Azerbaijan Food Safety Agency (AFSA)
countries.private_aviation: Unverified: third-party sites say live animals enter via Heydar Aliyev International Airport (Baku)
countries.authority: Azerbaijan Food Safety Agency (AFSA)
vaccinations: Unverified (third-party sites only): rabies at least 21–30 days before arrival (sources disagree)
documents: Unverified: international health certificate from origin country's accredited vet, government-endorsed

countries.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
countries.summary: Up to 5 pets with microchip and rabies vaccination. From the EU/EFTA, an EU pet passport is enough. From other countries, an official health certificate valid 10 days is needed, and a titer test is needed if the origin country is not listed. Entry is only through designated traveller entry points.
countries.microchip: Required: transponder, or a clearly legible tattoo applied before 3 July 2011
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EFTA or listed third countries (Annex IV Part B). Required from non-listed countries: ≥0.5 IU/ml at an approved lab, sample taken ≥30 days after vaccination and ≥3 months before import/transit
countries.import_permit: Not needed for ≤5 pets; more than 5 pets requires the full import procedure (contact info@vet.gov.ba)
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month from EU/listed countries; 4+ months from non-listed countries (titer + 3-month wait). Health certificate within 10 days of arrival
countries.private_aviation: Must enter through a BiH-designated traveller entry point with veterinary checks. Confirm in advance that the arrival airport performs pet checks
countries.export: To the EU: health certificate (model KZV-EU-11a) issued via an official or authorised vet registered with the Veterinary Office of BiH. New EU certificate rules apply from 22 April 2026 (Regs (EU) 2026/131, 2026/705). Echinococcus treatment is needed if going to FI/IE/MT/NO (listed under Reg 1152/2011)
countries.authority: Office for Veterinary Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina (Kancelarija/Ured za veterinarstvo BiH)
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet at ≥12 weeks of age, not before the microchip. For EU/EFTA pets, valid from 21 days after the primary vaccination; boosters must fall within the validity period
documents: EU pet passport (EU/EFTA origin), OR
Veterinary health certificate from the official vet of the origin country (third countries), valid 10 days from issue to the entry check

countries.name: Barbados
countries.summary: Get an import permit first (valid 6 months). Pets need an ISO microchip, rabies vaccination with a 35-day wait after a primary dose, and, if in a Category 2 country within 3 months or arriving by sea, a FAVN. Dogs need heartworm and tick/tapeworm treatment. An officially endorsed certificate within 7 days of travel is required, plus 3 working days' notice. The US is Category 1.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784 / ISO 11785 Annex A microchip, implanted before or at the time of rabies vaccination.
countries.rabies_titer: Required only for pets in a Category 2 country within the 3 months before travel (Category 1 = rabies-free or low risk; the US is Category 1) and for all sea arrivals. Blood drawn at an approved lab at least 30 days after vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml. Pets must have spent 3 continuous months in Category 1 countries to use the Category 1 route.
countries.parasite_treatment: Dogs only: ticks plus tapeworm (praziquantel) within 7 days before leaving. Heartworm test (dogs over 6 months) within 30 days, ELISA antigen; Knott's test if positive or previously treated. Cats: none.
countries.import_permit: Required, obtained FIRST from Veterinary Services, Barbados. Valid 6 months from issue.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2 months before travel (US-origin): permit, microchip and rabies (35-day wait), heartworm test within 30 days, vet exam and treatments within 7 days, APHIS endorsement, 3 working days' notice. From Category 2 countries (e.g. UAE), add the FAVN step. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~21 days from the USA (Category 1) if the rabies vaccine is more than 35 days old: permit, heartworm test within 30 days, exam and dog treatments within 7 days, endorsement, 3 working days' notice. Category 2 origins (e.g. UAE) add a FAVN.
countries.private_aviation: Give at least 3 working days' notice of arrival (246-427-5492 / 427-5073, vetservices@caribsurf.com) with the owner, customs broker and flight details. Animals go directly from the aircraft to the Animal Reception Centre; cabin pets are handed to handling agents, and customs treats pets as cargo. Government hours are Mon–Fri 8:15 am–4:30 pm; arrivals outside these hours, on weekends or on holidays incur overtime inspection fees. Effect for private jets: even a cabin pet is treated as cargo and handed over for veterinary and customs clearance through a customs broker.
countries.authority: Veterinary Services Department, Ministry of Agriculture, Food, Fisheries and Water Resource Management, Barbados
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated vaccine, first dose at 3 months or older. Wait 35 days after a primary vaccination, or after revaccination following a lapse (vaccination day = day 0). Boosters on or before the expiry date.
documents: Barbados import permit (Veterinary Services, Ministry of Agriculture), valid 6 months.
Official export health certificate: exam within 7 days of travel, endorsed by an official government vet (APHIS digital endorsement via VEHCS). Valid 10 days from endorsement.
Customs broker (required); airline 'Pre-Alert' listing the animals.

countries.name: Bangladesh
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.import_permit: Unverified. Secondary sources cite a Department of Livestock Services NOC (contact dg@dls.gov.bd per Australian MICoR).
countries.quarantine: Unverified. Sources conflict (none vs 21 days home quarantine).
countries.authority: Department of Livestock Services (DLS), Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock
vaccinations: Unverified (secondary sources): rabies 30 days to 12 months before arrival
documents: Unverified: government-endorsed health certificate; NOC from the Department of Livestock Services

countries.name: Belgium
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
countries.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry.
countries.restricted_breeds: No national dog-breed import ban identified in the official sources checked; local rules on dangerous dogs may apply - verify for bull/molosser types.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Belgian points of entry are listed by FASFC (list of 7 Mar 2024; not reviewed in detail - confirm the arrival airport is on it). Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: FASFC/AFSCA (Federal Agency for the Safety of the Food Chain) and FPS Public Health
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.
Young animals: this country does NOT accept unvaccinated/insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under ~15 weeks) from other EU states; never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
countries.summary: For US-origin pets (APHIS): USDA-accredited vet issues the bilingual APHIS 'Veterinary Health Certificate for Export of Dogs and Cats to Burkina Faso' (valid 30 days) certifying health and rabies vaccination; USDA original ink endorsement required. French MFA travel advice (updated 15 Sep 2026): dogs and cats need a microchip, an individual passport and an international vaccination booklet, and there is no quarantine in Burkina Faso.
countries.microchip: Required for dogs and cats (France Diplomatie, Sep 2026). The APHIS certificate identifies the animal by microchip number and/or name.
countries.parasite_treatment: Not required on the APHIS certificate (optional section for other vaccinations/treatments/tests).
countries.import_permit: Not mentioned by APHIS. Non-official sources report a permit from the Direction des Services Vétérinaires (Ouagadougou) — confirm locally.
countries.quarantine: None ('Il n'y a pas de quarantaine au Burkina Faso' — France Diplomatie); none mentioned by APHIS.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6 weeks before travel: confirm current rabies vaccination → vet exam and certificate within 30 days of arrival → APHIS ink endorsement (allow mailing time) → travel with original.
countries.authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Ressources animales et halieutiques — Direction des Services Vétérinaires; USDA APHIS (US export)
vaccinations: Rabies: animals must be vaccinated; certificate records vaccination date, vaccine name, batch number and end of validity (no minimum wait stated on the APHIS certificate).
documents: APHIS bilingual health certificate for Burkina Faso, issued by a USDA-accredited vet (electronic signature via VEHCS accepted), valid 30 days after issuance
Clinical exam on date of issue: free of infectious/contagious disease incl. rabies; from an area not quarantined for rabies
USDA APHIS endorsement with original ink signature and embossed seal (can be returned by mail with prepaid label); original must travel with the animal
International vaccination booklet and individual pet passport (France Diplomatie)

countries.name: Bulgaria
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry.

(EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
countries.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry.
countries.restricted_breeds: No national dog-breed import ban identified in the official sources checked; local rules on dangerous dogs may apply - verify for bull/molosser types.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Airport points of entry on the published list: Sofia, Varna, Burgas, Plovdiv. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: Bulgarian Food Safety Agency (BFSA)
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.

Young animals: this country authorises non-commercial entry from other EU states of pets under 12 weeks unvaccinated, or 12-16 weeks vaccinated but before the 21-day wait ends, with owner's declaration of no contact with rabies-susceptible wild animals or accompanied by vaccinated mother. Never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: Bahrain
countries.summary: A Bahrain Veterinary Quarantine import permit (Ministry of Municipalities Affairs and Agriculture) is required. The official USDA–Bahrain certificate requires a microchip, rabies vaccination, a rabies titre of at least 0.5 IU/ml, core vaccines, and a pet aged at least 3 months.
countries.microchip: Required (the microchip number field on the certificate is mandatory).
countries.rabies_titer: Required on the US-origin certificate: serum antibody of at least 0.5 IU/ml from an accredited laboratory. Timing is not specified. Requirements for other origins were not confirmed.
countries.import_permit: Required: Bahrain Veterinary Quarantine import permit. The government e-service is 'Import Permit Live Animal (Personal)' on services.bahrain.bh. Third-party sources say it is valid 30 days, which is unverified.
countries.quarantine: Not stated officially. Some older third-party sources mention quarantine for some origins, which is unverified.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3 months before travel: microchip → rabies and core vaccines (booster schedule) → titre test → import permit → endorsed health certificate (within 30 days).
countries.private_aviation: IATA Traveldoc (customs info) notes that emotional-support, service animals and pets may be carried on board in a small bag of 6 kg or less including the animal. This appears to be a carriage rule, not a veterinary clearance rule. Third-party sources claim pets must arrive as manifested cargo, which is unverified. Confirm with the Bahrain veterinary quarantine office and the FBO.
countries.authority: Ministry of Municipalities Affairs and Agriculture – Animal Wealth / Veterinary Quarantine
vaccinations: Rabies: fully vaccinated. The animal must be at least 3 months old.
Dogs: canine distemper, hepatitis (adenovirus), parainfluenza, parvovirus, leptospirosis.
Cats: feline herpesvirus (rhinotracheitis), calicivirus, panleukopenia.
The US-origin certificate requires a first dose, a booster 2 weeks to 1 month later, and 1 month after the booster before export.
documents: Bahrain Veterinary Quarantine import permit (permit number and expiry date are recorded on the certificate)
Official health certificate endorsed by the exporting country's government (US version valid 30 days after issuance)
Vaccination and titre records

countries.name: Burundi
countries.summary: Under Burundi's 2009 animal health police law, imported dogs and cats need a health certificate from an official vet in the country of origin, plus an international rabies vaccination certificate dated more than 15 and less than 180 days before import. A mandatory veterinary inspection on arrival happens in daytime only, at designated control posts, and inspection services must be notified at least 24 hours before arrival. Animals arriving without the certificate face a 15-day quarantine at the owner's expense.
countries.import_permit: Not stated in the 2009 law. No pet import permit is mentioned. Confirm with Burundi's veterinary services whether any implementing ordinance adds one.
countries.quarantine: 15 days at the entry control post, at the owner's expense, for animals arriving without the Art. 91 health certificate (Art. 98). Compliant animals may be held at the entry post for the time needed for examination, capped at a few days (the scanned text is partly illegible; it appears to say 3 days).
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3 weeks before travel: if the last rabies vaccination is more than ~5 months old, give a booster at least 15 days before arrival → official health certificate → notify Burundi's veterinary inspection at least 24 h before arrival → daytime arrival for inspection.
countries.private_aviation: Arrival must go through an official entry control post (the list is fixed by ministerial ordinance). The mandatory veterinary inspection happens in daytime only, and inspectors need at least 24 hours' notice. Plan a daytime arrival at Bujumbura and pre-notify the veterinary services.
countries.authority: Ministry in charge of livestock — official veterinary services, Burundi
vaccinations: Rabies: mandatory. The international rabies vaccination certificate must be dated more than 15 days and less than 180 days before import (Law of Dec 2009, Art. 91). This is stricter than the usual 1–3-year validity: a pet vaccinated more than 6 months ago needs a booster at least 15 days before arrival.
documents: Health certificate from an official veterinarian of the country of origin, attesting the animals come from a region not declared infected with a transmissible disease for more than 42 days (Art. 91)
International rabies vaccination certificate dated >15 and <180 days before import (Art. 91)
Advance notice to the veterinary inspection services at least 24 hours before arrival (Art. 86)

countries.name: Benin
countries.summary: Rabies vaccination is mandatory for dogs and cats entering Benin. The vaccination record must show it was given more than one month and less than one year before entry (French Ministry of Foreign Affairs travel advice, updated 15 Sep 2026). Benin publishes no official rules on an import permit or the health certificate format: confirm with the Direction de l'Élevage.
countries.import_permit: Not confirmed by an official source. Non-official sources mention a permit from the Direction de l'Élevage, and the French MFA does not mention one.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 5–6 weeks before travel: if the rabies vaccination is over 1 year old, revaccinate at least 30 days before arrival → vet health certificate (government-endorsed) shortly before departure → confirm with the Direction de l'Élevage whether a permit is needed.
countries.authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, de l'Élevage et de la Pêche — Direction de l'Élevage
vaccinations: Rabies: mandatory; given more than 1 month and less than 1 year before entry, shown in the pet's vaccination booklet (France Diplomatie). A 3-year vaccine given more than a year ago would not meet this rule, so plan a booster at least 30 days before travel.
documents: Vaccination booklet or certificate showing rabies vaccination 1–12 months old (France Diplomatie)

For US-origin pets (APHIS): Benin is on APHIS's 'Unknown Requirements' list. APHIS advises a vet-issued health certificate (e.g. APHIS Form 7001, preferably USDA-endorsed) plus proof of current rabies vaccination.

countries.name: Saint Barthélemy
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2 months before travel: obtain written conditions from DAAF Guadeloupe (Saint-Martin/Saint-Barthélemy unit) or the Collectivité de Saint-Barthélemy.
countries.private_aviation: Most St Barths arrivals connect via SXM (Dutch Sint Maarten), so transit pets may also face Sint Maarten rules.
countries.export: Pets going from Saint-Barthélemy to France or the EU that don't meet Reg. (EU) 576/2013 require an owner's veterinary-surveillance undertaking (DAAF form).
countries.authority: DAAF Guadeloupe (covers Saint-Barthélemy) / Collectivité de Saint-Barthélemy
documents: No APHIS page or official entry conditions found. Saint-Barthélemy left the EU in 2012, and France's agriculture ministry (DAAF Guadeloupe) treats it as a third country for pets returning to France. Its own entry rules for dogs and cats couldn't be confirmed.

countries.name: Bermuda
countries.summary: An import permit (Department of Environment & Natural Resources, Veterinary Services) is needed for each animal. Pets need 2 rabies vaccinations and a licensed-vet health certificate issued within 10 days before arrival. Animals under 10 months, or with only one qualifying rabies vaccine, cannot enter.
countries.microchip: Required, readable by a standard reader (ISO, FECAVA or AVID).
countries.parasite_treatment: On the day of the examination (within 10 days of arrival), treat with an acaricide that has residual action against ticks.
countries.import_permit: Required for each dog and cat. Your vet faxes or emails the documents to Bermuda Veterinary Services (fax 441-232-0046, animals@gov.bm). Valid 10 days from the vet certificate date.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 10–12 months ahead for a young or unvaccinated pet, because 2 rabies vaccines 6–12 months apart are needed and the pet must be at least 10 months old. For a fully vaccinated pet: vet exam and tick treatment within 10 days of arrival, then the permit.
countries.restricted_breeds: Bermuda prohibits or restricts certain dog breeds. See the list on gov.bm; restricted breeds need prior permission.
countries.authority: Government of Bermuda, Department of Environment and Natural Resources – Veterinary Services
vaccinations: Rabies: first vaccine NOT before 3 months of age; second vaccine 6–12 months after the first; no significant lapses; most recent vaccine at least 30 days and no more than 12 months before arrival (per the US certificate, protocol Sep 2015).
Vaccines must have been given by, or under the supervision of, a vet. Owner- or breeder-given vaccines are not accepted.
documents: Import permit (faxed or emailed back by Veterinary Services, usually within about 1 business day). Valid only 10 days from the date of the vet certificate.
Original health certificate from a licensed vet, inspection within 10 days before arrival. NO USDA endorsement required.
Original rabies certificates.

countries.name: Brunei
countries.summary: A Brunei import permit from the Department of Agriculture and Agrifood is required before shipment, and it sets the conditions for each import. For non-rabies-free origins (CFIA guidance): ISO microchip, rabies vaccination 60 days to 1 year before departure, and a titer of at least 0.5 IU/ml at least 30 days after vaccination. Veterinary inspection on arrival. Non-compliant animals can be held in quarantine for 6 months.
countries.microchip: ISO microchip (CFIA guidance for Brunei).
countries.rabies_titer: Required for Canada origin (and expected for other non-rabies-free origins such as the USA): approved lab, at least 30 days after vaccination, at least 0.5 IU/ml, valid 1 year from sampling. Confirm against the permit.
countries.import_permit: Yes. From the Department of Agriculture and Agrifood (Veterinary Public Health and Animal Import Management Unit, upa.jpt@agriculture.gov.bn, +673 2388 048). The permit sets the exact conditions.
countries.quarantine: Veterinary inspection on arrival. Suspect animals may be quarantined at the authority's discretion. If documents or shipment rules are not met, quarantine of up to 6 months from arrival (APHA notes).
countries.timeline: An already chipped and vaccinated pet (vaccine at least 60 days old) needs about 1 month: apply for the permit → titer blood draw → result → health certificate and exam shortly before departure.
countries.private_aviation: No private-aircraft rule found. The permit requires notice of transport arrangements and ETA, and transit landings must keep animals isolated.
countries.authority: Department of Agriculture and Agrifood (DAA), Brunei
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 60 days and no more than 1 year before departure. Not needed under 3 months of age (CFIA). For UK (rabies-free) origin, rabies vaccination is optional (APHA notes, revised Dec 2023).
documents: Brunei import permit, obtained before export, with transport arrangements and ETA notified
Official export health certificate. UK version: exam no more than 48 hours before export
Rabies vaccination certificate and titer report
Carrier declaration that the animals were carried separately and, if transhipped, kept isolated (UK notes)

countries.name: Bolivia
countries.summary: Dogs and cats need an individual zoosanitary certificate from the origin country's official veterinary authority (in Spanish); SENASAG also lists a Zoosanitary Import Permit (PZI) to be obtained before shipment via VUCE, with final certification on arrival. Official guidance is dated and partly inconsistent — confirm with SENASAG.
countries.microchip: Not stated in SENASAG documents found.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasites treated within 30 days before shipment (SENASAG 2017 document).
countries.import_permit: SENASAG Permiso Zoosanitario de Importación (PZI) listed on VUCE: form SENASAG-IMP-FOR-001, letter to the SENASAG departmental head, origin certificate copy, payment proof; certification issued on arrival at destination customs. Whether it is enforced for accompanied personal pets is unclear — confirm.
countries.quarantine: SENASAG may require supervised quarantine of at least 30 days after entry if deemed necessary.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6 weeks before travel: confirm PZI need with SENASAG → vaccinations and parasite treatment → official origin certificate (and consular legalization from the US) → SENASAG inspection on arrival.
countries.private_aviation: Confirm with SENASAG that an inspector will attend the private arrival; certification is issued at destination customs.
countries.export: No reliable official SENASAG export procedure found — check with Elysium Jet operations / SENASAG.
countries.authority: SENASAG (Servicio Nacional de Sanidad Agropecuaria e Inocuidad Alimentaria)
vaccinations: Rabies: required for animals over 3 months (SENASAG third-country requirements, 2017 document).
Dogs: distemper, canine hepatitis, leptospirosis (canicola, icterohaemorrhagiae), parvovirus and coronavirus, parainfluenza.
Cats: feline panleukopenia.
The 2017 SENASAG text says vaccinations are to be given within 60 days before shipment, with product, type and date stated — interpretation unclear; confirm with SENASAG.
documents: Individual zoosanitary certificate from the origin country's official veterinary authority, in Spanish (EU pet passports accepted in place of it per SENASAG regulation)
Inspection and identification by an official vet at embarkation (no tumours, fresh wounds, ectoparasites or signs of transmissible disease)
From the US: APHIS 7001 issued no more than 3 months before arrival, APHIS-endorsed, then legalized at a Bolivian consulate (per USDA APHIS)

countries.name: Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba
countries.summary: Under the Besluit invoer kleine dieren BES (Stb. 2010, 570), dogs and cats need a valid health certificate and valid proof of rabies vaccination. Dogs and cats coming from mainland South or Central America (except Suriname) are banned, unless they belong to someone settling on the islands who has owned them for 4+ months. Bonaire's veterinary service publishes no detailed timings, so confirm them.
countries.microchip: Not in the BES decree. Bonaire tourism guidance (secondary) cites an ISO 11784/11785 microchip implanted before the rabies vaccination. Confirm with the Bonaire veterinary service.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required by the BES decree. A secondary source suggests a titer for pets from EU-unlisted countries, but this is unconfirmed.
countries.import_permit: No veterinary import permit is set by the BES decree. Secondary sources say none is needed for travellers bringing their own pet. Pets imported as tax-exempt removal goods need a customs permit from Douane Caribisch Nederland.
countries.quarantine: None if the conditions are met. If they are not, the animal is quarantined immediately and the carrier must re-ship it at the first opportunity, paying all costs. The animal may be destroyed after quarantine (art. 3). Transit without rabies proof is allowed only in quarantine, for up to 6 weeks (art. 4).
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2 weeks before travel for an already microchipped and vaccinated pet: check rabies validity, then get the health certificate and official endorsement within about 10 days of arrival (secondary-source window).
countries.private_aviation: The ban applies to dogs and cats coming from mainland South and Central America (except Suriname), which matters for jets routing through Colombia, Venezuela or Panama. If the conditions are not met, the carrier (operator) must re-ship the animal and pay quarantine costs (art. 3). Declare the pet to customs on arrival at Flamingo Airport (BON).
countries.authority: Openbaar Lichaam Bonaire veterinary department (vet.afdeling@bonairegov.com, per secondary source) and Douane Caribisch Nederland, under the Besluit invoer kleine dieren BES (Dutch Ministry of LVVN)
vaccinations: Rabies: valid proof of vaccination required for dogs and cats (Besluit invoer kleine dieren BES, art. 2(2)). If proof is missing, the authority may have the animal vaccinated at the carrier's expense (art. 6).
Secondary sources (bonaire.com, Oct 2026) cite a rabies vaccine given at 12 weeks or older and at least 21–30 days before travel. This is not in the official text.
documents: Valid health certificate (gezondheidsverklaring), required by art. 2(1). The decree sets no validity window. Secondary sources cite a certificate from the origin country's official veterinary authority within 10 days of travel, which from the US means APHIS 7001 with USDA endorsement.
Valid proof of rabies vaccination (art. 2(2)).
Per Belastingdienst Caribisch Nederland, small animals without valid papers are prohibited goods and must be declared to customs on arrival.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.summary: Dogs and cats need an original International Veterinary Certificate (CVI) on the official model of Portaria MAPA 741/2024 (Mercosur GMC Res. 20/24, mandatory since 06/09/2025) or a valid official passport, issued/endorsed by the origin country's veterinary authority; VIGIAGRO checks on arrival. No import permit for dogs and cats.
countries.microchip: Not mandatory under Mercosur rules; if electronic ID is used it must be ISO 11784/11785 and its anatomical location stated on the CVI.
countries.parasite_treatment: Broad-spectrum treatment against internal AND external parasites within 15 days before CVI issue (date, lab, brand, active ingredient recorded separately for each).
countries.import_permit: Not required for dogs and cats. Other pets (rabbits, ferrets, rodents, etc.) need MAPA import authorization from the SFA of the destination state.
countries.quarantine: None routinely. Non-compliance may lead to refusal, re-export, retention or other measures at the owner's cost. Brazil may refuse animals previously diagnosed with leishmaniasis.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks before travel: rabies (≥21 days if primary) → antiparasitic within 15 days of CVI → vet exam within 10 days of CVI → official CVI/endorsement → VIGIAGRO check on arrival.
countries.private_aviation: Present the pet and original CVI to VIGIAGRO (MAPA) at the international point of entry; confirm VIGIAGRO coverage at the arrival airport/FBO in advance.
countries.export: Leaving Brazil: VIGIAGRO (MAPA) issues the CVI per destination requirements. Request online via gov.br (Bronze/Silver/Gold account), with vaccination record and destination-specific documents; free; review about 48 h; digitally signed PDF. Brazilian pet passport exists (IN MAPA 54/2013). A Brazil-issued CVI allows re-entry to Brazil within 60 days if rabies is valid. Queries: cvi.vigiagro@agro.gov.br.
countries.authority: MAPA – Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária / VIGIAGRO
vaccinations: Rabies: all animals aged 90 days or more, with a vaccine authorized in the country of application and within its validity; primary vaccination must be at least 21 days before embarkation (animals not revaccinated before expiry count as primary).
Under 90 days: may enter unvaccinated if the CVI certifies age and no contact with urban rabies in the last 90 days.
Animals from WOAH-recognised rabies-free countries/zones are exempt if Brazil recognises the status and it is certified on the CVI.
documents: Original CVI on the Mercosur/Portaria 741 model (old-format certificates may be refused), valid 60 days from issue while rabies vaccination is valid
Clinical exam by a registered vet within 10 days before CVI issue (certified on CVI)
Or: official passport valid in the issuing country, containing all CVI data
From the US: APHIS-endorsed certificate valid 60 days from accredited vet signature, valid on arrival (per USDA APHIS)

countries.name: Bahamas
countries.summary: Get a BAHFSA veterinary import permit (e-permitting, apply at least 4 weeks ahead) and a USDA-accredited vet export health certificate issued within 10 days of export. Dogs must be 6 months or older, ISO-microchipped before rabies vaccination, and not a banned breed. From 1 Jan 2027, US certificates must be electronically endorsed by APHIS.
countries.microchip: ISO-compliant microchip required (dogs), implanted before the rabies vaccination.
countries.parasite_treatment: Within 10 days before export: external parasite treatment and a broad-spectrum internal dewormer (licensed in the US).
countries.import_permit: Required. Apply through the Bahamas Agricultural Health and Food Safety Authority (BAHFSA) e-permitting portal at least 4 weeks before travel.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 5-6 weeks before travel: check the rabies vaccine window, apply for the BAHFSA permit at least 4 weeks ahead, then do the vet exam, deworming and tick treatment within 10 days before departure, and the APHIS endorsement. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~30 days from the USA: BAHFSA permit at least 4 weeks ahead; exam and parasite treatments within 10 days. Requirements from EU origin were not verified (sources are US-based).
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited (including crosses): Pit Bull, Presa Canario, Cane Corso, American Bully, Dogo Argentino, Staffordshire Terrier.
countries.private_aviation: BAHFSA conditions for other regulated animals (Sep 2026) require 24 hours' notice of arrival to Veterinary Services and a separate inspection fee for landings after 5 pm Mon–Fri, on weekends or on public holidays. Confirm the same applies to dogs and cats when the permit is issued.
countries.authority: Bahamas Agricultural Health and Food Safety Authority (BAHFSA), Veterinary Services Unit
vaccinations: Rabies (dogs): most recent vaccine given at 12 weeks or older. 1-year vaccine: no less than 1 month and no more than 10 months before import. 3-year vaccine: no less than 1 month and no more than 34 months before import.
Dogs: distemper, parvovirus, leptospirosis, hepatitis and parainfluenza, at least 10 days before export.
documents: BAHFSA veterinary import permit.

US export health certificate for pet dogs or cats (VEHCS forms dated Sep 2026). Inspection within 10 days before export. Includes New World screwworm statements if the animal comes from an APHIS-defined NWS-infested zone.
From 1 Jan 2027: electronically signed by the accredited vet AND electronically endorsed by APHIS.

countries.name: Bhutan
countries.summary: Pet imports need a permit from the Bhutan Food and Drug Authority (BFDA) after document verification. Personal pets then do 15 days of quarantine at the owner's home under official monitoring. Detailed health requirements are not published in an official English checklist, so confirm with BFDA.
countries.microchip: Advised by BFDA officials (per BBS report); not confirmed as a written requirement.
countries.rabies_titer: BFDA officials advise lab results confirming rabies immunity (per BBS report); confirm whether mandatory.
countries.import_permit: Yes. Permit issued by BFDA after document verification.
countries.quarantine: 15 days for all imported pets (clinical observation, testing, vaccination). Personal pets are quarantined at the owner's home under official monitoring. Commercial imports pay Nu 500 per pet.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6–8 weeks before travel and contact BFDA first. Paro (PBH) is the only international airport.
countries.private_aviation: No private-aircraft-specific rule found. Paro is the only international airport. Coordinate the BFDA inspection in advance.
countries.authority: Bhutan Food and Drug Authority (BFDA, formerly BAFRA)
vaccinations: Rabies: advised by BFDA officials, with at least 3 weeks between vaccination and import (per BBS report); confirm the formal requirement with BFDA.
documents: BFDA import permit (application fee Nu 100–300)
Supporting health and vaccination documents submitted for BFDA verification

countries.name: Botswana
countries.summary: No dog or cat may enter Botswana except under an import permit from the Director of Veterinary Services (UK official guidance). Pets need rabies vaccination 30 days–12 months before export and an official health certificate (exam within 48 hours). Pets routed via South Africa also need a South African transit permit. The gov.bw service listing says the permit is free and issued in about 1 working day.
countries.microchip: Microchip number required on the US-origin certificate. The UK certificate accepts any identification including tattoo. An ISO 11784/11785 chip is recommended.
countries.import_permit: Required: 'No dog or cat may be imported into Botswana except in accordance with the terms of an import permit' (UK NFG 3893). Issued by the Director of Veterinary Services, Private Bag 0032, Gaborone. gov.bw lists the import permit service as free, processed in about 1 working day, through District Veterinary Offices (help: DVSpermits@gov.bw, +267 368 9510/9513). Shipper claims of SADC exemptions are not confirmed officially.
countries.quarantine: No routine quarantine reported. Non-compliant animals may be quarantined, re-exported or euthanised at the owner's cost.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2–3 weeks for a vaccinated pet: apply for the DVS import permit (about 1 working day per gov.bw) → South African transit permit if needed → vet exam within 48 hours (UK model) or USDA-endorsed certificate → travel.
countries.private_aviation: No private-aviation rule found. A direct private flight into Botswana avoids the South African transit permit; arrange DVS inspection at the arrival airport in advance.
countries.export: Namibia accepts Botswana-origin pets with a state-vet health certificate and rabies vaccination.
countries.authority: Ministry of Lands and Agriculture – Department of Veterinary Services (DVS), Botswana
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 30 days and at most 12 months before export (UK EHC 3893). US certificate: current at export; animals under 3 months may travel if the dam was vaccinated.
Other vaccinations: the UK OV must be satisfied that 'necessary vaccinations' were done (core vaccines advisable).
documents: Botswana veterinary import permit (DVS)
Official health certificate (UK: OV exam within 48 hours, valid 7 days; US: APHIS Botswana certificate, USDA-endorsed)
Rabies vaccination certificate
Owner declaration: not imported into the exporting country in the past 6 months (UK)
South African in-transit permit if routed via South Africa

countries.name: Belarus
