countries.summary: EAEU common rules: up to 2 personal dogs/cats with an international pet passport (rabies + core vaccines, clinical exam within 14 days), or an EAEU Form 15 certificate. For US origin, APHIS allows up to 5 pets on a Form 15 certificate issued within 5 days of travel. Flights are heavily restricted by sanctions.
countries.microchip: Not mandated by EAEU rules (strongly recommended; required in practice to match documents)
countries.rabies_titer: Not required; only an alternative to a lapsed vaccination (≥0.5 IU/ml)
countries.parasite_treatment: Not mandatory (any treatment given should be recorded)
countries.import_permit: Not needed for ≤2 personal dogs/cats (EAEU). More than 2 / unaccompanied may need a permit and quarantine. APHIS states up to 5 pets total without special permission on Form 15
countries.quarantine: None for compliant personal pets (≤2 under EAEU passport rule; ≤5 under APHIS/Form 15 guidance)
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month: rabies + core vaccines ≥20 days before travel → clinical exam/certificate within 5 days (Form 15) or 14 days (passport mark)
countries.private_aviation: Heavily restricted: EU bans Belarusian carriers and EU operators avoid Belarus airspace; US export controls restrict flights of US-origin aircraft to Belarus. Check with Elysium Jet operations
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture and Food of Belarus — Department of Veterinary and Food Supervision (EAEU rules)
vaccinations: Rabies: all dogs/cats ≥3 months, given ≥20 days before travel unless vaccinated within the last 12 months (multi-year vaccine accepted while valid, or titer ≥0.5 IU/ml)
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis (adenovirus), parvovirus, adenovirus, leptospirosis (or dihydrostreptomycin prophylaxis) — ≥20 days and ≤12 months before travel
Cats: panleukopenia — ≥20 days and ≤12 months before travel
documents: ≤2 pets: international veterinary passport with vaccinations and competent-authority mark of clinical exam within 14 days before dispatch, OR
EAEU Veterinary Certificate Form 15 (APHIS: vet exam and issue within 5 days, APHIS-endorsed); cats examined clinically for ringworm

countries.name: Belize
countries.summary: All dogs and cats need a BAHA import permit and a health certificate from a USDA-accredited vet (no APHIS endorsement). Pets under 4 months are home-quarantined until 30 days after their rabies vaccination. Notify BAHA 2 days before arrival; all pets are inspected.
countries.parasite_treatment: Strongly recommended: internal and external parasite treatment within 30 days of export.
countries.import_permit: Required for all dogs and cats. Belize Agricultural Health Authority (animalhealthbz@gmail.com, +501 824-4872/99).
countries.quarantine: Home quarantine for pets under 4 months (until 30 days after rabies vaccination).
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3–4 weeks before travel: BAHA permit, vet certificate, 2 days' notice.
countries.private_aviation: Notify BAHA of the date, time and flight at least 2 days before arrival. A BAHA official inspects every pet; the crate must be new or disinfected.
countries.export: Return to the US: Belize IS a CDC high-risk dog-rabies country. US dogs need the USDA-endorsed Certification of U.S.-issued Rabies Vaccination before leaving the US; foreign-vaccinated dogs must arrive at an airport with a CDC-registered facility. A screwworm certificate (official vet, inspection within 5 days) is also required.
countries.authority: Belize Agricultural Health Authority (BAHA)
vaccinations: Rabies: pets under 4 months are home-quarantined in Belize until 30 days after a registered vet vaccinates them. Rabies timing for older pets is set in the BAHA permit conditions.
Strongly recommended: dogs (distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis, parvovirus); cats (rhinotracheitis, calicivirus, panleukopenia).
documents: BAHA import permit (application and current requirements on the BAHA website).
Health certificate by a USDA-accredited vet. USDA APHIS endorsement NOT required.

countries.name: Canada
countries.summary: Personal pet dogs (8 months or older) and cats (3 months or older) need a valid rabies vaccination certificate in English or French from a licensed vet; there's no quarantine and no permit. Commercial dogs (resale, adoption, fostering, breeding, show, research) from CFIA's high-risk dog-rabies countries have been banned since 28 Sep 2022, until further notice.
countries.microchip: Not specifically required by CFIA for personal pets. The certificate must clearly identify the animal.
countries.rabies_titer: Optional alternative to vaccination: RNATT of at least 0.5 IU/ml (drawn at least 30 days, or 3–4 weeks for dogs, after any prior vaccination).
countries.import_permit: Not required for personal pets. Commercial dogs under 8 months need CFIA import permits and kennel-of-origin and quarantine-facility conditions. Commercial dogs from high-risk countries are prohibited (no permits issued).
countries.quarantine: None. Pet dogs from any country are not subject to post-import quarantine. An inspector may order vaccination at the owner's expense if the paperwork is deficient.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month before travel: rabies vaccine (no minimum wait is stated, but vaccine must be valid), certificate in English or French; for a titer route, add 30+ days. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~3 days for a pet already rabies-vaccinated (certificate in English/French). No permit, no titer.
countries.restricted_breeds: None federally. Provincial or municipal rules apply (e.g. Ontario's pit bull ban), so check locally.
countries.private_aviation: No CFIA rule specific to private aircraft found; pets are presented to CBSA at the arrival airport with the rabies certificate.
countries.export: Leaving Canada: the destination's certificate is issued by a licensed vet and endorsed by CFIA where the destination requires it. Dogs going to the US follow CDC low-risk rules (Canada isn't a CDC high-risk country): CDC Dog Import Form, age 6 months or older, microchip.
countries.authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA); border inspection by CBSA
vaccinations: Dogs and cats 3 months or older: valid certificate showing current rabies vaccination, issued in English or French by a licensed vet. The APHIS Canada page says the vaccination must be current within 3 years of import.
Alternatives to vaccination: proof the animal comes from a CFIA-recognized rabies-free country where it lived for the past 6 months, OR a rabies titer of at least 0.5 IU/ml.
Animals under 3 months: no rabies requirement (proof of age may be requested).

Personal dogs under 8 months travelling unaccompanied: also need a vet certificate issued within 72 hours of import (dog at least 8 weeks old, vaccinated for distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus and parainfluenza at 6 weeks or older).
documents: Rabies vaccination certificate (English or French) identifying the animal, or a rabies-free-country certificate, or a titer result.
Unaccompanied personal dogs under 8 months: vet health certificate within 72 hours of import (no APHIS endorsement needed from the US).
Assistance dogs accompanying their user: not subject to import restrictions.

countries.name: DR Congo
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.import_permit: No current pet-specific rule found. The colonial-era Decree of 28 Jul 1938 on domestic animal health police (still listed in FAOLEX for DR Congo) makes the import of domestic animals subject to prior authorisation by the competent territorial authority nearest the veterinary entry post (Art. 142). For dogs, that authority may require a certificate from the origin country's veterinary authority stating there has been no rabies in the area of origin for at least 30 days (Art. 139). Whether this is still applied is unverified.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2 months before travel: obtain written requirements from DRC veterinary services (Ministry of Livestock / Kinshasa) or embassy, then vaccination and certificate as instructed.
countries.authority: Ministère de la Pêche et Élevage — Direction de la production et santé animales (to be confirmed)
documents: For US-origin pets (APHIS): no DR Congo pet page; APHIS 'Unknown Requirements' guidance advises a vet-issued health certificate (e.g. APHIS Form 7001, preferably USDA-endorsed) and proof of current rabies vaccination.

countries.name: Central African Republic
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2 months before travel: obtain written requirements from CAR's ministry in charge of livestock (veterinary services) or embassy, then vaccination and certificate as instructed.
countries.authority: Ministère de l'Élevage et de la Santé Animale — veterinary services (to be confirmed)
documents: For US-origin pets (APHIS): no CAR pet page; APHIS 'Unknown Requirements' guidance advises a vet-issued health certificate (e.g. APHIS Form 7001, preferably USDA-endorsed) and proof of current rabies vaccination.

countries.name: Congo-Brazzaville
countries.summary: Dogs and cats need a recent official health/origin certificate plus a rabies vaccination certificate (Congolese Arrêté of Dec 1968: vaccination more than 1 month and less than 6 months before travel; under-3-month-olds exempt). For US-origin pets (APHIS): bilingual APHIS Congo health certificate valid 30 days, digital USDA endorsement accepted.
countries.microchip: Not required by the Congolese arrêté; APHIS certificate identifies by microchip number and/or name (vet verifies any listed microchip).
countries.import_permit: Not required for carnivores under the 1968 arrêté (permit regime applies to live animals other than carnivores); APHIS mentions none.
countries.quarantine: None for dogs/cats in the arrêté; veterinary inspection on arrival — animals showing contagious disease or lacking documents may be refused entry.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6 weeks before travel: rabies vaccination 1–6 months before arrival → vet exam and health certificate a few days before departure (US: within 30-day validity) → government endorsement → travel with originals.
countries.authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, de l'Élevage et de la Pêche — Direction des services vétérinaires
vaccinations: Rabies: per Congolese Arrêté (1968, art. 5), certificate showing vaccination given more than 1 month and less than 6 months before travel; dogs/cats under 3 months exempt from formalities. APHIS certificate records date, vaccine, batch and validity end date.
documents: Certificate of origin and health issued shortly before departure (scanned 1968 arrêté text, art. 5, refers to 3 days; OCR ambiguous — confirm)
Rabies vaccination certificate

US origin: APHIS bilingual 'Veterinary Health Certificate for Export of Dogs and Cats to the Republic of Congo' by USDA-accredited vet, valid 30 days; APHIS digital endorsement accepted — printed endorsed certificate must accompany the animal

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.summary: EU-equivalent rules: from EU, microchip + valid rabies vaccination + pet passport; from third countries, health certificate (or Swiss/EU passport if already compliant), presentation at the red customs exit, and for rabies high-risk countries a titer test, minimum age 7 months and an FSVO import authorisation for direct flights.
countries.microchip: Microchip required, implanted before rabies vaccination.
countries.rabies_titer: Required from rabies high-risk third countries: antibody titration test at an EU-designated laboratory with long waiting periods (EU standard: sample >=30 days after vaccination, travel >=3 months after sample). Animals under 7 months may not enter from high-risk countries. Not required from EU or listed/low-risk countries.
countries.import_permit: FSVO import authorisation required for direct air arrivals from rabies high-risk countries; otherwise none.
countries.quarantine: None if requirements met; pets with missing documents are refused entry.
countries.timeline: EU/low-risk origin: at least 4 weeks (microchip -> rabies vaccination at >=12 weeks -> 21 days). High-risk origin: at least 4 months and pet >=7 months old (vaccination -> titer test -> waiting period -> FSVO authorisation -> certificate). LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~10 days from the USA (not a rabies high-risk country under EU/CH listing): health certificate endorsed by the exporting authority. From EU: passport only. From high-risk countries: 4+ months and FSVO authorisation.
countries.restricted_breeds: Import of dogs with docked ears and/or tails is prohibited. Cantonal dog-breed rules exist but were not reviewed - check the destination canton.
countries.private_aviation: Direct flights from third countries (including the UK, USA and UAE): accompanied pets (cabin or excess baggage) may only land at Basel, Geneva or Zurich; unaccompanied pets (air waybill) only Geneva or Zurich. The pet must be presented at the red customs exit for a mandatory entry control. Sion, Lugano, Bern, Samedan (St. Moritz) and other regional airports are NOT listed for direct third-country arrivals with pets: clear at Geneva/Zurich/Basel first, or enter Schengen at a designated EU point of entry and then continue. From EU/Schengen states: no border veterinary check, but documents are required. Rabies high-risk countries: FSVO import authorisation needed for direct flights.
countries.export: Destination rules apply; veterinary certificates for leaving are issued by the responsible cantonal veterinary service. Ensure Swiss re-entry conditions are met before departure.
countries.authority: Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO/BLV)
vaccinations: Rabies: first dose from 12 weeks of age, valid 21 days later; must follow microchipping.
documents: From EU: Swiss or EU pet passport.
From third countries: Swiss/EU passport if already compliant, otherwise health certificate issued by exporting country's authorities.
From high-risk countries by direct flight: FSVO import authorisation (application form on blv.admin.ch).
Owner travelling separately: authorised person, owner within 5 days, written declaration in passport.
Max 5 pets per private vehicle unless for events (registered, >6 months old; third-country animals need FSVO authorisation).

countries.name: Côte d'Ivoire
countries.summary: Dogs and cats need a prior import authorization (import permit) from the Directorate of Veterinary Services (DSV) plus an official health certificate issued close to travel, with current rabies vaccination. For US-origin pets (APHIS): certificate endorsed by APHIS within 10 days of travel.
countries.microchip: For US-origin pets (APHIS): the certificate verifies microchips listed for identification; no standalone microchip mandate stated in official sources found. Recommended for identification.
countries.parasite_treatment: For US-origin pets (APHIS certificate): vet certifies animals free of mange for at least the last 6 months; no specific treatment mandated.
countries.import_permit: Required. Apply to the DSV using the bilingual DSV application form; send the completed form and a copy of the rabies certificate by email (APHIS lists carv.dsvci@gmail.com and dsv.sdsa2017@gmail.com). An endorsed health certificate is not needed for the application. The DSV form asks for a copy of the international veterinary certificate and vaccination record.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 5–6 weeks before travel: make sure the rabies vaccine is 1–12 months old (booster ≥30 days before travel if needed) → email the permit application to the DSV → health certificate and government endorsement within 10 days of travel → carry the original permit and certificate.
countries.restricted_breeds: None found. Note: pets are not allowed in national parks and reserves (France Diplomatie).
countries.authority: Direction des Services Vétérinaires (DSV), Ministère des Ressources Animales et Halieutiques, Côte d'Ivoire
vaccinations: Rabies: must be current. For US-origin pets (APHIS): if primary vaccination, or a booster given after the previous vaccine's validity expired, wait at least 21 days before import; a booster given within validity needs no wait.

Older UK guidance (APHA NFG 3927, cleared 1996) says rabies not required, but its certificate allows vaccination 30 days to 12 months before export; treat the newer APHIS rule (current rabies) as authoritative.

French MFA travel advice (Sep 2026): rabies vaccination must be at least 1 month and less than 1 year old. Apply this stricter window: a 3-year vaccine given over a year ago needs a booster at least 30 days before travel.
documents: Prior import authorization (autorisation préalable d'importation) from the DSV, Ministry of Animal and Fish Resources
Official veterinary health certificate (US: APHIS 'ivory-coast-cat-dog' form, valid 10 days, original ink USDA endorsement and embossing required)
Rabies vaccination certificate / vaccination record
Owner declaration of 6-month residency (UK-origin guidance only)
Health and identification booklet (microchip or tattoo). Per France Diplomatie, pets are admitted 'with the special permission of customs'.

countries.name: Cook Islands
countries.summary: The Ministry of Agriculture publishes dog and cat import conditions only for New Zealand and Australia. Pets need a Biosecurity permit, an official government vet certificate, and must arrive by air as manifested cargo. Dogs also need a Police permit and must be desexed. No route was found for pets from other countries.
countries.parasite_treatment: Dogs from NZ: praziquantel (5 mg/kg) and a roundworm/whipworm anthelmintic within 3 days of departure; two insecticidal washes 7 days apart, the last within 3 days of departure; free of ectoparasites (especially ticks) at the exam within 3 days of departure.
countries.import_permit: Yes: from the Director of Biosecurity, Ministry of Agriculture (biosecurity@cookislands.gov.ck, +682 28710). Dogs also need a Police permit.
countries.quarantine: The pet is inspected and treated on arrival and held in the biosecurity area until a Permit to Land is issued. No fixed quarantine period is stated.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3 months: permits (Biosecurity and Police), vaccines 1-3 months before export, treatments and government vet exam within 3 days of departure, and flight details to Biosecurity at least 1 working day before shipping.
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited dogs (Police, Dogs Registration Amendment Act 1991): Doberman, Pit Bull Terrier, Bull Dogs, Rottweiler, plus any breed the Police specify. All imported dogs must be neutered or spayed and registered with the Police.
countries.private_aviation: The conditions require import only by air as manifested cargo. No private-aircraft provision was found; confirm with Biosecurity.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture – Biosecurity Service, Cook Islands
vaccinations: Dogs from NZ: distemper, hepatitis and parvovirus 1-3 months before export (parvovirus at 17+ weeks of age).
documents: Biosecurity import permit (Application Form for Live Animal)
Exporter's statutory declaration: 6 months' residence (or since birth), at least 4 months old, disease-free for 30 days
International animal health certificate signed by a full-time government vet of the exporting country
Dogs: Police import permit

countries.name: Chile
countries.summary: Under SAG Res. 3.343/2026 (amended by Res. 5.444/2026, in force since 27 July 2026), dogs and cats need permanent ID (microchip or tattoo), rabies vaccination, internal/external deworming 5–30 days before CVI issue, and an original CVI valid 10 days (+5 max) from the origin's official authority. SAG checks on arrival.
countries.microchip: Mandatory permanent individual ID: microchip (ISO 11784/11785) or tattoo; number must match the CVI.
countries.parasite_treatment: Broad-spectrum treatment effective against internal AND external parasites between 5 and 30 days before CVI issue; CVI must state date, trade name, active ingredient and dose of each product.
countries.import_permit: Not required for dogs and cats (ferrets need a SAG wildlife import authorization).
countries.quarantine: No fixed quarantine in the resolution; if requirements are not met SAG may apply sanitary measures at any authorised entry point at the importer's cost, plus sanctions.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–5 weeks before travel: microchip → rabies (≥21 days before entry if primary) → antiparasitic 5–30 days before CVI → vet exam within 10 days of CVI → official CVI (valid 10+5 days) → SAG inspection on arrival.
countries.restricted_breeds: None for import (SENASA Argentina destination page: not contemplated).
countries.private_aviation: Pets must be presented at an authorised border control point with SAG presence; confirm SAG inspection at the arrival airport/FBO in advance. Note the very short 10-day CVI window.
countries.export: Leaving Chile: SAG issues a Certificado Zoosanitario de Exportación (CZE). Pets returning to Chile may re-enter within 60 calendar days of CZE issue with the original/official copy, if rabies is valid and the animal has permanent ISO microchip or tattoo; trips longer than 60 days require full import requirements.
countries.authority: SAG (Servicio Agrícola y Ganadero)
vaccinations: Rabies: mandatory. Primary-vaccinated animals (first dose, or last dose given after the previous one expired), regardless of age, must be vaccinated at least 21 days before entry to Chile.
Non-primary animals: CVI must certify the last 2 rabies doses (otherwise treated as primary).
Exemption: animals that lived since birth or ≥6 continuous months in a country free of dog-transmitted rabies recognised by Chile, certified by the origin authority.
documents: Original CVI from the origin country's competent veterinary authority, in Spanish plus origin language or English; valid 10 days from issue, extendable max 5 days depending on travel
Clinical exam by a vet within 10 days before CVI issue
CVI must include species, breed, sex, age, ID number, neutered status, owner details, transport mode, whether accompanied, last 2 rabies vaccinations (serial, lab, validity), antiparasitic details
From EU countries: EU pet passport (Spanish or English) accepted if it shows compliance

countries.name: Cameroon
countries.summary: Rules differ by origin. For US-origin pets (APHIS): microchipped dog/cat, current rabies vaccination, APHIS Cameroon health certificate (valid 30 days) with USDA original ink endorsement. For UK-origin pets (UK EHC 3038): rabies vaccination 30 days–12 months before export, official-vet exam within 48 h, certificate valid 10 days, import permit number if applicable.
countries.microchip: For US-origin pets (APHIS): microchip number must be listed and verified by the vet. UK certificate allows identification incl. tattoo.
countries.import_permit: UK certificate has a field 'Import permit no. (if applicable)'; APHIS does not mention a permit. Non-official sources report a MINEPIA import authorization — confirm with MINEPIA before travel.
countries.quarantine: None stated in official certificates.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6 weeks before travel: microchip + rabies vaccination (≥30 days before for UK route) → ask MINEPIA whether an import permit is needed → vet exam/certificate (US: within 30 days; UK: within 48 h, valid 10 days) → government endorsement → travel with originals.
countries.authority: Ministère de l'Élevage, des Pêches et des Industries Animales (MINEPIA)
vaccinations: Rabies (US origin, APHIS): current at time of export; certificate records date, vaccine, batch and end of validity.
Rabies (UK origin, EHC 3038): given not less than 30 days and not more than 12 months before export; copy of vaccination certificate attached.
documents: US origin: APHIS 'Veterinary Health Certificate for Export of Dogs and Cats from the USA to Cameroon' (form dated Aug 2025) by USDA-accredited vet, valid 30 days; original USDA ink-signed and embossed endorsement must accompany the animal
UK origin: Export Health Certificate 3038 signed by an Official Veterinarian, exam within 48 h of export, valid 10 days from signature

countries.name: China (Mainland)
countries.summary: One dog or cat per person per entry. To enter through any port with no quarantine, the pet needs an ISO microchip, at least two rabies vaccinations and a rabies titer of at least 0.5 IU/ml from a GACC-recognised lab (titer not needed from GACC 'designated' countries/regions such as Hawaii and Guam). Otherwise the pet must enter through a designated port with a quarantine facility and do 30 days of quarantine.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785, 15-digit, required for the quarantine-exempt route. Bring a reader for non-ISO chips.
countries.rabies_titer: Pets from non-designated countries/regions: rabies antibody result of at least 0.5 IU/ml from a GACC-recognised lab. Sample taken on or after the 2nd vaccination. Valid up to 1 year from sampling (per APHIS). Not required from GACC-designated countries/regions (e.g. Hawaii and Guam per APHIS; check the current GACC list).
countries.import_permit: No import permit for personal pets. On the quarantine route, notify Chinese Customs in advance.
countries.quarantine: None if fully compliant (on-site customs inspection only). Otherwise 30 days in a customs-designated isolation facility at a designated port, at the owner's cost. Guide, hearing and search-and-rescue dogs have their own route.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2–3 months before travel: microchip → rabies #1 → rabies #2 → titer blood draw → result → health certificate within 14 days before arrival (US) → government endorsement. Dogs must be registered with local police within about 1 month of arrival (per APHIS).
countries.private_aviation: No business-jet-specific GACC rule found. A fully compliant pet (chip, 2 vaccinations, titer) may enter through any port, including business-aviation arrivals at an open international port. A non-compliant pet must enter through a designated port with quarantine facilities. APHIS lists Beijing Capital, Shanghai Pudong, Shanghai Hongqiao, Guangzhou Baiyun, Urumqi Diwopu, plus several rail and sea ports; the full GACC list is longer. The one-pet-per-person limit still applies.
countries.export: Local customs (GACC) issues the export animal health certificate after inspection, based on the destination's requirements. Arrange with customs at the departure port in advance.
countries.authority: General Administration of Customs of the People's Republic of China (GACC)
vaccinations: Rabies: official rabies vaccination certificate, current at arrival. The quarantine-exempt route requires at least two lifetime doses (per APHIS).
documents: Official health/quarantine certificate from the exporting country's veterinary authority, one per pet, naming the traveller, who must match the passport. For US origin: issued within 14 days of arrival and USDA-endorsed.
Original rabies vaccination certificate
Rabies titer report (non-designated origins, quarantine-exempt route)
Passport copy and a printed photo of the pet (per APHIS)

countries.name: Colombia
countries.summary: Dogs and cats need an official health certificate from the origin country dated no more than 10 calendar days before entry, current vaccinations (rabies plus core vaccines) and deworming within 60 days; on arrival ICA inspects and issues the Certificado de Inspección Sanitaria (CIS). Pre-registration in ICA's SISPAP system is available to speed clearance.
countries.microchip: Not mentioned in ICA entry requirements.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external antiparasitic treatment within 60 days before the trip; product name, active ingredient and date on the certificate.
countries.import_permit: No ICA import permit for personal pet dogs and cats; ICA issues the CIS on arrival after documentary and physical inspection. Fee paid online via SISPAP (Colombian bank account) or by card at the ICA office (no cash).
countries.quarantine: Only if non-compliant: retention, home quarantine, re-shipment or euthanasia at owner's cost.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks before travel (ICA suggests starting early): vaccinations (rabies ≥21 days if first) → deworming within 60 days → official health certificate ≤10 days before entry → SISPAP Pre-CIS + payment → ICA inspection on arrival.
countries.private_aviation: ICA offices operate at international airports, border crossings and seaports; for arrivals outside ICA hours, Sundays or holidays, tick 'Servicio Especial' in the SISPAP Pre-CIS request.
countries.export: Leaving Colombia: ICA issues an export CIS only at its airport/port/border offices; the request is filed in SISPAP (by the owner or private vet) with health and vaccination certificates plus destination-specific annexes. Framework: ICA Res. 100164 of 2021. Five or more animals per user are treated as commercial.
countries.authority: ICA (Instituto Colombiano Agropecuario)
vaccinations: Rabies: vaccine name, lot, date and validity certified; primary vaccination at least 21 days before embarkation. If the origin country does not vaccinate against rabies, home quarantine and vaccination in Colombia.
Dogs: distemper, canine hepatitis, leptospirosis (canicola, icterohaemorrhagiae), parvovirus, coronavirus, parainfluenza.
Cats: panleukopenia, viral rhinotracheitis, calicivirus.
Minimum age for entry: 15 weeks.
documents: Health certificate issued or endorsed by the origin country's official veterinary authority (original seal/signature or electronic signature), dated ≤10 calendar days before entry, stating animal is free of infectious/parasitic disease and fit to travel
Current vaccination certificate
Pre-CIS request and payment receipt (if done in SISPAP); one request per species, up to 10 animals
From the US: APHIS-endorsed health certificate within 10 days of travel plus rabies certificate; no consular stamp needed (per USDA APHIS)

countries.name: Costa Rica
countries.summary: Pets need an APHIS-endorsed bilingual health certificate: exam within 2 weeks of departure, endo/ectoparasite treatment within 15 days, core vaccines, and rabies vaccination (current at entry) for animals over 3 months. An import permit is needed only for unaccompanied pets.
countries.parasite_treatment: Endo- and ectoparasite treatment within 15 days before export (product, active ingredient and lot recorded); free of ticks.
countries.import_permit: Required only for unaccompanied pets (MAG/SENASA importer process).
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3 weeks before travel: vaccines current, parasite treatment within 15 days, vet exam within 14 days, APHIS endorsement.
countries.export: Return to the US: Costa Rica is NOT on the CDC high-risk list. It is screwworm-affected, so dogs need a screwworm certificate.
countries.authority: Servicio Nacional de Salud Animal (SENASA), Ministerio de Agricultura y Ganadería
vaccinations: Rabies: dogs and cats over 3 months, vaccine valid on the day of entry.
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus and leptospirosis.
Cats: rhinotracheitis, calicivirus and panleukopenia.
documents: US health certificate for dogs and cats to Costa Rica (exam within 2 weeks of departure), endorsed by APHIS (digital via VEHCS).

countries.name: Cuba
countries.summary: Under Resolución 165/2026 (MINAG, Gaceta Oficial No. 75 Ordinaria of 9 Sep 2026, regulation of Decreto-Ley 127), animal-health inspectors may admit domestic dogs and cats that are vaccinated against rabies and other diseases in the import requirements and that carry a veterinary certificate from the origin country. Entry can be refused for zoosanitary reasons tied to the origin country. Home quarantine under supervision is permitted. Certificate timing and the list of other vaccines are not published, so confirm with CENASA.
countries.microchip: Not mentioned in Resolución 165/2026.
countries.import_permit: Not specified for accompanied pets. CENASA's director publishes a resolution, after risk analysis, listing countries and products eligible for travellers' imports (art. 17).
countries.quarantine: Arrival inspection is mandatory at ports and airports (art. 16). Dogs and cats may do home quarantine under the territorial animal-health department's supervision, if CENASA's requirements are met (arts. 13 and 43). Duration is not published. Non-compliant animals may be held, confiscated or re-shipped (art. 24).
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month before travel: get CENASA's current requirements in writing (vaccines, certificate validity), then vaccinate, then get the origin veterinary certificate. Expect inspection and home quarantine on arrival.
countries.private_aviation: Aircraft arriving from abroad may not arrive with live animals unless authorised by CENASA, nor release animals, including pets, without animal-health control (Res. 165/2026, art. 42.3). The inspector briefs the captain on arrival. Get prior CENASA clearance for a private arrival. US sanctions and travel restrictions on Cuba also apply.
countries.export: Return to the US: Cuba is a CDC high-risk dog-rabies country. US dogs need the USDA-endorsed CDC rabies certification before leaving the US, and Cuba is on APHIS's screwworm-affected list.
countries.authority: Centro Nacional de Sanidad Animal (CENASA), Ministerio de la Agricultura, Cuba
vaccinations: Rabies: required (Res. 165/2026, art. 18.1a).
Other vaccines 'established in import requirements' are not listed in the regulation. Confirm with CENASA.
documents: Veterinary certificate issued in the country of origin (art. 18.1a). Its content is harmonised between CENASA and the origin authority (art. 20).

countries.name: Cabo Verde
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.import_permit: Likely required, but not confirmed by a Cabo Verde government source. An Azores Airlines pet-transport information sheet (Nov 2021; airline source, used as a last resort) states that an Import Authorisation is required for animals entering Cabo Verde. Non-official guides attribute it to DGASP.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2 months before travel: obtain written requirements from Cabo Verde's DGASP (Direção Geral da Agricultura, Silvicultura e Pecuária) or embassy, then vaccination and certificate as instructed.
countries.authority: Direção Geral da Agricultura, Silvicultura e Pecuária (DGASP)
documents: For US-origin pets (APHIS): no Cabo Verde pet page; APHIS 'Unknown Requirements' guidance advises a vet-issued health certificate (e.g. APHIS Form 7001, preferably USDA-endorsed) and proof of current rabies vaccination.

countries.name: Curaçao
countries.summary: Pets need an official international health certificate valid no more than 2 weeks (USDA ink-endorsed), an ISO microchip, rabies vaccination at 12 weeks or older and at least 21 days before departure, ecto- and endoparasite treatment within 14 days, and must be at least 15 weeks old. Pit bull-type dogs are banned.
countries.microchip: ISO microchip; number and implant date on the certificate.
countries.parasite_treatment: Ectoparasites: treatment 14 days before departure with a product giving at least 28 days' persistent efficacy. Endoparasites: registered treatment within 14 days before departure. Record dates and products.
countries.import_permit: None listed on the APHIS page.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–5 weeks before travel: microchip, rabies (21 days), parasite treatments and certificate within 14 days, USDA ink endorsement (allow mail time).
countries.restricted_breeds: Pit bull terrier-type dogs may not be imported.
countries.authority: Ministry of Health, Environment and Nature (GMN) – Veterinary Service, Curaçao
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated vaccine at 12 weeks or older, at least 21 days before departure, within the manufacturer's 12–36-month validity.
documents: Official international health certificate by an accredited vet, endorsed by USDA with an original ink signature and embossing, valid at most 2 weeks.

countries.name: Cyprus
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
countries.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry.
countries.restricted_breeds: No national dog-breed import ban identified in the official sources checked; local rules on dangerous dogs may apply - verify for bull/molosser types. Cyprus-specific breed rules were not verified.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Points of entry (list dated Nov 2013): Larnaka and Pafos international airports, plus Limassol/Larnaka/Paphos/Latchi ports and Limassol, Larnaka and Saint Raphael marinas. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: Veterinary Services, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.
Young animals: this country does NOT accept unvaccinated/insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under ~15 weeks) from other EU states; never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: Czechia
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
countries.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry.
countries.restricted_breeds: No national dog-breed import ban identified in the official sources checked; local rules on dangerous dogs may apply - verify for bull/molosser types.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Points of entry listed by SVS (not reviewed in detail - confirm arrival airport). Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: State Veterinary Administration (SVS)
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.

Young animals: this country authorises non-commercial entry from other EU states of pets under 12 weeks unvaccinated, or 12-16 weeks vaccinated but before the 21-day wait ends, with owner's declaration of no contact with rabies-susceptible wild animals or accompanied by vaccinated mother. Never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: Germany
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry. Import ban on four bull-terrier-type breeds except for stays up to 4 weeks.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO 11784/11785-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU. Per the DGAL note (June 2026) listing the titer-exempt countries of Reg. (EU) 2026/636, the following are NOT listed, so pets coming from them need the titer + 3-month wait: Türkiye, Morocco, Israel, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Thailand, South Africa, Maldives, Bahamas (Mexico, Barbados, Cayman Islands, Malaysia and Taiwan ARE listed; Russia and Belarus were removed in 2024).
countries.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~10 days from the USA (EU-listed country; pet already chipped and rabies-vaccinated more than 21 days ago): EU animal health certificate issued and government-endorsed (USDA APHIS) within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From an unlisted country without a prior titer: ~100+ days.
countries.restricted_breeds: Federal import ban (Dog Transfer and Import Restrictions Act) on Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, Bull Terrier and their crosses. Exceptions: visitors staying no longer than 4 weeks; dogs returning to the Land where owner is authorised to keep them; service/guide/rescue dogs (with documents). Länder may restrict further breeds.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, NO, SM, VA) may only use authorised entry points, where customs or the veterinary service read the microchip and check documents (BMLEH). The current BMLEH entry-point list could not be retrieved; older versions list the main international airports by Land (e.g. Stuttgart, Nuremberg). Unverified whether business-aviation-only fields are included: confirm with the airport customs office before routing. EU pet rules do not require cargo carriage. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no border check.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: Federal Ministry of Agriculture (BMLEH) / Länder veterinary authorities; German Customs (Zoll)
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 (Annex IV) model remain acceptable until 31 Mar 2027 if issued before 1 Oct 2026 (DGAL note, June 2026).
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.
Young animals: this country does NOT accept unvaccinated/insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under ~15 weeks) from other EU states; never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: Denmark
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry. Denmark bans 13 dog breeds (and crosses), including for visitors.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
countries.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry.
countries.restricted_breeds: 13 prohibited breeds and their crosses: Pit Bull Terrier, Tosa Inu, American Staffordshire Terrier, Fila Brasileiro, Dogo Argentino, American Bulldog, Boerboel, Kangal, Central Asian Ovcharka, Caucasian Ovcharka, South Russian Ovcharka, Tornjak, Sarplaninac. Ban applies to tourists too (unless documented as acquired before the 2010 Act). Transit allowed if the dog stays in the vehicle with no unnecessary stops.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Only three points of entry for pets arriving directly from non-EU countries: Copenhagen Airport (Kastrup), Billund Airport, Aalborg Airport; entry through any other airport/port is not permitted. Pets from AD, FO, GI, IS, LI, MC, NO, SM, CH, VA may enter anywhere. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.

countries.name: Dominica
countries.summary: An import permit from the Veterinary Services (Livestock Development & Veterinary Unit) is required. To get it, a dog or cat needs rabies vaccination 30 days to 1 year before export, a FAVN/RNATT titer of at least 0.5 IU/ml drawn at least 1 month after vaccination (lab results sent direct to Veterinary Services), heartworm test and treatment, parasite freedom, DHLPP+C records and a vet health certificate. Official guidance dates from 2011, and the 1955 regulations limit dog and cat origins, so confirm before booking.
countries.microchip: Not mentioned in official guidance.
countries.rabies_titer: RNATT/FAVN at a reputable rabies reference laboratory, at least 0.5 IU/ml, sampled at least 1 month after vaccination. The lab sends results directly to Veterinary Services before the permit is issued. Results take 3–4 weeks or longer.
countries.parasite_treatment: The animal must be free of internal and external parasites, and tested and treated for heartworm, with heartworm-free certification for export.
countries.import_permit: Required for every animal (reg. 4), from the Chief Technical Officer / Veterinary Unit, Botanic Gardens, Roseau. 2011 contacts: tel. (767) 266-3827/3824; agrivet4@hotmail.com / forestvet@gmail.com. Processing and other fees may apply. Note: reg. 10(1) (as amended 1990) allows dogs and cats only directly from Great Britain, Northern Ireland, Ireland and Commonwealth Caribbean territories. The 2011 guidance covers 'all countries', so confirm in writing how US/EU-origin pets are permitted.
countries.quarantine: The inspector may order quarantine in an approved depot at the consignee's cost and risk (regs. 7–8). The 2011 guidance says the Quarantine Inspector examines the pet on arrival and may accept or reject it.
countries.timeline: For a vaccinated pet, plan at least 5–6 weeks before travel: FAVN blood draw (at least 1 month after vaccination) with a 3–4 week result, then heartworm test, parasite treatment, permit, health certificate and endorsement.
countries.private_aviation: Animals may be landed only at Roseau or Portsmouth ports or an official airport, unless the Chief Technical Officer gives a written permit for another place. No animal may be landed without the inspector's prior written permission (regs. 5–6). Coordinate the inspector for Douglas-Charles (DOM) or Canefield (DCF).
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Blue and Green Economy: Division of Agriculture, Livestock Development & Veterinary Unit (Chief Technical Officer / Veterinary Services)
vaccinations: Rabies: approved vaccine given by an official veterinarian, at least 30 days and not more than 1 year before export, recording type, serial number, expiry and date.
Current DHLPP+C immunisation record, or for other endemic diseases of importance.
documents: Import permit, sent by fax or email once the requirements are met.
Health certificate from a licensed, accredited veterinary authority in the exporting country.

Under the Animals Diseases (Importation) Control Regulations (Chap. 61:02, reg. 10, as amended 1990), the certificate must be by a government veterinary officer of the exporting country. It must state good health and that there has been no rabies among unquarantined animals in that country for the past 6 months.
Vaccination records and FAVN result.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
countries.summary: Personal dogs and cats need an APHIS-endorsed health certificate (valid 10 days) showing current rabies vaccination; a first vaccination must be at least 30 days before travel. No import permit is needed for personal pets.
countries.import_permit: Not required for personal pets. Commercial imports need a permit from the Dirección General de Ganadería.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 5 weeks before travel for an unvaccinated pet (rabies vaccine at least 30 days before departure); otherwise about 2 weeks for the vet certificate (within 10 days) and APHIS endorsement.
countries.export: Return to the US: the Dominican Republic IS a CDC high-risk dog-rabies country. US dogs need the USDA-endorsed Certification of U.S.-issued Rabies Vaccination before leaving the US; foreign-vaccinated dogs must use an airport with a CDC-registered facility. Screwworm certificate required (APHIS-affected list).
countries.authority: Dirección General de Ganadería (DIGEGA), Ministerio de Agricultura
vaccinations: Rabies: required once old enough (12 weeks). Must be current per the manufacturer's validity; a first-time vaccine must be given at least 30 days before departure. The vet may certify too-young animals as unvaccinated.
documents: US health certificate for dogs and/or cats to the Dominican Republic (bilingual), valid 10 days after issuance, endorsed by APHIS (digital via VEHCS accepted).
No consular endorsement required for personal pets.

countries.name: Algeria
countries.summary: For US origin, USDA requires a health certificate (APHIS 7001) issued and endorsed within 10 days of departure, current rabies vaccination with a copy of the certificate, and deworming. All animals undergo veterinary inspection on entry.
countries.parasite_treatment: Deworming before export (no window specified).
countries.quarantine: Veterinary inspection at entry (Traveldoc). No quarantine period stated.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month before travel: rabies vaccination current → deworming → health certificate within 10 days of departure.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries – Direction des Services Vétérinaires
vaccinations: Rabies: must be current. A copy of the rabies certificate travels with the pet.
documents: Health certificate issued and endorsed within 10 days of departure (US: APHIS 7001)
Copy of current rabies vaccination certificate

countries.name: Ecuador
countries.summary: Dogs and cats need an official zoosanitary export certificate from the origin country (in Spanish) covering vaccinations, deworming within 21 days and a clinical exam within 10 days; Agrocalidad inspects on arrival. GALÁPAGOS: entry of pets is generally prohibited by the Galápagos biosecurity agency (ABG).
countries.microchip: Identification by name, tattoo or microchip (Agrocalidad general requirements, as reported by SENASA Argentina).
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasites treated within 21 days before embarkation; date and active ingredient stated.
countries.import_permit: Agrocalidad Permiso Zoosanitario de Importación applies to pets arriving as cargo (documents emailed to the arrival airport 72 h before arrival; inspection at SENAE warehouse; fee per Agrocalidad tariff). Pets travelling with the passenger (cabin) or by land need only the origin export certificate (per Agrocalidad, as quoted) — confirm for private flights.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–5 weeks before travel: vaccinations (avoid any vaccine in the final 14–21 days) → deworming within 21 days → official certificate ≤10 days before entry → email Agrocalidad airport office 72 h before arrival → inspection on arrival.
countries.private_aviation: Notify the Agrocalidad airport office ≥72 h before arrival: Quito (aeropuerto.quito@agrocalidad.gob.ec) or Guayaquil (aeropuerto.guayaquil@agrocalidad.gob.ec); permits delivered 24/7 with prior email notice. Do NOT plan pet carriage to Galápagos (pets generally prohibited by ABG).
countries.export: Leaving Ecuador: Agrocalidad issues the Certificado Zoosanitario de Exportación per destination requirements; start at least 72 h before travel with a health certificate from a registered private vet (press reports; official page not accessible).
countries.authority: Agrocalidad (Agencia de Regulación y Control Fito y Zoosanitario); Galápagos: ABG (Agencia de Regulación y Control de la Bioseguridad para Galápagos)
vaccinations: Rabies: animals over 3 months; vaccines must be current. Agrocalidad documents differ on timing (no vaccine within 21 days before embarkation in the 2021 Americas sheet vs. 14 days after application in the 2023 general sheet) — confirm.
Dogs: distemper, canine hepatitis, leptospirosis, parvovirus (per SENASA Argentina destination page citing Agrocalidad).
Cats: rhinotracheitis, panleukopenia, calicivirus.
Animals under 3 months not permitted.
documents: Official zoosanitary (export) certificate from the origin country's veterinary authority, in Spanish, issued no more than 10 calendar days before entry
Clinical exam by authorised vet within 10 days before embarkation
Vaccination and antiparasitic record; owner passport and contact details

countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry.

Per the DGAL note (June 2026) listing the titer-exempt countries of Reg. (EU) 2026/636, the following are NOT listed, so pets coming from them need the titer + 3-month wait: Türkiye, Morocco, Israel, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Thailand, South Africa, Maldives, Bahamas (Mexico, Barbados, Cayman Islands, Malaysia and Taiwan ARE listed; Russia and Belarus were removed in 2024).

LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~10 days from the USA (EU-listed country; pet already chipped and rabies-vaccinated more than 21 days ago): EU animal health certificate issued and government-endorsed (USDA APHIS) within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From an unlisted country without a prior titer: ~100+ days.
countries.restricted_breeds: Not verified in official sources this check (Spain has a 'potentially dangerous dog' licensing regime for residents; municipal rules vary).
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories) must enter through a travellers' point of entry on MAPA's list (updated 2 Jun 2026). Airports listed: Madrid-Barajas (check at the Air Cargo Centre), Barcelona-El Prat (owner collects the animal's documents at the cargo warehouse, WFS or Swissport, then goes to the Animal Health office), Palma de Mallorca (Son Sant Joan), Málaga, Valencia, Alicante, Sevilla, Girona, Reus, Jerez, Santiago de Compostela, Vitoria, Santander, Bilbao, Gran Canaria, Tenerife Norte, Tenerife Sur, Lanzarote, Fuerteventura and La Palma, plus several ports. IBIZA, MENORCA and Madrid-Torrejón are NOT on the list: a private jet arriving there from outside the EU with a pet is not compliant; route the first EU landing via a listed airport (e.g. Palma, Barcelona, Madrid). Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no border check, documents must be carried. Non-compliant animals face re-dispatch, isolation or euthanasia (measures shown per point on the list).
countries.export: To EU: EU pet passport. To non-EU: destination rules; export certificates are issued/legalised by the Government 'Áreas de Agricultura' (appointment required for legalisation).

countries.name: Ethiopia
countries.summary: Dogs and cats need an official, government-endorsed health certificate with microchip ID and current rabies vaccination; UK official guidance also requires an Ethiopian Ministry of Agriculture import permit that travels with the animal. Requirements differ by origin country.
countries.microchip: Microchip identification listed and verified on the official certificate (APHIS July 2026 certificate; UK certificates identify by microchip number).
countries.parasite_treatment: Certificates require animals clinically free of external parasites (UK) / internal and external parasites (Slovenian certificate, exam within 72 hours); Slovenian certificate also requires screwworm inspection within 5 days before shipment.
countries.import_permit: Required per UK official guidance (dogs: Veterinary Public Health, Inspection and Quarantine Team; cats: Ministry of Agriculture, Animal & Plant Health Regulatory Directorate, Addis Ababa). Not mentioned on the APHIS page; confirm with the Ministry.
