countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
countries.parasite_treatment: Dogs only: treatment against Echinococcus multilocularis with praziquantel (or proven equivalent) given by a vet 24-120 hours before scheduled entry and recorded in the passport/certificate. Not required for dogs moving directly from IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland. Cats: none.
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> tapeworm treatment for dogs 24-120 h before arrival -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry.
countries.restricted_breeds: No national dog-breed import ban identified in the official sources checked; local rules on dangerous dogs may apply - verify for bull/molosser types.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Helsinki(-Vantaa) is the only airport point of entry on the published list (other points are road/rail crossings and ports). Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: Finnish Food Authority (Ruokavirasto)
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.

Young animals: this country authorises non-commercial entry from other EU states of pets under 12 weeks unvaccinated, or 12-16 weeks vaccinated but before the 21-day wait ends, with owner's declaration of no contact with rabies-susceptible wild animals or accompanied by vaccinated mother. Never allowed from third countries. (Finland: non-commercial yes, commercial no.)

countries.name: Fiji
countries.summary: A Biosecurity Authority of Fiji (BAF) import permit is required; the conditions in it depend on the origin country. Pets must go straight from arrival into mandatory Post Entry Quarantine (PEQ) at Koronivia, which must be booked at least 1 month ahead.
countries.microchip: Required: readable by AVID, TROVAN, DESTRON or an ISO-compatible reader.
countries.rabies_titer: Set by the permit according to origin; not stated on the BAF page.
countries.parasite_treatment: Treatments and their intervals are specified in the permit.
countries.import_permit: Yes. Apply to BAF (animalimports@baf.com.fj) and pay the fee on lodgement. Processing takes about 5 working days and the permit is valid 6 months.
countries.quarantine: Mandatory PEQ at Koronivia, Nausori. The minimum period is set by BAF/permit (not stated on the page). Book at least 1 month before arrival. Guide and service dogs may be exempt case by case.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2-3 months (longer if origin requires rabies serology): apply for the permit, book PEQ 1+ month ahead, complete tests and treatments per the permit, notify BAF Nadi and the Chief Veterinary Officer before arrival.
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa, Pit Bull Terriers (including American Pit Bull Terrier and crosses); serval cats and serval hybrids within 5 generations. Pets under 4 months and females more than 21 days pregnant are not allowed.
countries.private_aviation: BAF requires the most direct route, intact crate seals, and confirmation that the aircraft carries no animals from other countries. Notify BAF Nadi Airport (+679 6720053) and the CVO (+679 3312512) in advance. No explicit private-jet rule was found; confirm with BAF.
countries.authority: Biosecurity Authority of Fiji (BAF)
vaccinations: As specified in the permit, by origin country.
documents: Original BAF import permit (valid 6 months)
Home-country health certificate
Veterinary certificates with all lab results
Vaccination records
Microchip proof

countries.name: Falkland Islands
countries.summary: Live animals, including pets, may only enter under an import licence issued by the Falkland Islands Veterinary Service and with veterinary health certification; all live animals undergo quarantine after arrival. Detailed pet conditions are not published — contact the Veterinary Service well in advance.
countries.parasite_treatment: Not published for imports. Note: all dogs on the Islands are dosed with praziquantel every five weeks under the hydatid control programme.
countries.import_permit: Required: import licence from the Veterinary Service (tel. +500 27366).
countries.quarantine: All live animals undergo a period of quarantine after arrival; duration not published.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3 months before travel: contact Veterinary Service → obtain import licence and its specific conditions → health certification in origin country → quarantine on arrival.
countries.private_aviation: Confirm with the Department of Agriculture how quarantine/inspection is handled for private arrivals before booking.
countries.export: Contact the Department of Agriculture Veterinary Service; no published pet export procedure found.
countries.authority: Falkland Islands Government – Department of Agriculture, Veterinary Service / Biosecurity
documents: Import licence from the Veterinary Service (Department of Agriculture)
Veterinary health certification from the exporting country as specified in the licence

countries.name: Micronesia (Federated States of)
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.authority: FSM Department of Resources and Development (quarantine) and state agriculture offices

countries.name: Faroe Islands
countries.summary: Visitors cannot bring dogs or cats: under Faroese Executive Order 82/2021 §6, only people with permanent residence in the Faroes or people moving there may import dogs and cats. Pets may not transit the Faroes, and pets carried on an aircraft or ship from abroad may not be landed (except in approved units of authorised carriers). Residents and movers need an HFS import permit (apply at least 6 business days before departure), microchip, full vaccinations at least 4 weeks old, parasite treatments and a health certificate no older than 2 days. A rabies titer and a 12-week wait apply from group B countries. From other countries (e.g. USA), the Chief Veterinary Officer sets conditions case by case.
countries.microchip: Required: ISO 11784 microchip (HDX or FDX-B, readable with ISO 11785). The number must appear on the permit application, the permit and the health certificate.
countries.rabies_titer: Group A countries (Denmark excl. Greenland, Finland, Ireland, Iceland, Norway excl. Svalbard, UK, Sweden): not required. Group B countries (most other EU states, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Greenland, Svalbard): required, ≥0.5 IU/ml at an EU-approved lab, sample at least 4 weeks after rabies vaccination; entry no earlier than 12 weeks after the sample. Other countries (e.g. USA): conditions set case by case by the Chief Veterinary Officer (§11).
countries.parasite_treatment: Required, within the product's validity when travel begins. Dogs: roundworm, French heartworm (Angiostrongylus vasorum), tapeworm incl. Echinococcus granulosus and E. multilocularis, scabies, lice, fleas, Ixodes ricinus ticks. Cats: same list except French heartworm. Must be certified in the health certificate.
countries.import_permit: Required for every dog/cat, issued by the Faroese Food and Veterinary Authority (HFS). Only for permanent residents or people moving to the Faroes. Apply at least 6 business days before departure. Carriers must refuse to transport a pet without a valid permit.
countries.quarantine: None for compliant pets. Non-compliant pets may be quarantined under HFS supervision, returned to the country of dispatch or euthanised at the owner's expense.
countries.timeline: Visitors: not possible. Residents/movers from group A: apply ≥6 business days before departure → health certificate ≤2 days before departure, sent to HFS 2 business days ahead. Because of this, departures to the Faroes are only possible on Wednesday–Saturday (HFS publishes special dates around holidays). From group B: add a titer test and 12 weeks from the blood sample. From other countries: case-by-case conditions.
countries.restricted_breeds: Dog breeds deemed dangerous are prohibited (list on hfs.fo). Hybrids are prohibited regardless of percentage, e.g. wolfdogs, Bengal and Savannah cats.
countries.private_aviation: Executive Order 82/2021 §6(3): dogs and cats taken on board aircraft or ships abroad may not be landed in the Faroes, and the crew must ensure they stay on board. This does not apply to approved transport units of an authorised carrier. §45: carriers transporting dogs/cats to the Faroes must hold an animal-transport authorisation, carry the valid permit and have a reception facility. §6(2): the owner or a designated escort must accompany the animal. Transit with a pet through the Faroes is prohibited.
countries.export: Faroese residents travelling abroad and returning need an HFS travel permit (ferðaloyvi), with separate forms for group A and group B countries. EU lists the Faroes as an Annex I territory for entry into the EU.
countries.authority: Heilsufrøðiliga Starvsstovan (HFS, Faroese Food and Veterinary Authority), Smyrilsvegur 7, FO-100 Tórshavn, +298 55 64 00, hfs@hfs.fo
vaccinations: Dogs: rabies, canine distemper, infectious canine hepatitis, parvovirus, parainfluenza, leptospirosis
Cats: rabies, feline panleukopenia, feline viral rhinotracheitis, feline calicivirus, feline leukaemia virus (FeLV)

All vaccinations at least 4 weeks old on arrival and within the manufacturer's validity. On-time boosters need no waiting period. Puppies/kittens must be at least 12 weeks old when vaccinated and arrive no earlier than 4 weeks after the last required vaccination.
documents: HFS import permit application on the official form (a copy of the pet passport is not enough), with receipt for the fee (minimum DKK 750)
Veterinary health certificate on the HFS form (clinical exam and parasite treatments). It must reach HFS (hfs@hfs.fo) 2 business days before departure and be no more than 2 days old at departure
Import permit signed by an HFS official veterinarian, carried with the animal and shown to customs on arrival

countries.name: France
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131, documents Reg. 2026/705, listed countries Reg. 2026/636): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test with 3-month wait if the country is unlisted), presented to French Customs on arrival. Category 1 attack dogs are banned outright, even in transit. Imported dogs must have at least one adult tooth.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO 11784/11785-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU. Per the DGAL note (June 2026) listing the titer-exempt countries of Reg. (EU) 2026/636, the following are NOT listed, so pets coming from them need the titer + 3-month wait: Türkiye, Morocco, Israel, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Thailand, South Africa, Maldives, Bahamas (Mexico, Barbados, Cayman Islands, Malaysia and Taiwan ARE listed; Russia and Belarus were removed in 2024).
countries.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~10 days from the USA (EU-listed country; pet already chipped and rabies-vaccinated more than 21 days ago): EU animal health certificate issued and government-endorsed (USDA APHIS) within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From an unlisted country without a prior titer: ~100+ days.
countries.restricted_breeds: Category 1 (attack dogs, import banned, including in transit): dogs of Staffordshire Terrier / American Staffordshire Terrier ('pit-bull'), Mastiff ('boerbull') or Tosa type WITHOUT registration in a recognised pedigree book. Category 2 (import allowed with proof of pedigree registration; leash, muzzle and owner obligations apply): pedigree Staffordshire Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier and Tosa, and ALL Rottweilers or Rottweiler-type dogs with or without pedigree. Bengal and Savannah cats without proof of breed (pedigree/birth certificate) are treated as hybrids and need a prior import permit from the regional DREAL. Wolf-dog hybrids likewise. Any dog imported from a third country must have at least one adult tooth (Code rural L236-1), which in practice excludes very young puppies.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories such as CH, MC, AD, GI, IS, LI, SM, VA, FO, GL and Northern Ireland) must present the pet to French Customs (red channel/'filtre') for documentary and identity checks before leaving the international zone; no appointment is needed. Le Bourget (LFPB) and Nice (LFMN): France has no published airport-by-airport list in the official sources retrieved. The DGAL note (June 2026) states customs carry out these checks 'aux points ouverts au trafic international de voyageurs', and the Ministry of Agriculture's guidance says pets from third countries are checked by customs 'at all passenger entry points'. On that basis both LFPB and LFMN (customs-staffed international airports; Nice is also a designated live-animal border control post) can receive pets travelling with their owners, but neither is named individually in any official list found, so ask the FBO to pre-notify the customs post at the airport. A small airfield without permanent customs would not qualify. Pets more than 5 per person, or travelling more than 5 days apart from the owner, are commercial and must go through a SIVEP border control post (Le Bourget is NOT one; CDG, Nice, Lyon, Marseille, Toulouse and Deauville are). EU pet rules do not require cargo carriage; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliant animals can be re-exported, isolated at the owner's cost or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture (DGAL) and French Customs (DGDDI)
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 (Annex IV) model remain acceptable until 31 Mar 2027 if issued before 1 Oct 2026 (DGAL note, June 2026).
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.

Young animals: this country does NOT accept unvaccinated/insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under ~15 weeks) from other EU states; never allowed from third countries. (French Customs: dogs under 16 weeks are not admitted.)

countries.name: Gabon
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6–8 weeks before travel: obtain written requirements from Gabon's veterinary services via embassy; as APHIS fallback, carry a government-endorsed health certificate and proof of current rabies vaccination.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture / Livestock (veterinary services), Gabon — not confirmed

countries.name: United Kingdom (Great Britain and Northern Ireland)
countries.summary: Great Britain: microchip, rabies vaccination (21-day wait), correct document (EU pet passport, GB AHC or GB pet health certificate), tapeworm treatment for dogs, entry only via an approved route/carrier (no route needed from Ireland/within UK); unlisted countries also need a titer test and 3-month wait. Northern Ireland follows EU rules (see notes).
countries.microchip: Microchip before (or at the same time as) rabies vaccination; otherwise revaccination needed.
countries.rabies_titer: Great Britain: required only from unlisted countries (not EU and not listed): sample >=30 days after vaccination, EU-approved lab, >=0.5 IU/ml, wait 3 months from sample date; exception if vaccinated, tested and documented in the EU before going to the unlisted country. Northern Ireland: same (Category 3 = unlisted).
countries.parasite_treatment: Dogs: tapeworm (Echinococcus) treatment by a vet not less than 24 hours and not more than 5 days before arrival in GB (not needed for dogs coming directly from Ireland, Finland, Malta, Northern Ireland or Norway - per EU equivalence; confirm on gov.uk tapeworm page). Northern Ireland: dogs 24-120 h before arrival; not required from Republic of Ireland.
countries.quarantine: None if compliant. Non-compliant pets may be quarantined for up to 4 months (or refused entry if arriving by sea), at owner's expense.
countries.timeline: EU/listed origin: at least 4 weeks (microchip -> rabies at >=12 weeks -> 21 days -> document -> dog tapeworm 1-5 days before). Unlisted origin: at least 4 months (add blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then 3-month wait). Book an approved carrier/route before travel. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~10 days from the USA or EU (listed countries): GB pet health certificate (or EU pet passport / AHC), dog tapeworm 1-5 days before arrival, and an approved charter operator booked for the arrival airport.
countries.restricted_breeds: Banned types (by appearance): Pit Bull Terrier, Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, XL Bully. Cannot be brought into GB without a valid Certificate of Exemption. Northern Ireland has its own XL Bully rules.
countries.private_aviation: GREAT BRITAIN: pets normally must travel as cargo by air, EXCEPT on a chartered private plane, but only with operators on the APHA 'approved air routes - charter airlines' list for the specific arrival airport (pets carried in the cabin). Charter-listed GB airports include Biggin Hill, Farnborough, London Luton, London Stansted, London Gatwick, London Heathrow, London Oxford, Blackbushe, Birmingham, Manchester, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Bristol, Cambridge, Cardiff, Bournemouth, Southampton, Liverpool, Newcastle, Leeds Bradford, East Midlands, Lydd, Blackpool, Gloucestershire, Humberside, Sheffield, often via named pet-check providers. Northolt, Doncaster and Prestwick are NOT on the list (gov.uk list updated 9 Oct 2026). No approved route needed from Ireland or within the UK. Verify the operator/airport pairing on gov.uk before each flight. NORTHERN IRELAND: air points of entry Belfast International, Belfast City, City of Derry; for air arrivals notify DAERA at least 10 days before travel (daeratradeimports@daera-ni.gov.uk).
countries.export: Great Britain to EU (and to Northern Ireland outside NIPTS): Animal Health Certificate (AHC) issued by an Official Veterinarian, new AHC for each trip, used within 10 days of issue for EU entry; then valid 6 months for onward EU travel and re-entry to GB (if rabies vaccination stays valid). EU pet passports issued in GB cannot be used by GB residents to enter the EU. Northern Ireland residents can use EU pet passports. Max 5 pets in a private vehicle unless for events.
countries.authority: Defra / Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) - Great Britain; DAERA - Northern Ireland
vaccinations: Rabies: pet >=12 weeks; wait at least 21 full days after the first vaccination (or last dose of primary course); boosters within validity need no wait.
documents: GB from EU: EU pet passport, or GB AHC issued within previous 6 months, or GB pet health certificate (or GB pet passport issued before 1 Jan 2021).
GB from listed non-EU countries: GB pet health certificate (some listed territories, e.g. AD, IS, NO, CH, GI, also accept pet passport/AHC).
GB from unlisted countries: GB pet health certificate + rabies blood test result.
Pet travel declaration (non-commercial).
From Northern Ireland, Channel Islands, Isle of Man: no pet passport or health certificate needed for GB.
More than 5 pets (not for event), pet travelling >5 days apart from owner, or sale/rehoming: Balai commercial import rules.

NORTHERN IRELAND: from GB, UK-resident pets can use the NI Pet Travel Scheme (free NI Pet Travel Document + declaration not to travel on to EU); otherwise EU rules - EU pet passport or AHC (10 days from issue for entry); Part 2 listed countries (incl. GB not using NIPTS) and unlisted countries must enter via a Travellers' Point of Entry.

countries.name: Grenada
countries.summary: Dogs and cats from the USA need an import permit from the Veterinary Officer, presented at the port of entry. They also need rabies vaccination within 12 months before arrival and a vet health certificate issued within 2 weeks before arrival. The Veterinary Officer must be told the port of entry and arrival time. Submit the permit form by fax with the health certificate at least 2 weeks before arrival.
countries.import_permit: Required: issued by the Veterinary Officer, Veterinary Department, Ministry of Agriculture, Ministerial Complex, Botanical Gardens, Tanteen, St George's. Tel. (473) 440-2708/3386/3078; agriculture@gov.gd; fax (473) 440-4191. It must be presented at the port of entry.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3 weeks before travel: have the vet issue the health certificate (and APHIS endorsement from the US) about 14 days before arrival, then fax the permit and certificate to the Veterinary Department at least 14 days before arrival, then notify the Veterinary Officer of the port and ETA.
countries.private_aviation: The permit names the port or airport of landing and the expected arrival date. The Veterinary Officer must be notified of the port of entry and arrival time, so give the FBO airport (e.g. Maurice Bishop International, GND) and ETA.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Grenada: Veterinary Department (Veterinary Officer)
vaccinations: Rabies: within 12 months before arrival (Ministry of Agriculture instructions). Secondary sources say 2- and 3-year vaccine validity is not accepted, so the vaccine must have been given within 12 months.
documents: Import permit (Pet Permit form): applicant name and country of residence, pet's age, sex, colour and breed, Grenada port or airport of landing, and expected arrival date. Fax it to (473) 440-4191 with the health certificate for approval and signature at least 2 weeks before arrival.
Health certificate issued by a veterinarian within 2 weeks before arrival. USDA APHIS says it must be APHIS-endorsed and issued no earlier than 3 weeks before arrival.
Rabies vaccination certificate.

countries.name: Georgia
countries.summary: No import permit for up to 5 non-commercial pets. Each needs a current rabies vaccination (at least 21 days after primary) and a health certificate valid 10 days. Dogs must be treated for internal and external parasites. A titer test is needed only when transiting a country outside the Article 7 list (or the owner signs Annex 3).
countries.microchip: Identification required on the model certificate (microchip)
countries.rabies_titer: Not required when travelling directly or only via Article 7-listed countries. If transiting a non-listed country: titer ≥3 months before export and >30 days after last rabies vaccination, OR owner signs Annex No. 3
countries.parasite_treatment: Dogs: internal (anthelmintic) and external (flea/tick) treatment before travel
countries.import_permit: Not required (US-origin pets, per APHIS)
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month: rabies (21 days) → dog parasite treatments → certificate within 10 days of travel
countries.authority: National Food Agency of Georgia (Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture)
vaccinations: Rabies: current; ≥21 days after primary vaccination (else Annex No. 2 for pets <12 weeks unvaccinated, or 12–16 weeks with <21 days unless accompanied by vaccinated mother)
documents: International health certificate for pet dogs, cats and ferrets (valid 10 days from issue; US: APHIS-endorsed)
Annex No. 5 non-commercial declaration (all pets)
Annex No. 2 / No. 3 where applicable

countries.name: French Guiana
countries.summary: French Guiana is an EU outermost region (France), so EU non-commercial pet rules (Delegated Reg. (EU) 2026/131) apply to arrivals from non-EU countries: ISO microchip, rabies vaccination, EU animal health certificate and, from countries not listed in Implementing Reg. (EU) 2026/636 (e.g. Brazil, Suriname, Guyana), a rabies titer test. USDA APHIS lists simpler rules — confirm with DAAF Guyane.
countries.microchip: Required (ISO-compliant per Reg. 2026/132), implanted before rabies vaccination; tattoo accepted only if applied before 3 July 2011.
countries.rabies_titer: Required from non-listed countries (Brazil, Suriname, Guyana and most of South America except Argentina, Chile, Falklands, which are in Annex II of Reg. 2026/636; US also listed): blood drawn ≥30 days after vaccination and ≥90 days before certificate issue, ≥0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated lab.
countries.timeline: From non-listed countries plan at least 4 months: microchip → rabies → titer blood draw ≥30 days later → wait ≥90 days → EU health certificate within 10 days of arrival. From listed countries (US, AR, CL): at least 4 weeks.
countries.restricted_breeds: French national dangerous-dog rules (categories 1 and 2) apply in French territory; check before travel.
countries.private_aviation: EU rules require entry via a designated travellers' point of entry with documentary/identity checks; confirm with DAAF Guyane (SALIM) which airport applies for private arrivals.
countries.export: Leaving French Guiana: requirements depend on destination; travel to mainland EU is intra-EU (EU pet passport). Contact DAAF Guyane.
countries.authority: DAAF Guyane (French Ministry of Agriculture) under EU legislation
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 12 weeks old at vaccination; valid from 21 days after primary vaccination; boosters within validity.

USDA APHIS page (US origin) instead states: valid rabies certificate signed by a licensed vet; first vaccination or lapsed boosters more than 30 days before travel; max 3 animals per family, only one under 6 months.
documents: EU animal health certificate (Reg. 2026/705 model; certificates under old Reg. 577/2013 accepted if issued before 1 Oct 2026), endorsed by origin authority, valid 10 days to entry checks
Owner's declaration of non-commercial movement
Titer test report where required
Max 5 pets; owner must travel with pet (or within 5 days)

countries.name: Guernsey
countries.summary: From the UK, Northern Ireland or the Crown Dependencies, pets travelling with their owners need no documents or vaccinations; pets from abroad must first have legally landed in the UK/Crown Dependencies. Directly from the EU, pets need a microchip, rabies vaccination (titer only if from an unlisted country), a pet passport or health certificate and tapeworm treatment for dogs. They must also be pre-notified at least 24 h ahead and arrive on an approved route/carrier. Listed restricted dog breeds need a specific licence.
countries.microchip: Required for entry directly from the EU. From UK/Crown Dependencies, no Guernsey document check, but UK law requires dogs over 8 weeks to be microchipped and registered.
countries.rabies_titer: Only for pets coming from a country that is not 'listed' (entry directly via the EU route).
countries.parasite_treatment: Dogs entering directly from the EU: tapeworm treatment by a vet (timing not stated on gov.gg; UK-standard 24–120 h before arrival). None from UK/Crown Dependencies.
countries.import_permit: Not needed for pets with owners from the UK/Crown Dependencies. EU arrivals: written pre-notification ≥24 h. Listed restricted breeds and dog/cat hybrids: specific import licence. Commercial movements/re-homing: separate rules.
countries.quarantine: Pets that do not follow the rules may be quarantined for up to 4 months or refused entry, at the owner's expense.
countries.timeline: From UK/Crown Dependencies: no preparation. From the EU: pre-notify ≥24 h and give the dog tapeworm treatment shortly before arrival. From the USA: no direct route; the pet must first legally enter Great Britain under GB rules. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~10 days, i.e. the GB health certificate before landing in GB, then onward travel; ~2 days from the EU.
countries.restricted_breeds: Need a specific licence: Akbash Dog, American Bulldog, American Bully (incl. XL Bully), American Staffordshire Bull Terrier, Anatolian Shepherd, Bandog type, Boerboel Mastiff, Cane Corso, Caucasian Shepherd, Central Asian Shepherd, Czechoslovakian Wolfdog, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa/Tosa Inu, Kangal Shepherd, Moscow Guard Dog, Neapolitan Mastiff, Perro de Presa Canario, Perro de Presa Mallorquin, Pit Bull Terrier type, Šarplaninac, South Russian Ovcharka, Spanish Mastiff, Tornjak, Yugoslavian Shepherd Dog, Wolf hybrids F1–F4; also dog/cat hybrids.
countries.private_aviation: Pets may enter only via St Peter Port Harbour and Guernsey Airport. Pets may fly in with their owners on a private plane without approval only from the UK, Crown Dependencies, Ireland or Northern Ireland, with no foreign stop (other than Ireland/NI) en route. From elsewhere (e.g. the EU), entry must be via an approved carrier; at the airport this means handling through the Aiglle or ASG hangars (carriers can apply to the States Vets for approval). Direct arrival from outside the UK/EU is not provided for.
countries.export: Bailiwick residents can no longer use EU pet passports: an animal health certificate (AHC) is needed for each trip to the EU/Northern Ireland (valid 10 days for EU entry, 4 months onward travel in the EU, 4 months for re-entry to the Bailiwick). Dogs travelling to FI, IE, NI, NO or MT also need tapeworm treatment.
countries.authority: States of Guernsey – States Veterinary Officer (svo@gov.gg) / Office of Environmental Health and Pollution Regulation
vaccinations: From UK/Crown Dependencies: none required
Directly from the EU: valid rabies vaccination
documents: From UK/Crown Dependencies: none (minimum age 8 weeks; operators may ask for a fitness-to-travel certificate)
Directly from the EU: valid pet passport (part 1 listed country), or AHC issued in GB/Channel Islands/Isle of Man (valid up to 4 months), or GB pet health certificate
Animal Import Notification to the Office of Environmental Health and Pollution Regulation at least 24 h before arrival (not required for pets with owners from UK/NI/Crown Dependencies)

countries.name: Ghana
countries.summary: Dogs and cats may only enter with a signed Veterinary Import Permit from the Veterinary Services Department (VSD), issued after MOFA approval via ICUMS, plus an official health certificate. Dogs need negative lab tests and core vaccinations; cats need a health attestation and vaccination records.
countries.microchip: Not stated by VSD. APHIS certificate records microchip numbers if present; recommended for identification.
countries.parasite_treatment: Dogs: negative tests required before permit — Brucella canis, Trypanosoma evansi, Babesia gibsoni, Dirofilaria immitis (microfilaria/Knott), Leishmania spp.; original lab reports, valid 31 days.
countries.import_permit: Required. Apply to the Chief Veterinary Officer (P.O. Box M161, Accra); Minister of MOFA approves; approval letter submitted on ICUMS to Director of VSD; processing about 72 working hours. UK guidance asks for notice at least 4 weeks before arrival. Airlines are told pets can only be carried on a signed permit. Contact: vsd@mofa.gov.gh, Import Desk +233 242649497.
countries.quarantine: Not stated for domestic dogs/cats; inspection and possible sampling at port of entry. (30-day quarantine listed for felids/wild cats.)
countries.timeline: Plan at least 8 weeks before travel: vaccinations at least 1 month before departure → dog lab tests (reports valid 31 days) → apply to CVO/MOFA and VSD via ICUMS (≥4 weeks before arrival) → official health certificate → inspection on arrival at KIA.
countries.authority: Veterinary Services Department (VSD), Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MOFA), Ghana
vaccinations: Dogs: rabies, canine distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, Leptospira canicola and L. icterohaemorrhagiae, parainfluenza — each at least one month old and valid for 12 months before departure (VSD).
Cats: rabies, feline panleukopenia, calicivirus, rhinotracheitis (VSD).
UK-origin guidance (APHA NFG 3901, revised 12/2023) says rabies not more than 6 months before export — conflicts with VSD; follow the stricter if UK-origin.
documents: Veterinary Import Permit (VSD, via ICUMS)
MOFA ministerial approval letter
Official veterinary health certificate signed by the exporting country's official vet (US: APHIS 'ghana-dog-cat' form, valid 30 days, digital VEHCS endorsement accepted)
Original lab reports (dogs) and vaccination records; health attestation report (cats)
Proof of fee payment
UK-origin: owner declaration of residency for prior 6 months

countries.name: Gibraltar
countries.summary: Microchip, rabies vaccination at least 21 days before entry and an EU-model pet passport or equivalent certificate; from the UK a health certificate showing up-to-date vaccinations suffices; from unlisted countries a rabies titer test at an EU-approved laboratory is also required.
countries.microchip: Microchip required; vaccination must follow microchipping.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU, UK or listed countries (e.g. CH, NO, AD, AU, CA, US, JP). From other third countries: titer >=0.5 IU/ml, sample by authorised vet about 3 months before the move, tested at an EU-approved laboratory.
countries.import_permit: No licence for dogs/cats (licensing applies to non-pet animals).
countries.quarantine: Not stated on the official page.
countries.timeline: At least 4 weeks (microchip -> rabies -> 21 days); about 4 months from unlisted countries (titer test ~3 months before move).
countries.restricted_breeds: Not stated on the official page.
countries.private_aviation: Not covered by the official page; contact the Environmental Agency (admin@eag.gi, +350 20070620) before a private arrival at Gibraltar airport. Note that onward travel into Spain (EU) is an EU entry from an Annex I territory (no titer or point-of-entry requirement).
countries.export: EU lists Gibraltar in Annex I (pets enter EU without titer or point-of-entry checks). For GB, Gibraltar-origin pets may use pet passport, AHC or GB pet health certificate per gov.uk.
countries.authority: Environmental Agency Gibraltar
vaccinations: Rabies: after microchipping, completed at least 21 days before entry (even if already up to date).
documents: EU-model pet passport from an authorised vet, or equivalent certificate.
From the UK: health certificate detailing up-to-date vaccinations is accepted instead of a pet passport.

countries.name: Greenland
countries.summary: Every dog or cat needs an import permit from the Greenland Representation in Copenhagen. The permit is issued only after written approval from the municipality of residence. Rabies vaccination must be at least 30 days and at most 12 months old, and the vet health certificate no more than 14 days old. Female dogs and all cats must be sterilised/neutered. Dogs may only be imported to south-west Greenland (Kangaamiut south to Kap Farvel). They are banned north of 66°N on the west coast, including Sisimiut, Kangerlussuaq and Ilulissat up to Qaanaaq, and in all of East Greenland (sled-dog districts). Fighting/muscle dog breeds are banned.
countries.microchip: Not mentioned by the Greenland Representation's requirements (recommended, and an EU pet passport makes return to Denmark easier).
countries.rabies_titer: Not required.
countries.parasite_treatment: Cats: owner's declaration of tapeworm treatment and 14 days of isolation before departure. Dogs: none specified.
countries.import_permit: Required: issued by the Greenland Representation in Copenhagen (Strandgade 91, DK-1401 Copenhagen K, +45 3283 3800, info@ghsdk.dk), after the municipality has approved the application. Apply well before departure. Without the permit the animal can be refused at departure.
countries.quarantine: None mentioned.
countries.timeline: Get the municipality's written approval → rabies vaccination (≥30 days, ≤12 months old) → health certificate ≤14 days before travel → send everything to the Greenland Representation → permit issued. Processing times are not published, so allow several weeks.
countries.restricted_breeds: Fighting and 'muscle' dog breeds may not be imported (Info Norden). At sheep-farming sites only Border Collie, Kelpie and their crosses are allowed. No dogs at all in the sled-dog districts (north of 66°N on the west coast and all of East Greenland), except sled, police or service dogs by dispensation from the Greenland Veterinary and Food Authority.
countries.private_aviation: Dogs cannot be imported to the sled-dog districts, which include Kangerlussuaq, Ilulissat and all of East Greenland (e.g. Kulusuk/Constable Pynt). A private jet carrying a dog must therefore use an airport in south-west Greenland (Nuuk, Narsarsuaq) and the dog must remain there. The import permit must travel with the animal.
countries.export: EU lists Greenland as an Annex I territory for entry into the EU. An EU pet passport makes return to Denmark easier (Info Norden). The same permit procedure applies to re-import after a stay abroad.
countries.authority: Greenland Representation in Copenhagen (import permits); Veterinary and Food Authority of Greenland (Veterinær- og Fødevaremyndigheden i Grønland, dispensations); Greenland municipalities (permission to keep dogs/cats)
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 30 days and no more than 12 months old at the time of application/travel (an older multi-year vaccination does not qualify). Puppies/kittens under 3 months may be exempt if the mother was rabies-vaccinated before birth.
Dogs: a vaccination certificate is also required (Norden/Info Norden lists it separately; diseases not specified)
documents: Application (letter or email, no set form)
Written permission to keep a dog/cat from the municipality of residence in Greenland (each municipality has its own dog and cat bylaws)
Rabies vaccination certificate
Veterinary health certificate no older than 14 days, plus owner's declaration (Danish Veterinary and Food Administration forms)
Female dogs: proof of sterilisation (Info Norden: dispensation possible for stays under 3 months). Cats: proof of sterilisation/neutering (Info Norden)
Cats: owner's declaration on tapeworm treatment and 14-day isolation
Import permit from the Greenland Representation, which must accompany the animal during the journey

countries.name: Gambia
countries.summary: Only older UK official guidance found: obtain an import permit from the Department of Livestock Services (Abuko) and travel with an official health certificate showing microchip/tattoo ID and vaccinations including rabies. Verify current rules before booking.
countries.microchip: UK-origin dogs: identified by microchip or tattoo number plus full description (UK NFG 6544, 2006).
countries.parasite_treatment: Certificate states dog free of external parasites at exam within 72 hours of export.
countries.import_permit: Advised (UK guidance): Department of Livestock Services, Abuko, The Gambia.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6–8 weeks before travel: microchip and vaccinations → request import permit from Department of Livestock Services → vet exam within 72 h and official certificate (valid 10 days).
countries.authority: Department of Livestock Services, Abuko (Ministry of Agriculture), The Gambia
vaccinations: UK-origin dogs: rabies, distemper, leptospirosis and parvovirus per manufacturer's instructions (UK EHC 6544, 2006). No cat guidance found.
documents: Import permit from Department of Livestock Services, Abuko
Official health certificate (UK EHC 6544: exam within 72 h, valid 10 days)
Vaccination records

countries.name: Guinea
countries.summary: For US-origin pets (APHIS): a USDA-endorsed bilingual health certificate (valid 30 days) certifying a clinical exam, no rabies exposure and rabies vaccination. No official import-permit information found; rules for other origins unknown.
countries.microchip: For US-origin pets (APHIS): microchip verified if listed; not explicitly mandatory.
countries.import_permit: Not mentioned by APHIS; confirm with Guinea's Direction Nationale des Services Vétérinaires.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel: rabies vaccination → confirm with Guinea's veterinary services whether a permit is needed → health certificate and endorsement within 30 days of travel.
countries.authority: Direction Nationale des Services Vétérinaires, Ministry of Livestock (Guinea)
vaccinations: Rabies: required per APHIS certificate (date, vaccine, batch and validity recorded); no minimum interval stated.
documents: For US-origin pets: APHIS 'guinea-pet' health certificate (English/French), valid 30 days, digital VEHCS endorsement accepted
Rabies vaccination certificate

countries.name: Guadeloupe
countries.summary: A French overseas department in the EU. APHIS says pets follow the requirements for France (EU rules): ISO microchip, rabies vaccination at least 21 days before entry, and an EU animal health certificate endorsed by APHIS. A titer test is needed only from non-EU-listed countries.
countries.microchip: ISO microchip implanted and scanned before rabies vaccination. If not ISO, carry a reader.
countries.rabies_titer: Only for pets from non-EU-listed third countries: blood drawn at least 30 days after vaccination and at least 3 months before travel, result at least 0.5 IU/ml. The US and Canada are listed, so no titer is needed from them.
countries.import_permit: Not under EU non-commercial rules. DAAF may request a prior-import declaration for third-country pets, so confirm.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 5 weeks before travel from the US (microchip, rabies, 21 days, EU certificate, APHIS endorsement within 10 days). From non-listed countries, add 3+ months.
countries.restricted_breeds: French dangerous-dog law: category 1 attack-type dogs cannot be imported. Confirm with DAAF.
countries.authority: DAAF Guadeloupe (Service de l'alimentation) / French Ministry of Agriculture
vaccinations: Rabies: by an authorized vet after microchipping, primary at 12 weeks or older (French DAAF guidance), then at least 21 days before entry; boosters must not lapse.
documents: EU non-commercial health certificate (up to 5 pets; owner or authorized person within 5 days), USDA-endorsed with an original ink signature and embossing, used for entry within 10 days of endorsement. New US versions apply from 1 Oct 2026.
French DAAF guidance also cites a prior-import request form for pets from third countries, so confirm with DAAF Guadeloupe.

countries.name: Equatorial Guinea
countries.summary: Per the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs (updated 15 Sep 2026), pet owners must present the pet's international vaccination booklet from the country of origin on entry. Rabies vaccination is mandatory, with yearly boosters. Older UK guidance (1999) adds that dogs must be registered with the Veterinary Services on arrival. No official health-certificate or permit rules were found: confirm with the embassy.
countries.quarantine: None stated. UK guidance (1999): on arrival the dog must be taken to the Veterinary Services (Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Stockfarming) for official registration and identification.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel: make sure the rabies vaccination is under 12 months old (booster at least 30 days before travel is prudent) → vet exam and health certificate a few days before departure → register the pet with Veterinary Services on arrival.
countries.authority: Veterinary Services, Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Forests (Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Stockfarming per UK guidance)
vaccinations: Rabies: mandatory, with boosters every year (France Diplomatie). Treat a vaccine given more than 12 months ago as expired for Equatorial Guinea.
documents: International vaccination booklet from the country of origin, presented on entry (France Diplomatie)
Vet health certificate issued shortly before travel (recommended; UK-origin EHC 4798 from 1999 required an exam within 48 hours of export and was valid 7 days)

countries.name: Greece
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO 11784/11785-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU. Per the DGAL note (June 2026) listing the titer-exempt countries of Reg. (EU) 2026/636, the following are NOT listed, so pets coming from them need the titer + 3-month wait: Türkiye, Morocco, Israel, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Thailand, South Africa, Maldives, Bahamas (Mexico, Barbados, Cayman Islands, Malaysia and Taiwan ARE listed; Russia and Belarus were removed in 2024).
countries.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~10 days from the USA (EU-listed country; pet already chipped and rabies-vaccinated more than 21 days ago): EU animal health certificate issued and government-endorsed (USDA APHIS) within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From an unlisted country without a prior titer: ~100+ days.
countries.restricted_breeds: No national dog-breed import ban identified in the official sources checked; local rules on dangerous dogs may apply - verify for bull/molosser types.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories) must enter at a designated point. The only list published (Greek document hosted by the European Commission, dating from the 2004 regime and not updated for Reg. 2026/131) names: Athens International Airport, Thessaloniki airport and port, Piraeus port, several land borders, and island points Rhodes, Kos, Kalymnos, Mytilene, Limnos (Myrina), Chios, Samos, Syros (Ermoupolis), Argostoli (port), Heraklion, Chania and Corfu. MYKONOS, SANTORINI, Zakynthos and other popular private-jet islands are NOT listed. For a non-EU departure with a pet, clear first at Athens (or another listed airport) and continue domestically, or confirm in writing with the Ministry of Rural Development and Food before routing directly to an unlisted island. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no border check.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: Ministry of Rural Development and Food - Veterinary Directorates
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 (Annex IV) model remain acceptable until 31 Mar 2027 if issued before 1 Oct 2026 (DGAL note, June 2026).
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.
Young animals: this country does NOT accept unvaccinated/insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under ~15 weeks) from other EU states; never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.private_aviation: No airport/airstrip; access is by sea only and strictly controlled under GSGSSI biosecurity rules. Bringing pets is very unlikely to be permitted; contact GSGSSI.
countries.authority: Government of South Georgia & the South Sandwich Islands (GSGSSI)

countries.name: Guatemala
countries.summary: MAGA-VISAR requires a vet health certificate (practising vet's stamp and signature) stating the pet is healthy, free of infectious and parasitic disease signs, with current vaccinations and deworming. Pets also need a rabies vaccination record (animals under 3 months exempt) and SEPA/OIRSA inspection at the point of entry, for a fee. From the US, the bilateral USDA-endorsed dog/cat certificate may be used. Foreign-language documents must be translated into Spanish.
countries.microchip: Not required in the MAGA requirements sheet.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external deworming recorded on the health certificate. No timing window is published by MAGA.
countries.import_permit: Not listed for dogs and cats in the MAGA requirements sheet.
countries.quarantine: Not listed. Inspection by SEPA/OIRSA staff at the point of entry (air, sea or land). A 2021 AGN item cites a fee of US$14 per pet.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 week before travel for a vaccinated pet: deworm, have the vet issue the certificate, get USDA endorsement (from the US), then SEPA/OIRSA inspection on arrival.
countries.private_aviation: SEPA/OIRSA inspection applies at any point of entry, so arrange an inspector for the FBO arrival.
countries.export: If the pet leaves Guatemala more than 30 days after entry, a sanitary or international zoosanitary export certificate from MAGA is needed. Return to the US: Guatemala is a CDC high-risk dog-rabies country, and a screwworm certificate is required.
countries.authority: Ministerio de Agricultura, Ganadería y Alimentación (MAGA): VISAR, Departamento de Protección y Sanidad Pecuaria (cuarentenaanimal@maga.gob.gt; tel. 1557 ext. 7426)
vaccinations: Rabies: current, with validity shown and signed by the vet. Animals under 3 months are exempt. A 2021 government news item (AGN) cites vaccination at least 1 month and at most 1 year before travel. Confirm with MAGA.
documents: Health certificate stamped and signed by a practising veterinarian: pet details (name, age, sex, breed, colour), exam, healthy and free of infectious or parasitic disease signs, vaccinations with validity, and deworming. From the US, the bilingual 'US health certificate for dogs and cats to Guatemala', signed by an accredited vet and endorsed by USDA, may be used instead.
Rabies vaccination record.
Spanish translation of documents in other languages.

countries.name: Guam
countries.summary: This US territory runs a rabies-free regime. Every dog and cat needs a Guam Department of Agriculture entry permit before travel. The default is 120 days in an approved quarantine facility. A '5 days or less' then home-quarantine program is open to pets from the mainland US (and CNMI) that meet pre-arrival requirements: microchip, 2 lifetime rabies vaccines, a FAVN of at least 1.0 IU/ml within 12 months, other core vaccines, and a 10-day health certificate.
countries.microchip: Required, except for the full 120-day quarantine. It must be readable by an AVID universal scanner, and its number must appear on the FAVN result and health certificate.
countries.rabies_titer: FAVN drawn at least 10 days after a rabies vaccination, within 12 months of arrival, at an approved lab (e.g. KSU), with results sent directly to DOAG. The 5-day/home-quarantine program needs at least 1.0 IU/ml. 'Calculated' quarantine needs at least 0.5 IU/ml, and the pet stays quarantined until 120 days after the lab received the sample.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatment within 14 days of arrival, with products and dates on the health certificate.
countries.import_permit: Required for every animal, including service animals. Arriving without one can bring a fine of up to US$1,000 and penalties for the transporter. DOAG recommends submitting documents 2–3 months before arrival (quarantine@doag.guam.gov; tel. 671-300-7964/66).
countries.quarantine: 120 days by default. 'Calculated' quarantine runs to 120 days from FAVN lab receipt. Pets from the mainland US with a FAVN of at least 1.0 IU/ml get 5 days or less, then home quarantine. Pets are exempt from quarantine after at least 120 days' residence in the British Isles, Australia, NZ, Japan or Hawaii, arriving direct. Draft amendments (Apr 2026) are not confirmed as adopted.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2–3 months before travel: FAVN draw (if not current), then submit permit documents to DOAG 2–3 months ahead, then the quarantine reservation, then parasite treatment within 14 days and the health certificate within 10 days of arrival.
countries.restricted_breeds: Animals over 45 days pregnant are refused for quarantine, and permits are refused for pets under 5 months needing the 120-day quarantine. Ferrets and most other vertebrates are generally prohibited.
countries.private_aviation: A licensed quarantine facility collects non-exempt pets at the airport, where the quarantine vet examines them and verifies the microchip. Any flight change must be approved by DOAG and the facility. Exempt-area pets need clearance scheduled with Guam Customs & Quarantine (671-642-8071/2). Foreign-vaccinated dogs from CDC high-risk countries cannot enter the US via Guam.
countries.authority: Guam Department of Agriculture: Division of Animal Health / Animal Quarantine Program (163 Dairy Road, Mangilao), with Guam Customs and Quarantine Agency
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 2 lifetime vaccinations at least 30 days apart, using an inactivated (not modified-live) vaccine. The latest must be current at release, and must not be given after the FAVN draw.

Dogs: distemper, hepatitis/adenovirus-2, leptospirosis, parainfluenza, parvovirus, Bordetella. Cats: panleukopenia, rhinotracheitis, calicivirus. These must be given at least 10 days before departure (CQA, 2019 revision).
documents: Guam entry permit application. The fee is US$65 per pet per the DOAG brochure (2024 rev.); CQA's 2019 page says US$60. Pay by money order or cashier's cheque to 'Treasurer of Guam'.

Current and prior rabies certificates, FAVN result, health certificate from an accredited vet within 10 days of arrival (English, specific breed, microchip number), flight itinerary, and CDC Dog Import Form receipt (dogs).
Confirmed quarantine-facility reservation where applicable, including layovers over 4 hours.

countries.name: Guinea-Bissau
countries.summary: Per the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs (updated 15 Sep 2026), a pet entering Guinea-Bissau must be identified, protected against rabies, and carry an international health certificate issued one week before departure. Guinea-Bissau's own veterinary authority does not publish official rules: confirm with the embassy.
countries.microchip: Identification required (France Diplomatie). A microchip is the practical standard.
countries.import_permit: None mentioned by official sources found.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2–3 weeks before travel: check that identification and rabies vaccination are valid → international health certificate about 7 days before departure (with government endorsement if the origin country requires it).
countries.authority: Direção Geral de Pecuária / veterinary services, Ministry of Agriculture (Guinea-Bissau) — not confirmed
vaccinations: Rabies: required (animal must be 'protected against rabies'). No timing rule published.
documents: International health certificate issued about one week before departure (France Diplomatie)
Rabies vaccination certificate

countries.name: Guyana
countries.summary: An import permit must be requested from the Guyana Livestock Development Authority before importing dogs and cats, submitting health and vaccination records. Detailed sanitary conditions are not published officially — confirm with GLDA.
countries.import_permit: Required: issued by the Guyana Livestock Development Authority within about 3 working days, signed by a Senior/designated Veterinary Officer and CEO/Deputy CEO; decision considers species, origin disease status and vaccination.
countries.quarantine: Not stated officially; may depend on origin disease status — confirm.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel: apply for GLDA import permit → meet permit conditions (health certificate, vaccinations) → inspection on arrival.
countries.export: No reliable official information found — check with GLDA.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture – Guyana Livestock Development Authority (GLDA), Veterinary Services
vaccinations: Vaccination status (records) assessed for the permit; specific vaccines/timing not published officially.
documents: Import permit application form
Health and vaccination records of the animal
Health certificate as specified on the permit

countries.name: Hong Kong
countries.summary: An AFCD Special Permit is required BEFORE travel. Requirements and quarantine depend on the origin group. Group I (UK, Ireland, Australia, NZ, Fiji, Hawaii, Japan, Jersey) and Group II (39 places, incl. continental USA, Canada and much of Western Europe) are normally quarantine-exempt if compliant. Group IIIA (Chinese Mainland, Macao, Hungary, Lithuania, Malaysia, Thailand) has at least 30 days of quarantine. All others (IIIB) have at least 120 days.
countries.microchip: ISO or AVID-compatible chip, all groups. Group IIIA: implanted before rabies vaccination and titer. If the chip is unreadable, the owner must supply a reader or the pet may be returned. Dogs aged 5 months or older must get a Hong Kong dog licence on arrival (HK-compliant chip implanted and rabies vaccination if needed).
countries.rabies_titer: Group IIIA only: FAVN or RFFIT result of at least 0.5 IU/ml at an AFCD-recognised lab, sample taken 90 days to 1 year before export (at least 30 days after a primary vaccination). Not required for Groups I, II or IIIB.
countries.import_permit: Yes. AFCD Special Permit is mandatory for all dogs and cats (also for transit). Do not book transport until it is issued. Notify AFCD at the airport at least 24 hours before arrival.
countries.quarantine: Groups I and II: normally none if fully compliant. Group IIIA: at least 30 days (Chinese Mainland since 3 June 2025). Group IIIB: at least 120 days at an AFCD Animal Management Centre or a licensed quarantine centre. Any group can be extended to at least 6 months for doubtful history or non-compliance. Government quarantine space has long waiting lists, so book early.
countries.timeline: Group I/II: plan at least 6–8 weeks. Apply for the permit (≥5 working days), complete vaccines and certificates (within 14 days of export), notify AFCD ≥24 h before arrival. Group IIIA: at least 4–5 months because of the 90-day titer window plus quarantine booking. Group IIIB: book quarantine space months ahead. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~30 days from the USA (continental) or France/Germany (Group II) or the UK (Group I): permit about 5 working days, certificates within 14 days of export. UAE origin is Group IIIB: 120 days' quarantine.
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Pit Bull Terrier (incl. American Staffordshire Terrier), Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro and their crosses. Staffordshire Bull Terrier needs a statutory breed declaration. Bengal cats need proof of 5th generation or later domestic ancestry. Savannah cats are not covered by the standard permit terms. Age minimum: 60 days (Group I/IIIB), 5 months (Group II). No pets more than 4 weeks pregnant.
countries.private_aviation: AFCD permit terms (verified, Group II terms) require pets arriving by air to be MANIFESTED CARGO; excess or hand baggage is not permitted, and the Captain's Affidavit must state the animal travelled the entire journey without leaving its crate. AFCD's import guide says arrivals 'by other routes' must contact AFCD well in advance for special arrangement. Non-official sources report private-jet arrivals at the HK Business Aviation Centre can be cleared with prior AFCD arrangement. Confirm with AFCD (airport office +852 2182 1001, foii_airport@afcd.gov.hk) and the FBO before booking; notify at least 24 hours before arrival.
countries.export: Contact AFCD to arrange an export health certificate for the destination. Pets that leave Hong Kong need a new Special Permit to return and are subject to the same import rules on re-entry.
countries.authority: Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD), Import & Export Division
vaccinations: Group I: no rabies vaccine in the import terms. Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus. Cats: panleucopaenia and cat flu. Given 14 days to 1 year before export.
Group II: rabies 30 days to 1 year before export (primary dose at age 90 days or older), plus the same core vaccines 14 days to 1 year before export.
Group IIIA: inactivated or recombinant rabies vaccine 30 days to 1 year before export (primary at age 90 days or older), plus full core vaccination 14 days to 1 year before.
Group IIIB: rabies certificate optional. Full core vaccination 14 days to 1 year before export.
documents: AFCD Special Permit (form AF240 + UN110 + ID copy). Fee HK$432 for the first animal and HK$102 for each additional animal. Normally issued in 5 working days, valid 6 months for one consignment.
Animal Health Certificate (VC-DC1 / VC-DC2 / VC-DC3A or equivalent), government-signed or endorsed. Dated within 14 days of export (Group IIIA: within 7 days).
Groups I and II: residence certificate. Group I: 180 days or since birth. Group II: 180 days or since birth, and no rabies within 10 km for 180 days.
Groups I and II: Airline Certificate / Captain's Affidavit (PC101) stating the pet stayed crated with no animal contact
Vaccination certificates; rabies antibody report (IIIA)

countries.name: Honduras
countries.summary: SENASA's 2026 regulation (Acuerdo CD-SENASA-001-2026, La Gaceta No. 37,146, 20 May 2026) applies to dogs and cats travelling with their owners. They need an International Veterinary Export Certificate from the origin country's competent authority and a current vaccination record. Rabies vaccination is preferably given 30 days before shipment, and internal and external deworming preferably within 30 days. Quarantine officers inspect pets at the point of entry. An import permit is needed only for 3 or more pets.
countries.microchip: Not required. The certificate must give full identification of the pet.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external deworming, preferably within 30 days before shipment, recorded with date, expiry, product type and brand (art. 4.2.2).
countries.import_permit: Required only when 3 or more pets are imported (art. 3.15c). For 1–2 pets, no permit is needed.
countries.quarantine: None if compliant. A healthy pet arriving by air or sea without health documents may enter only after a licensed Honduran vet issues a 'Constancia de Cuarentena Fiduciaria' committing to supervise at least 10 days of quarantine and then report to SENASA (art. 3.7).
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 week before travel for an already vaccinated pet: deworm (within 30 days), get the vet exam and an official export certificate from the origin authority, then present the pet and documents at the SENASA quarantine post on arrival.
countries.private_aviation: The owner must present the pet and documents to the SENASA Agricultural Quarantine post at the customs office of entry (art. 3.1). Arrange an officer for the FBO arrival.
countries.export: To leave Honduras, report to Agricultural Quarantine with the SENASA-issued Veterinary Export Certificate (art. 3.12–3.13). Short stays of 20 days or less with vaccines still current are exempt from the export certificate (art. 3.15). Return to the US: Honduras is a CDC high-risk dog-rabies country, and a screwworm certificate is required.
countries.authority: SENASA Honduras (Servicio Nacional de Sanidad e Inocuidad Agroalimentaria): Dirección Técnica de Cuarentena Agropecuaria / Salud Animal
vaccinations: Rabies (dogs and cats over 4 months): preferably given 30 days before the shipment date (art. 4.2.3).

The vaccination record must show the application date, expiry, vaccine type, brand and duration of protection (art. 4.2.1). If 1 or 2 non-rabies vaccines are missing, the owner signs an Acta de Compromiso to have them given within 5 days (art. 3.9).
documents: Certificado Veterinario Internacional de Exportación from the exporting country's competent authority, following WOAH model content. It must state the consignor and consignee, full identification of the pet, and an exam at embarkation by a veterinarian (healthy, no tumours, wounds, disease signs or ectoparasites), with the vet's name and date (art. 4.1).
Current vaccination record (cartilla de vacunación) including deworming.
For guide or emotional-support animals: a supporting document from the prescribing medical professional (art. 3.11).
Per USDA APHIS, Honduras does not require APHIS endorsement of US health certificates.

countries.name: Croatia
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
countries.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry.
countries.restricted_breeds: No national dog-breed import ban identified in the official sources checked; local rules on dangerous dogs may apply - verify for bull/molosser types.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Points of entry listed at veterinarstvo.hr (not reviewed in detail - confirm arrival airport). Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries - Veterinary and Food Safety Directorate
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.

Young animals: this country authorises non-commercial entry from other EU states of pets under 12 weeks unvaccinated, or 12-16 weeks vaccinated but before the 21-day wait ends, with owner's declaration of no contact with rabies-susceptible wild animals or accompanied by vaccinated mother. Never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: Haiti
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2 months before travel: obtain written requirements from Haiti's Ministry of Agriculture (MARNDR) or embassy first.
countries.export: Return to the US: Haiti IS a CDC high-risk dog-rabies country (CDC notes Haiti has the Western Hemisphere's highest human rabies death rate). US-vaccinated dogs need the USDA-endorsed CDC certification BEFORE leaving the US; foreign-vaccinated dogs may arrive only at an airport with a CDC-registered facility. A screwworm certificate is also needed (APHIS-affected).
countries.authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Ressources Naturelles et du Développement Rural (MARNDR) (not verified)
documents: APHIS lists Haiti under 'Unknown Requirements'. APHIS's general advice is a vet health certificate (ideally USDA-endorsed) and proof of current rabies vaccination.
