countries.name: Indonesia
countries.summary: The USDA certificate for Indonesia requires: a pet at least 3 months old, a killed rabies vaccine, a rabies antibody (FAVN) result of 0.5 IU/ml or more, 6 months' residence in the exporting country, no rabies in the area for the last 6 months, and a vet exam within 5 days of departure. Cats (not dogs) also need a negative SARS-CoV-2 PCR result before export. Barantin's import procedure, quarantine length and authorised entry points could not be confirmed officially. Bali has historically closed entry to dogs and cats (Governor Reg. 88/2008), so do not route pets to Bali without written confirmation.
countries.microchip: Microchip number is recorded on the USDA certificate.
countries.rabies_titer: FAVN result of 0.5 IU/ml or more (USDA certificate). The official sources reviewed give no wait period or sample timing.
countries.import_permit: Barantin (Indonesian Quarantine Agency) handles pet entry through its PTK Online system. Permit details were not confirmed from official sources.
countries.quarantine: Not confirmed officially. Secondary sources cite 7-14 days at a Barantin facility.
countries.timeline: An already chipped and vaccinated pet needs at least 1 month: FAVN blood draw → result (no official wait period published) → Barantin pre-notification/permit → exam and USDA endorsement within 5 days of departure (and PCR for cats).
countries.private_aviation: Unverified secondary sources say pets must enter via designated airports such as Jakarta (CGK), not Denpasar (DPS). Bali (rabies-affected) has closed entry to dogs, cats and monkeys under Governor Regulation 88/2008 (cited in later Denpasar regulations; current status unconfirmed). Get written Barantin and Bali confirmation before routing pets to Bali.
countries.authority: Indonesian Quarantine Agency (Badan Karantina Indonesia, Barantin)
vaccinations: Rabies: killed vaccine, pet at least 3 months old (USDA certificate for Indonesia).
Cats only: negative COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2) PCR result before export (USDA Indonesia page).
documents: USDA-endorsed 'Veterinary Health Certificate for Export of Dogs and Cats from the USA to Indonesia'. It covers the microchip check, the exam (within 5 days of departure), 6 months' residence, no rabies in the area for 6 months, killed rabies vaccine, and FAVN of 0.5 IU/ml or more.
FAVN laboratory report
Cats: negative SARS-CoV-2 PCR report
Barantin import/quarantine documents (not verified)

countries.name: Ireland
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry. Dogs also need tapeworm treatment 24-120 h before entry. Non-EU arrivals (incl. from Great Britain) need advance notice and must use a TPOE (Dublin, Cork, Shannon airports).
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
countries.parasite_treatment: Dogs only: treatment against Echinococcus multilocularis with praziquantel (or proven equivalent) given by a vet 24-120 hours before scheduled entry and recorded in the passport/certificate. Not required for dogs moving directly from FI, MT, NO, Northern Ireland. Cats: none.
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> tapeworm treatment for dogs 24-120 h before arrival -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry.
countries.restricted_breeds: Restricted breeds (and crosses) under Control of Dogs Regulations must be muzzled and on a strong lead (max 2 m) held by a person over 16 in public: American Pit Bull Terrier, English Bull Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, Bull Mastiff, Dobermann, German Shepherd, Rhodesian Ridgeback, Rottweiler, Japanese Akita, Japanese Tosa, Bandog. XL Bully type: import, breeding, sale and rehoming banned since 1 Oct 2024; ownership requires a Certificate of Exemption since 1 Feb 2025.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Travellers' points of entry: Dublin Airport, Cork Airport, Shannon Airport (plus Dublin Port, Rosslare, Ringaskiddy). Advance notice via the DAFM Advance Notice Portal is required before bringing a pet from a non-EU country (including Great Britain); a compliance check is done on arrival. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost. DAFM 'may facilitate' landing of pets by private aircraft where possible: contact the chosen TPOE in advance to ask whether a private arrival can be facilitated; pets from non-EU countries must arrive at a TPOE with advance notice and undergo a compliance check. Pets not compliant must not disembark.
countries.export: To EU: EU pet passport from your vet (no tapeworm needed to leave, but dogs returning need tapeworm treatment from a vet abroad 24-120 h before re-entry). To non-EU: destination requirements; certificate endorsed by the DAFM Regional Veterinary Office - contact the RVO at least 2 months before travel. Dublin Airport (DAA) does not accept pets outbound as excess baggage since 19 July 2021.

Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.
Non-EU arrivals (incl. GB): complete DAFM Advance Notice Portal (www.pettravel.gov.ie) before travel; for assistance dogs at least 24 h before departure.
Young animals: this country does NOT accept unvaccinated/insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under ~15 weeks) from other EU states; never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: Israel
countries.summary: Up to two dogs or cats travelling with their owner on the same flight need no import permit, but must meet the health conditions: microchip, rabies vaccination, a titre of at least 0.5 IU/ml (except for pets born in listed rabies-free countries), and an Israeli-model certificate within 10 days. The Veterinary Services at the port must be notified in advance.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785 microchip (or tattoo), implanted before the rabies vaccine and blood test. If the chip is non-ISO, the owner must supply a reader.
countries.rabies_titer: Required at 0.5 IU/ml or more from a WOAH- and/or EU-approved lab. The sample must be taken at least 30 days after vaccination, or 14 days if the pet has had multiple vaccinations and more than 30 days have passed since the first. Per the 2020 USDA guidance, the result stays valid for life while rabies vaccinations remain current. Exempt: pets born in the rabies-free countries listed above.
countries.import_permit: Not required for up to 2 dogs or cats accompanying the owner on the same flight, provided the pet stays with the owner. Otherwise an import licence from the Director of Veterinary Services is required, and permit animals arrive as manifested cargo only (cargo inspections Sunday to Thursday, 06:00–24:00).
countries.quarantine: No quarantine for compliant pets.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2–3 months before travel (less for pets from rabies-free countries): microchip → rabies vaccination at 3 months or older → titre at least 30 days later → health certificate within 10 days of departure → send Annex B notification at least 2 working days before departure → arrive at an approved port. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~30 days from the USA or EU: titer on a currently vaccinated pet (no post-test wait) plus certificate within 10 days and notification 2 working days ahead. Pets born in listed rabies-free countries: ~10 days.
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited unless a case-by-case import permit is granted (vs-ie@moag.gov.il): American Staffordshire Terrier, Bull Terrier, Dogo Argentino, Japanese Tosa, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, Pit Bull Terrier, Fila Brasileiro, Rottweiler, plus crosses and look-alikes. Minimum age 4 months on arrival (3 months for pets from rabies-free countries).
countries.private_aviation: Approved ports of entry: Ben Gurion Airport, Haifa, Ashdod and Eilat seaports. Private jets should arrive at Ben Gurion (TLV). Other airports (e.g. Ramon/ETM) are not listed. A pet travelling with its owner on the same private flight fits the 'accompanied' route (2 pets or fewer, no permit). Send the pre-arrival notification to vs-airport@moag.gov.il at least 2 working days before departure. Shipments are not released until the Veterinary Services authorise them.
countries.export: Israel's Veterinary Services publish separate pet export guidance (not reviewed). Israel is on the CDC high-risk list and is not EU-listed: for return to the US or EU, prepare the US rabies certification / EU titer before leaving.
countries.authority: Israeli Veterinary Services and Animal Health (IVSAH), Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security
vaccinations: Rabies: vaccinated at 3 months or older, not more than 1 year and not less than 30 days before arrival. No 30-day wait if the pet has had more than one vaccination and is still within validity.
Pets born in rabies-free countries (Australia, New Zealand, Sweden, Cyprus, Singapore, Japan, UK, Ireland): if not vaccinated, dogs must be vaccinated within 5 days of arrival.
documents: Veterinary health certificate on the Israeli model, signed or endorsed by a government veterinarian of the origin country, issued within 10 days before departure (USDA: no more than 10 days before arrival)
Owner declaration that the pet has been in their possession for at least 90 days (Annex C)
Notification of Pet Arrival (Annex B) plus a copy of the certificate, sent to the port's Veterinary Services
Import permit only for more than 2 animals, unaccompanied or cargo shipments, or restricted breeds

countries.name: Isle of Man
countries.summary: Free movement of most dogs/cats from Great Britain (no animal health requirements) and from Northern Ireland; pets from the EU cannot land directly by private plane or boat (except from Ireland with DEFA pre-notification) and generally come via GB with an approved transporter; direct import from non-EU countries is prohibited (must enter GB first).
countries.microchip: Required for routes via GB/EU per GB/EU rules; not required for GB-IoM movement.
countries.rabies_titer: Only as required by GB rules for unlisted countries (pets must clear GB first).
countries.parasite_treatment: Dogs from the EU: tapeworm treatment 24-120 h before arrival in the UK/IoM (per GB rules).
countries.import_permit: Direct import from non-EU countries prohibited.
countries.quarantine: None for compliant GB-cleared pets.
countries.timeline: Contact your vet at least 4 months before travel (gov.im advice).
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited from import: XL Bully, Pit Bull Terrier, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa (by appearance); UK exemption certificates are not valid on IoM.
countries.private_aviation: Animals cannot be landed directly from an EU country to IoM by private aircraft (exception: Republic of Ireland with DEFA pre-notification). Non-EU origin: prohibited directly; enter GB via a Border Control Post first. GB to IoM by private jet: free movement for non-banned dogs/cats.
countries.export: To EU and Northern Ireland: Animal Health Certificate from a vet for each journey (Official Veterinarian), microchip, rabies, dog tapeworm, entry via Travellers' Point of Entry; EU pet passports issued to GB/IoM residents no longer valid from 22 Apr 2026. To Dublin Port: advance notice at least 24 h before arrival.
countries.authority: Department of Environment, Food and Agriculture (DEFA), Isle of Man
vaccinations: Rabies: required for pets coming from the EU/other countries via GB under GB rules; not for GB-IoM movement.
documents: GB/NI to IoM: none.
From Ireland direct: pre-notify DEFA.
EU via GB: GB entry documents (pet passport/AHC) and DEFRA-authorised pet transporter by prior arrangement with DEFA.

countries.name: India
countries.summary: Up to 2 pet dogs or cats per passenger may be imported under the Baggage Rules: transfer of residence (2+ years abroad), re-import, or short stay (short stay needs a DGFT licence). An Advance NOC must be obtained from AQCS through the CBIC ATITHI 2.0 portal at least 7 working days before embarkation. Entry only through the notified ports: Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru and Hyderabad.
countries.microchip: Required. Microchip number goes on the NOC application, and a vaccination and microchip certificate is submitted.
countries.import_permit: Advance NOC (AQCS) for all pets. A DGFT import licence for pets not on transfer of residence or re-import (short stays). More than 2 pets needs a DAHD sanitary import permit or DGFT licence.
countries.quarantine: None if the pet is healthy and documents are in order (Final NOC at the port). Pets failing the examination or showing disease signs: 15 days at the AQCS quarantine station at the owner's cost.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel (longer if a DGFT licence is needed, about 1 month): rabies vaccine ≥30 days before → health certificate and endorsement → ATITHI 2.0 application ≥7 working days before embarkation → Advance NOC (about 1 working day) → arrival inspection → Final NOC.
countries.private_aviation: No private-aircraft-specific rule found. The arrival airport must be one of the six notified ports (Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad), and the AQCS officer must examine the pet on arrival. Coordinate with AQCS and customs at that airport.
countries.export: Apply to AQCS for the export veterinary health certificate / NOC (fee Rs 500). Keep the AQCS export certificate, because it is required for later re-import.
countries.authority: Animal Quarantine and Certification Services (AQCS), Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD)
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 30 days and not more than 1 year before travel (Indian consulate guidance). US 3-year vaccines older than 1 year must be repeated.

Other vaccinations per the AQCS veterinary health certificate (Annexure 1.1.1). The certificate covers freedom from rabies and distemper, and for dogs also Aujeszky's, leishmaniasis and leptospirosis.
documents: Advance NOC from AQCS through the ATITHI 2.0 portal (application Annexure 1.1). Fee Rs 1000. Airlines will not carry the pet without it.
Official veterinary health certificate in AQCS format (Annexure 1.1.1), signed by the exporting country's competent authority
Vaccination and microchip certificate / pet passport
Air ticket or airway bill, passport copy
Proof of eligibility: transfer of residence (2-year overseas stay, relocation proof), re-import (earlier AQCS export certificate), or a DGFT licence for short stays
Final NOC issued by AQCS at the port after inspection, then customs clearance

countries.name: Iraq
countries.summary: The USDA–Iraq certificate requires a health certificate from a licensed veterinarian (valid 30 days, no USDA endorsement needed) with rabies vaccination details. No Iraqi official source was found for other origins.
countries.microchip: Listed if present (the certificate verifies microchips but does not explicitly require one).
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month before travel: rabies vaccination → health certificate within 30 days of travel. Kurdistan Region (Erbil) arrivals may have separate procedures, which are unverified.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture – Iraqi Veterinary Hospital / veterinary quarantine
vaccinations: Rabies: vaccination with date, vaccine name and validity period recorded on the certificate.
documents: Veterinary health certificate (US version: issued by a licensed vet, valid 30 days after issuance, USDA endorsement not required)

countries.name: Iran
countries.summary: Domestic animals need a health certificate from the origin country and approval from the Iran Veterinary Organization (IATA Timatic). Australia's export authority, citing customs regulations of Tehran's veterinary quarantine division, lists further documents: an international health certificate with the microchip number, issued by the origin veterinary authority and no more than 7 days old, the vaccination record (especially rabies), and the owner's passport, all in original plus copy. Belgium's foreign ministry advises against travelling to Iran with pets.
countries.microchip: Microchip number to be stated on the international health certificate (Micor citing Tehran veterinary quarantine regulations)
countries.import_permit: IVO approval required (IATA Timatic). Procedure not published.
countries.timeline: Obtain IVO approval → health certificate within 7 days before arrival. Contact IVO 1–2 months ahead.
countries.export: Leaving Iran: domestic animals need a health certificate from the Iran Veterinary Organization (IATA Timatic).
countries.authority: Iran Veterinary Organization (IVO)
vaccinations: Rabies: vaccination must be documented on the animal's health/vaccination card
documents: International health certificate issued by the official veterinary organisation of the origin country, with microchip number, issued no more than 7 days before presentation
Animal health identification card / vaccination record (especially rabies), original + copy
First page of the owner's passport, original + copy
Approval from the Iran Veterinary Organization (IVO)

countries.name: Iceland
countries.summary: Strict national regime (not the EU pet passport system): import permit from MAST, origin from an approved country, rabies vaccination plus titer test, multiple vaccinations/tests/parasite treatments, arrival only via Keflavík and minimum 14-day quarantine at an approved station.
countries.microchip: ISO-compliant microchip; number verified at every veterinary procedure for import.
countries.rabies_titer: Required from all origins: sample at least 30 days after vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml, EU-approved laboratory; valid while vaccination is kept up to date. For category 2 countries (e.g. Hungary, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Greenland, USA, Canada) travel only 90 days or more after sampling; animals qualify at earliest ~7 months old (category 1: ~4.5 months).
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal + external parasite treatment twice: 21-28 days and 5-10 days before import (products registered for roundworm, tapeworm, lice, fleas, ticks). Dogs: Angiostrongylus vasorum test within 30 days OR preventive imidacloprid+moxidectin treatment 5-10 days before.
countries.import_permit: Yes - MAST import permit required before import. Animal must have lived in an approved category 1 or 2 country since birth or for the last 6 months. Category 1 includes all EU states except HU, PL, RO, SK (category 2), plus NO (excl. Svalbard), CH, LI, FO, GB, AU, JP, SG, AE.
countries.quarantine: Minimum 14 days at an approved quarantine station (Reykjanesbær/Hafnir or Mósel/Hella), booked in advance; admissions only in set 3-day windows about 3 weeks apart; arrival at Keflavík 06:00-17:00 on admission dates; no overnight stays at the airport. Service dogs may apply for home quarantine.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4-6 months (category 2: ~7 months minimum age): import permit application (>=30 days before) -> book quarantine slot -> rabies vaccination -> titer test >=30 days later -> other vaccinations -> tests within 30 days of arrival -> parasite treatments at 21-28 and 5-10 days -> health exam + certificate 5-10 days before -> send to MAST >=5 days before -> fly to Keflavík on admission date.
countries.restricted_breeds: Banned: wolf hybrids (10 generations); Pit Bull Terrier/Staffordshire Bull Terrier (service-dog form also lists American Staffordshire Terrier and American Bulldog), Fila Brasileiro, Tosa Inu, Dogo Argentino, Cane Corso, Presa Canario, Boerboel and crosses (5 generations), plus dogs MAST assesses as comparable. Pregnant/lactating animals not accepted.
countries.private_aviation: Pets may only arrive by air at Keflavík Airport (only approved entry port; ferry arrival not permitted). Animals must be in a hard IATA-compliant crate (soft carriers not allowed); flight number and arrival time are recorded on the certificate; arrival must match a quarantine admission date and 06:00-17:00 window. Confirm with MAST and the quarantine station before planning a private-jet arrival.
countries.export: Leaving Iceland: destination-country rules apply (EU treats Iceland as an Annex I listed territory - EU pet passport/certificate, no titer). Contact MAST for export certification.
countries.authority: Icelandic Food and Veterinary Authority (MAST)
vaccinations: Rabies: valid vaccination; per MAST overview given at least 45-60 days before import (titer sample at earliest 30 days after vaccination).
Dogs: leptospirosis, distemper, infectious canine hepatitis, parvovirus, parainfluenza - last dose at least 14 days before import.
Cats: feline panleukopenia, rhinotracheitis, calicivirus - last dose at least 14 days before import.
Dogs from category 2 countries USA, Canada or Singapore: canine influenza vaccination also required (per certificate form).
documents: MAST import permit (apply at least 30 days before; valid 1 year; fee payable).
MAST certificate of health and origin (D1/D2 dogs, C1/C2 cats by country category), completed by authorised vet 5-10 days before import after health exam.
Lab reports: rabies titer; dogs Brucella canis (within 30 days) and Leishmania (intact dogs, within 30 days); cats FeLV and FIV (within 30 days).
Scanned certificate + lab results to petimport@mast.is no later than 5 days before arrival (later submission may be rejected).
Originals travel with the animal; customs declaration (VAT if owned < 12 months).

countries.name: Italy
countries.summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid. If the chip is not ISO 11784/11785-compliant, the owner must supply a reader.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU. Per the DGAL note (June 2026) listing the titer-exempt countries of Reg. (EU) 2026/636, the following are NOT listed, so pets coming from them need the titer + 3-month wait: Türkiye, Morocco, Israel, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Thailand, South Africa, Maldives, Bahamas (Mexico, Barbados, Cayman Islands, Malaysia and Taiwan ARE listed; Russia and Belarus were removed in 2024).
countries.parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks (EU/listed origin) or 4+ months (unlisted origin): microchip -> rabies vaccination (pet >=12 weeks) -> wait 21 days -> [unlisted origin: titer blood test >=30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months from sample] -> health certificate within 10 days before arrival (third countries) or EU passport -> enter via point of entry. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~10 days from the USA (EU-listed country; pet already chipped and rabies-vaccinated more than 21 days ago): EU animal health certificate issued and government-endorsed (USDA APHIS) within 10 days before arrival. From another EU state: no lead time beyond a valid EU pet passport. From an unlisted country without a prior titer: ~100+ days.
countries.restricted_breeds: No national dog-breed import ban identified in the official sources checked; local rules on dangerous dogs may apply - verify for bull/molosser types.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals from a non-EU country (other than Annex I territories AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA and Northern Ireland) must land at an airport designated as a travellers' point of entry and present the pet for documentary and identity checks (customs red channel). Italy's list (verified, 'aggiornato a settembre 2026', under Reg. 2026/131) designates about 40 airports incl. Rome Fiumicino and Ciampino, Milan Malpensa and Linate, Bergamo, Venice, Treviso, Florence, Pisa, Bologna, Naples, Olbia, Cagliari, Alghero, Catania, Palermo, Genoa, Turin, Verona, Rimini, Bari, Brindisi, Lampedusa, Pantelleria, Salerno, Comiso, Cuneo, Brescia, Parma, Perugia, Pescara, Trieste, Bolzano and others, plus ports. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
countries.export: To other EU/EEA states: EU pet passport from an authorised vet (plus tapeworm treatment for dogs going to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland). To non-EU countries: meet destination rules; export certificates are typically endorsed by the national/regional official veterinary service.
countries.authority: Ministry of Health - Directorate General for Animal Health
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 (Annex IV) model remain acceptable until 31 Mar 2027 if issued before 1 Oct 2026 (DGAL note, June 2026).
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.
Young animals: this country does NOT accept unvaccinated/insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under ~15 weeks) from other EU states; never allowed from third countries.

countries.name: Jersey
countries.summary: From UK, Isle of Man or other Channel Islands: no official health requirements. From EU/listed countries: microchip, rabies vaccination (21 days), EU pet passport or recent AHC, dog tapeworm treatment, non-commercial declaration; unlisted countries add a titer test. Pets may only arrive with approved carriers/routes - NOT by private aircraft.
countries.microchip: Microchip (or qualifying tattoo) before rabies vaccination.
countries.rabies_titer: Unlisted non-EU countries only: titer test passed, taken at least 30 days after vaccination and at least 3 months before travel into Jersey.
countries.parasite_treatment: Dogs: tapeworm treatment 24-120 h before scheduled arrival, recorded by the vet (product, date, time, stamp/signature). Exempt if travelling directly from Republic of Ireland, Malta, Finland or Norway.
countries.import_permit: Not for non-commercial pets; XL Bully type dogs need a licence to be imported/exported (since 24 Feb 2024, per gov.je).
countries.quarantine: None if compliant.
countries.timeline: UK/CI/IoM origin: none. EU/listed: at least 4 weeks. Unlisted: at least 4 months. Book an approved carrier.
countries.restricted_breeds: Certain dog types are illegal to bring into Jersey (see gov.je 'Dogs not allowed in Jersey'); dogs showing banned-breed characteristics may be seized. XL Bully types require a licence.
countries.private_aviation: Pets CANNOT enter Jersey on a private aircraft or private boat (except private boats from the Republic of Ireland). Only approved air/sea carriers and routes may be used.
countries.export: To EU: AHC (UK pet passports not accepted for EU entry). To UK/IoM/Guernsey: no official health requirements, though carriers may ask for documents.
countries.authority: Government of Jersey - Animal Health and Welfare (States Veterinary)
vaccinations: Rabies: pet >=12 weeks at vaccination, after microchipping, at least 21 days before travel.
documents: From EU: EU pet passport, or AHC issued in GB/Channel Islands/IoM within last 4 months (per gov.je), or GB pet health certificate, or GB pet passport issued before 1 Jan 2021.
Non-commercial declaration.
Australia (cats): Hendra certificate; Peninsular Malaysia: Nipah certificate.

countries.name: Jamaica
countries.summary: A strict permit regime applies. Get Preliminary Application approval, then a Veterinary Import Permit (J$5,000, valid 3 months). Pets need an ISO microchip, rabies vaccination, a FAVN of at least 0.5 IU/ml drawn 3–12 months before import, extensive tests and treatments, an officially endorsed certificate, arrival into Kingston, and at least 14 days' post-entry quarantine (Plumb Point).
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785 microchip, implanted before rabies vaccination (otherwise revaccinate). The number must match on all documents.
countries.rabies_titer: FAVN at an OIE/WOAH-approved lab, result at least 0.5 IU/ml. The pet is eligible for entry no less than 3 months and no more than 12 months after the successful blood draw. Send a copy to the Permit Unit at least 72 hours before export.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal: fecal exam plus 2 broad-spectrum dewormings at least 14 days apart, the last within 7 days of export. External: 2 treatments, the first about 30 days before shipment and the second within 7 days of export. Dogs: heartworm prevention within 7 days.
countries.import_permit: Required, or the pet is refused entry. Submit the Preliminary Application at least 1 month before travel (6 months if requirements aren't yet met), to vsdpermits@moa.gov.jm. Don't start tests (except rabies and FAVN) before approval. Fee J$5,000, valid up to 3 months.
countries.quarantine: At least 14 days of post-entry quarantine at the National Quarantine Facility, Plumb Point, unless the inspector permits otherwise (e.g. service dogs or approved pet travel schemes at an approved place).
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6 months before travel: microchip and rabies, FAVN, then a 3-month wait, preliminary application, permit; tests and treatments in the final 45 days; 3 weeks' notice plus a 72-hour confirmation.
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa, Pit Bull Terrier, and wolf or other hybrids.
countries.private_aviation: Pets must arrive directly into Kingston (Norman Manley/Palisadoes) unless the Chief Veterinary Officer authorizes another port. Pets normally travel as manifested cargo and are checked at the freight terminal (service dogs excepted), so obtain CVO approval for a private-jet or FBO arrival in advance. Arrive Mon–Thu 8:30 am–5:00 pm or Fri 8:30 am–4:00 pm; other times, weekends and holidays attract extra fees.
countries.export: Leaving Jamaica: follow the Ministry's 'Protocol for export of dogs and cats'. A pet that leaves loses its Jamaican health status, so discuss re-entry with the Veterinary Officer before departure, as a new import permit is needed. Jamaica isn't a CDC high-risk country, but it is on APHIS's screwworm-affected list, so dogs going to the US need a screwworm certificate.
countries.authority: Veterinary Services Division, Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Mining (Permit Unit)
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated vaccine given at 90 days of age or older and valid at export. Primary vaccination 6–12 months before shipment, or a booster no more than 1 year before shipment (per the 2017 US guidelines).
Dogs: distemper, parvovirus, hepatitis/adenovirus-2 and parainfluenza at least 2 weeks before export. Leptospira canicola vaccination up to date, or treatment within 30 days.
Cats: FHV-1, calicivirus, panleukopenia (FeLV for kittens) at least 2 weeks before export.
documents: Approved Preliminary Application Form, then a Veterinary Import Permit (applied online via MOA trade system).
Official model veterinary health certificate for Jamaica, completed or endorsed by an official vet (USDA), every page signed and stamped. Exam within 7 days of export.

Dogs: negative heartworm antigen (6 months or older, within 30 days); Babesia, Lyme and Ehrlichia ELISA within 16 days; Leishmania within 45 days; Brucella canis within 45 days (intact dogs); coccidia test.
Animal Landing Notification Form; customs broker details.

countries.name: Jordan
countries.summary: Per advice from Jordan's Ministry of Agriculture relayed by Australia's export authority (27 Nov 2025), import permits for pet cats and dogs are no longer issued. Pets need a veterinary health certificate stating the animal is free of rabies and rabies-vaccinated, and each traveller may bring at most 2 pets of each species (cats/dogs). It is not explicit whether the end of permits means no permit is needed or that permit-based imports stopped, so confirm with the Ministry (Agri@moa.gov.jo). Belgium's foreign ministry advises against bringing pets to Jordan.
countries.import_permit: Jordan MoA (via Australian DAFF Micor, 27 Nov 2025): import permits for pet cats and dogs will no longer be issued. Confirm with the Ministry what this means in practice.
countries.timeline: Rabies vaccination → health certificate shortly before travel. Validity window not published; confirm with the Jordanian Ministry of Agriculture.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture of Jordan (Agri@moa.gov.jo)
vaccinations: Rabies: vaccination required (timing not specified by official sources)
documents: Veterinary health certificate stating the animal is free of rabies and has received rabies vaccination

countries.name: Japan
countries.summary: From non-designated regions (most of the world, incl. mainland US and EU): microchip, then at least two rabies vaccinations, then a FAVN titer of at least 0.5 IU/ml, then a 180-day wait from the blood draw. Notify AQS at least 40 days before arrival. From designated rabies-free regions (Iceland, Australia, New Zealand, Fiji, Hawaii, Guam): microchip, residence proof and a government health certificate, with no vaccination or titer.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785, 15-digit. Must be implanted BEFORE the first rabies vaccination, or that vaccine is invalid. Chips starting '900 202' are currently not accepted. Other '900'-prefix chips may be duplicates, so tell AQS early.
countries.rabies_titer: Non-designated regions: FAVN at an AQS-designated laboratory, blood drawn after the 2nd vaccination, result of at least 0.5 IU/ml. Valid 2 years from sampling. Arrival must be at least 180 days after the blood draw. Not required from designated regions.
countries.import_permit: No permit, but the 40-day advance notification and AQS approval are mandatory. Late notifications are generally refused. You cannot move the arrival date earlier or add or swap animals.
countries.quarantine: If fully compliant, released after arrival inspection, within about 12 hours. If not compliant (including certificate errors or an early arrival before the 180 days are up), detained at an AQS facility for up to 180 days at the owner's cost, or returned.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 7–8 months before travel from non-designated regions: microchip → rabies #1 → rabies #2 (≥30 days later) → FAVN blood draw → wait 180 days → notify AQS ≥40 days before arrival → vet exam ≤10 days before departure → government endorsement → fly. Designated regions: at least 2 months (40-day notice plus certificates). LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~190 days from the USA or EU if the pet already has two valid rabies doses given after the microchip: FAVN draw, then 180 days, with the 40-day notice inside that window. If only one prior dose: ~220 days.
countries.private_aviation: AQS has no separate rule for private or business aircraft. Dogs may enter only through 19 designated ports. The 11 airports are New Chitose, Narita, Haneda, Chubu, Kansai, Osaka-Itami, Kobe, Kitakyushu, Fukuoka, Kagoshima and Naha. Cats arriving elsewhere need advance contact with AQS. Coordinate the AQS arrival inspection with the airport's AQS office and the FBO in advance. Full requirements apply as for commercial flights.
countries.export: Apply to AQS in advance and present the pet for export inspection at the date and time AQS sets. AQS issues the export quarantine certificate after meeting the destination's rules. For pets that will return, AQS recommends doing Japan's import requirements (microchip, 2 rabies shots, FAVN) before departure so re-entry is possible without detention.
countries.authority: Animal Quarantine Service (AQS), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF)
vaccinations: Rabies (non-designated regions): at least 2 doses of inactivated or recombinant vaccine. RNA and live vaccines are not accepted. Dose 1 at 91 days of age or older and after the microchip. Dose 2 at least 30 days after dose 1 and within dose 1's validity. Immunity must still be valid on arrival (booster if needed).
Designated regions: no rabies vaccination required.
documents: Advance notification to AQS at the port of entry (NACCS or email), at least 40 days before arrival, and the resulting approval

Health certificate Form AC (plus ATTACH if needed): completed by a vet and endorsed by the exporting country's government. Original in ink. E-certificates accepted only from USA, Brazil and Spain (designated regions: only Hawaii and Guam).
Clinical exam within 10 days before departure: no signs of rabies (dogs also no leptospirosis)

Designated regions: certificate of residence (since birth, 180+ days, or since import from Japan). Direct flight required, or an official crate seal plus a transport certificate if transiting a non-designated region.

countries.name: Kenya
countries.summary: Kenya requires an import permit from the Director of Veterinary Services, which must travel with the pet. The Ministry of Livestock Development's permit conditions require pets not from a WOAH rabies-free country to have a microchip, rabies vaccination and a rabies antibody titer of at least 0.5 IU/ml taken 3–24 months before shipment. Otherwise up to 6 months' quarantine may apply. The conditions also say pets must travel as manifest cargo in the hold, not in the cabin, which directly affects private-jet arrivals.
countries.microchip: Required for pets not from a rabies-free country (permanent mark such as a microchip; number stated on the certificate) per the Ministry of Livestock Development permit conditions. The UK certificate also records the microchip number.
countries.rabies_titer: Required for pets not kept since birth or for 6 months in a WOAH rabies-free country: antibody test of at least 0.5 IU/ml, sample taken 3–24 months before shipment (permit conditions). Without it, Kenya may quarantine the pet for up to 6 months at the owner's cost.
countries.parasite_treatment: The certificate (dated within 48 hours of embarkation) must attest the pet is free of internal and external parasites. No specific treatment window is stated.
countries.import_permit: Required. Issued by the Director of Veterinary Services (State Department for Livestock Development), Kabete, Nairobi, or via Kenyan missions (UK: Kenya High Commission, London). Valid 30 days maximum, single consignment, must accompany the animal. Recent embassy pages say applications go through the Kenya TradeNet (KenTrade) platform via accredited agents. Mission fees vary (e.g. USD 50 per animal).
countries.quarantine: None if compliant. Pets not meeting the microchip, vaccination and titer conditions may be quarantined for up to 6 months at the owner's expense. UK guidance says the same may apply if the animal lands in an intermediate country other than Australia, New Zealand, Norway, Sweden or Ireland without rabies vaccination in the past 6 months.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3 months for a vaccinated pet from a non-rabies-free origin (US and most of the EU): titer blood sample at least 3 months before shipment → apply for the permit via KenTrade, an agent or a mission → vet exam within 48 hours of departure and government endorsement → captain's certificate on arrival. Primary-vaccinated pets need at least 6 months after vaccination.
countries.private_aviation: High impact. The Ministry of Livestock Development permit conditions say animals must travel as manifest cargo in the aircraft freight compartment, not as baggage or in passenger cabins. They also require a captain's certificate that the animal stayed on board and was isolated. The ports of entry are named on the permit (normally JKIA or Mombasa). Get written confirmation from DVS before booking a cabin-carriage private flight, and pre-arrange veterinary inspection at the arrival airport.
countries.authority: Directorate of Veterinary Services (State Department for Livestock Development), Kenya
vaccinations: Rabies (pets not from a WOAH rabies-free country): inactivated or recombinant vaccine. A primary vaccination must be given at 3+ months of age and 6–12 months before shipment; a booster no more than 1 year before shipment (Ministry of Livestock Development permit conditions, published by the Kenya Embassy Spain, 2024).
The certificate must state vaccine name, manufacturer, batch number, date and the animal's age at vaccination (UK NFG 2913, revised 11/2023).
The US-origin APHIS certificate asks for rabies vaccination within 12 months before export; the permit conditions above are stricter, so follow the permit.
documents: Kenyan import permit (Director of Veterinary Services). Valid 30 days maximum, one consignment, and must accompany the animal.

International veterinary health certificate: exam within 48 hours of embarkation (permit conditions). The UK certificate requires an exam within 5 days and is valid 7 days. The US APHIS certificate is valid 30 days.
Rabies vaccination certificate and rabies titer lab report (non-rabies-free origins)

Certificate from the captain of the aircraft or ship stating the animal did not leave the aircraft between embarkation and Kenya and was isolated from other dogs and cats (permit conditions; UK master's declaration 2913MAS)
For the permit: formal request letter and copy of the owner's passport (Kenyan missions). Embassy pages say applications go through the Kenya TradeNet platform via accredited agents.

countries.name: Kyrgyzstan
countries.summary: EAEU member with the same rules as Russia. Up to 2 personal dogs/cats may enter on an international passport with rabies and core vaccines and a clinical-exam mark from within 14 days; otherwise an EAEU Form 15 certificate is needed. For US origin, APHIS allows up to 5 pets on Form 15 issued within 5 days of travel.
countries.microchip: Not mandated by EAEU rules; recommended
countries.rabies_titer: Not required (alternative only)
countries.import_permit: Not needed for ≤2 personal pets (EAEU); APHIS states up to 5 without special permission
countries.quarantine: None for compliant personal pets
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month: vaccines ≥20 days before → exam/certificate within 5 days
countries.authority: Veterinary authority of the Kyrgyz Republic, Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture and Processing Industry (EAEU common veterinary requirements)
vaccinations: Rabies: dogs/cats ≥3 months, ≥20 days before travel unless vaccinated within last 12 months (multi-year vaccine OK while valid)
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, adenovirus, leptospirosis — ≥20 days, ≤12 months before
Cats: panleukopenia — ≥20 days, ≤12 months before
documents: International pet passport with clinical exam mark ≤14 days (≤2 pets), or EAEU Form 15 certificate (APHIS: issued and endorsed within 5 days of travel)

countries.name: Cambodia
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.authority: General Directorate of Animal Health and Production (Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries)

countries.name: Kiribati
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.authority: Ministry of Environment, Lands and Agricultural Development (Agriculture and Livestock Division)

countries.name: Comoros
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2 months before travel: obtain written requirements from the Comoros Ministry of Agriculture (veterinary services) or embassy, then vaccination and certificate as instructed.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Environment — veterinary services (to be confirmed)
documents: For US-origin pets (APHIS): no Comoros pet page; APHIS 'Unknown Requirements' guidance advises a vet-issued health certificate (e.g. APHIS Form 7001, preferably USDA-endorsed) and proof of current rabies vaccination.

countries.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
countries.summary: A Veterinary Services import permit is required. Pets from rabies-endemic countries (including the US) need an ISO microchip, current rabies vaccination, a FAVN of at least 0.5 IU/ml (lab sends results directly), a government-endorsed health certificate within 30 days, parasite treatment within 5 days, and 14 days of home confinement after arrival.
countries.microchip: ISO-compatible microchip (e.g. AVID, HomeAgain). The number must appear on the application, certificates, blood sample and titer result.
countries.rabies_titer: From rabies-endemic countries: one FAVN of at least 0.5 IU/ml at a WOAH-approved lab (in the US: Kansas State or Auburn), drawn at least 30 days after the most recent rabies vaccine and at least 3 months before that vaccine expires. The lab emails results directly to Veterinary Services (St Kitts: skbvet12@gmail.com; Nevis: ambi.james@gmail.com). If it fails, give a booster and retest after 30 days.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatment (broad-spectrum anthelmintic, product named) within 5 days of arrival, on a health certificate by an accredited vet.
countries.import_permit: Required. Apply to Veterinary Services, Department of Agriculture, La Guerite, Basseterre (tel. 869-465-2110). The application states the arrival date, flight and time.
countries.quarantine: 14 days of home confinement for new entrants, with 3 home visits; a completion certificate is issued at the end.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6–8 weeks before travel: microchip, rabies, FAVN at least 30 days later, permit application, health certificate within 30 days, parasite treatment within 5 days of arrival.
countries.private_aviation: Non-compliance can lead to deportation or euthanasia (APHIS). Confirm the arrival port and inspector availability for private flights with Veterinary Services.
countries.authority: Veterinary Services, Department of Agriculture, St. Kitts (and Nevis office)
vaccinations: Rabies: current (1- or 3-year), approved monovalent killed vaccine, not given before 3 months of age. The health certificate lists the last 2 rabies vaccinations.
Core vaccines (dogs and cats) up to date.
documents: Import permit application (fee EC$55 or US$20 per animal, by international money order to 'Accountant General', or paid on arrival).
Government-issued international health certificate (USDA-endorsed) within 30 days of arrival. Required for first entry only.
Cats (first entry): FIV and FeLV negative within 30 days of arrival.
Rabies certificate; FAVN report with the microchip number.

countries.name: North Korea
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.authority: Unknown (DPRK state veterinary authority)

countries.name: South Korea
countries.summary: ISO microchip plus a government-endorsed health certificate. Dogs and cats aged 90 days or older from non-rabies-free countries (incl. the USA) also need a current rabies vaccination and a rabies antibody test of at least 0.5 IU/ml. No post-titer waiting period. Pets missing the chip or titer are held in quarantine at the owner's cost until it is done.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785 compliant, number on the health certificate. If missing, it can be implanted after arrival during quarantine at the owner's cost.
countries.rabies_titer: Non-rabies-free origin, age 90 days or older: rabies-neutralising antibody result of at least 0.5 IU/ml, from an internationally approved lab or the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 24 months from blood draw. No waiting period after the result. Older sources say sampling must be at least 30 days after vaccination. If missing or under 0.5, the test is done in quarantine after arrival.
countries.import_permit: No import permit for personal pets. Larger groups need advance notification to APQA and prior approval of a quarantine facility. Sources cite 5 or more and 10 or more animals, so confirm the threshold.
countries.quarantine: None if compliant (arrival inspection only). Pets missing the chip or titer, with a mismatched chip, or with a titer under 0.5 IU/ml are held at the owner's expense until it is resolved, typically about 10 days, sometimes longer. A missing health certificate can mean return to origin.
countries.timeline: An already chipped and vaccinated pet needs about 1 month: titer blood draw (common practice: at least 30 days after the vaccine) → lab result (usually 2–4 weeks) → Korea-specific health certificate (valid 30 days) and USDA/official endorsement. A titer result from the last 24 months can be reused.
countries.restricted_breeds: No import breed ban found. Korea has domestic 'dangerous dog' rules (e.g. Tosa, Pit Bull types, Rottweiler) that impose owner obligations after entry. Verify before travel.
countries.private_aviation: No private-aircraft-specific rule found. Arrange the APQA arrival inspection at the arrival airport (e.g. Incheon or Gimpo) in advance through the handler or FBO.
countries.export: APQA issues an export quarantine certificate after inspection at its airport or port office, based on the destination's requirements.
countries.authority: Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency (APQA / QIA), Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs
vaccinations: Rabies (age 90 days or older, non-rabies-free origin): current at arrival. The APQA FAQ indicates at least 30 days since vaccination and still within immunity. If under 30 days, the pet is held until 30 days have passed.
Pets under 90 days or from APQA-listed rabies-free countries: rabies vaccination not required, but chip and certificate still required.
documents: Health certificate issued or endorsed by the exporting country's veterinary authority, stating the microchip number, birth date, rabies vaccination and titer result. For US origin, USDA-endorsed within 30 days of export.
Rabies vaccination certificate
Rabies antibody test report (where required)
Cats from Australia and dogs/cats from Malaysia: extra Hendra/Nipah freedom certificate, otherwise quarantine is extended 21 days (older official guidance)

countries.name: Kuwait
countries.summary: PAAF's official health certificate (Oct 2026 version) requires rabies vaccination and a rabies titre of at least 0.5 IU/ml taken 3–12 months before entry. It also requires core vaccines, parasite treatment within 14 days, and IATA transport. A long list of dog breeds is prohibited.
countries.microchip: Microchip number (10 to 15 digits) recorded on the PAAF certificate.
countries.rabies_titer: Required: an antibody titration of at least 0.5 IU/ml per the WOAH Manual, with the sample taken not less than 3 months and not more than 12 months before entry into Kuwait.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatment within 14 days before export.
countries.import_permit: Not stated on the official PAAF certificate or the USDA page. Third-party guides report that a PAAF import permit is needed, possibly via a local agent, and that individuals are limited (e.g. one dog per year). Commercial imports of dogs and cats were reportedly banned. Verify with PAAF (info@paaf.gov.kw).
countries.quarantine: No routine quarantine is stated. Animals are held in the Kuwait quarantine station if certificate conditions are not met.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 months before travel: microchip → rabies vaccination → titre blood draw (at least 3 months before entry) → core vaccines → parasite treatment within 14 days → PAAF-format health certificate → arrival.
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited (including any mixes): Pit Bulls, American Pit Bull Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, American Bully, American Staffordshire Terrier, American Bulldog, Mastiff, Tibetan Mastiff, Fila Brasileiro, Dogo Argentino, Neapolitan Mastiff, Dogue de Bordeaux, Perro de Presa Canario/Dogo Canario, Cane Corso, Tosa, Bully Kutta/Alangu, Bullmastiff, Boerboel, Rottweiler, Central Asian Shepherd (Alabai), Wolf Dog, Caucasian Shepherd (Ovcharka), Doberman Pinscher, Anatolian Shepherd/Kangal.
countries.authority: Public Authority of Agriculture Affairs and Fish Resources (PAAF)
vaccinations: Rabies: required for animals from rabies-infected countries, using a WOAH-compliant vaccine given per the manufacturer's recommendations.
Dogs: canine parvovirus, canine distemper, infectious canine hepatitis, leptospirosis (icterohaemorrhagiae and canicola).
Cats: feline panleukopenia, feline rhinotracheitis, feline calicivirus.
documents: PAAF veterinary health certificate for dogs, cats and ferrets, endorsed by the official government veterinarian of the exporting country. The USDA page conflicts on whether APHIS endorsement is needed for US origin, so confirm.
Rabies vaccination and titre details on the certificate
Clinical examination statement (free of infectious disease, fit to travel)

countries.name: Cayman Islands
countries.summary: A Department of Agriculture import permit is needed. Pets need an ISO microchip, rabies vaccination per Cayman guidelines and, unless coming from a 'no rabies-risk' territory, a FAVN titer: 'low-risk' origins (US mainland, Canada) may enter no sooner than 2 months after the blood draw, 'high-risk' origins (e.g. Mexico, Puerto Rico, Dominican Republic) 3 months. 'No-risk' territories include the UK, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Switzerland, Netherlands, Portugal, Greece, Monaco, Bahamas, Barbados, Australia and New Zealand. No quarantine option: non-compliant pets are returned or destroyed. No direct imports from Asia (incl. UAE), Africa, or Central/South America.
countries.microchip: ISO-compliant 15-digit chip if implanted on or after 1 Mar 2019 (older chips: 10 or more characters), implanted BEFORE rabies vaccination, otherwise revaccinate. Scanned at each step.
countries.rabies_titer: Required unless coming from a 'no rabies-risk' territory (official 2026 list includes e.g. UK, Ireland, France, Germany, Italy, Spain incl. Balearics/Canaries, Portugal, Greece, Netherlands, Belgium, Switzerland, Monaco, Austria, Bahamas, Barbados, Bermuda, Jamaica, Hawaii, Australia, New Zealand). Blood drawn at least 30 days after vaccination at a Cayman-approved lab, result at least 0.5 IU/ml with the microchip number, repeated every 12 months. Earliest entry after the draw: 2 months for 'low risk' origins (US mainland, Canada, Bulgaria, Croatia, Hungary, Latvia, Estonia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Grenada, Trinidad & Tobago) and 3 months for 'high risk' origins (e.g. Mexico, Puerto Rico, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Haiti, Poland, Romania, Lithuania, Serbia, Montenegro, Greenland). Pets must have resided in the origin country for at least 3 months. Animals arriving by sea are treated as high risk.
countries.parasite_treatment: On the day of the vet examination, within 14 days before travel: praziquantel at 5 mg/kg (tapeworm) plus a systemic tick product with residual action. Shampoos, collars and flea-only products are not accepted.
countries.import_permit: Required. Email the application and documents to ci.agriculturevs@gov.ky, up to 6 months before travel. Fee CI$50 / US$61 per animal. Decision within 3 working days of a complete file. The health certificate must be added within 14 days before entry.
countries.quarantine: None available. Non-compliant animals are refused and returned immediately, or destroyed, at the importer's expense. Dogs staying more than 30 days must be licensed.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3 months (US mainland) or 4 months (higher-risk origins) before travel: microchip, then rabies vaccine, then FAVN at least 30 days later, then wait 2–3 months; apply for the permit; vet exam and treatments within 14 days of travel; give 48 hours' notice of arrival. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~65 days from the US mainland (titer blood draw on a currently vaccinated pet, then 2 months' wait). From 'no-risk' EU countries or the UK: ~3 weeks (permit, exam and treatments within 14 days). From the UAE: not possible directly (must route via a non-Asian country).
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Pit Bull Terrier types, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa, and dogs bred for fighting. Crosses are allowed only if spayed or neutered (proof required) and not pregnant. Purebreds not originating in Cayman are never admitted.
countries.private_aviation: Travel by the most direct route. No animal may be imported DIRECTLY from Asia (including the UAE/Dubai), Africa, or Central or South America. Transit through such a country requires a government-sealed crate. Give 48 hours' notice of arrival time and flight. DoA office hours are Mon–Fri 8:30 am–5:00 pm, so confirm inspector availability for FBO arrivals outside these hours.
countries.export: Leaving Cayman: DoA export permit/health certificate (fee CI$20 / US$25 per animal). Pets abroad for less than 14 days can re-enter on the export certificate plus a tick and tapeworm treatment.
countries.authority: Cayman Islands Department of Agriculture – Veterinary Services
vaccinations: Rabies: first vaccine at 12 weeks or older; booster 9–12 months later; 2- or 3-year intervals only after that second dose. Valid for entry 30 days after vaccination for 'no-risk' origins.
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis and parvovirus mandatory. Cats: panleukopenia, herpesvirus and calicivirus mandatory.
documents: Cayman Islands import permit (single entry, valid 14 days from the health-certificate exam date).

Veterinary health certificate completed within 14 days of travel. The new US VEHCS certificate (Sep 2026) includes a USDA endorsement block, and APHIS indicates endorsement applies from 1 Oct 2026; previously Cayman needed no APHIS endorsement for dogs and cats. Original presented on arrival.
FAVN report, rabies and routine vaccination certificates, signed breed declaration and full-body colour photo (dogs).

countries.name: Kazakhstan
countries.summary: EAEU member with the same rules as Russia. Up to 2 personal dogs/cats may enter on an international passport with rabies and core vaccines and a clinical-exam mark from within 14 days; otherwise an EAEU Form 15 certificate is needed. For US origin, APHIS allows up to 5 pets on Form 15 issued within 5 days of travel.
countries.microchip: Not mandated by EAEU rules; recommended
countries.rabies_titer: Not required (alternative only)
countries.import_permit: Not needed for ≤2 personal pets (EAEU); APHIS states up to 5 without special permission
countries.quarantine: None for compliant personal pets
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month: vaccines ≥20 days before → exam/certificate within 5 days
countries.authority: Committee of Veterinary Control and Supervision, Ministry of Agriculture of Kazakhstan (EAEU common veterinary requirements)
vaccinations: Rabies: dogs/cats ≥3 months, ≥20 days before travel unless vaccinated within last 12 months (multi-year vaccine OK while valid)
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, adenovirus, leptospirosis — ≥20 days, ≤12 months before
Cats: panleukopenia — ≥20 days, ≤12 months before
documents: International pet passport with clinical exam mark ≤14 days (≤2 pets), or EAEU Form 15 certificate (APHIS: issued and endorsed within 5 days of travel)

countries.name: Laos
countries.summary: A DLF import licence is required before shipment, plus the official Lao import health certificate (Form 3). Requirements: microchip, core vaccines at least 14 days before export, rabies vaccination at least 30 days before export, and a titer of at least 0.5 IU/ml (blood drawn at least 30 days after vaccination and within 6 months of export). Internal and external parasite treatment 2–7 days before export. Certificate valid 7 days. Pets not meeting the rabies rules are vaccinated on arrival and confined at home for at least 21 days.
countries.microchip: Required in practice: the certificate records a microchip (or ID) number scanned before export that matches the vaccination certificate.
countries.rabies_titer: Rabies neutralising antibody of at least 0.5 IU/ml by a WOAH-prescribed test. Blood drawn at least 30 days after rabies vaccination and within 6 months before export. The test report must go with the certificate. The form says 'whenever require'; if the rabies conditions are not met, the pet is vaccinated on arrival and confined separately at home for at least 21 days.
countries.parasite_treatment: External (fleas and ticks) and internal (nematodes and cestodes) treatment between 2 and 7 days before export, with product, active ingredient and date recorded.
countries.import_permit: Yes. A valid Department of Livestock and Fisheries (DLF) import licence must be obtained before shipment. Processing time and fees are not published officially; secondary sources cite an application at least 15 days before arrival.
countries.quarantine: No routine quarantine for compliant pets. Pets not meeting the rabies conditions are vaccinated on arrival and confined at home for at least 21 days.
countries.timeline: An already chipped and vaccinated pet (vaccine at least 30 days old) needs about 1 month: titer blood draw → result → DLF licence → parasite treatments, exam and official endorsement within 7 days of export.
countries.restricted_breeds: Banned with crosses: Pit Bull types (incl. American Pit Bull Terrier), American Staffordshire Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, American Bulldog, Neapolitan Mastiff, Tosa, Akita, Dogo Argentino, Boerboel, Fila Brasileiro, Perro de Presa Canario. Also Bengal and Savannah cat crosses of 4th generation and below. Pregnant females are not accepted.
countries.private_aviation: No private-aircraft rule found. Clearance needs customs and quarantine officers at the port of entry, so arrange this in advance for a GA arrival (e.g. Vientiane Wattay).
countries.authority: Department of Livestock and Fisheries (DLF), Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, Lao PDR
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated or recombinant vaccine acceptable to DLF, at least 1 month before export, and a valid primary or booster course.
Dogs: distemper, infectious hepatitis and parvovirus, at least 14 days before export.
Cats: calicivirus, rhinotracheitis and panleukopenia, at least 14 days before export.
documents: DLF import licence (number shown on the certificate)

Animal Health Certificate for the Import of Dogs and Cats into Lao PDR (Form 3). Sections I–III by a government-approved or official vet; Section IV endorsed by the official government vet of the exporting country (USDA for the US). Valid 7 days.
Rabies vaccination certificate and titer report
Present the import licence and health certificate to customs and quarantine officers at the port of entry

countries.name: Lebanon
countries.summary: According to IATA Traveldoc, pets must be declared to customs and carry a valid health certificate from the country of origin and a valid rabies vaccination certificate. USDA has not been officially informed of Lebanon's requirements.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month before travel: rabies vaccination → health certificate from the origin country → declare at customs. Confirm with the Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture (Lebanon) / Lebanese Customs
vaccinations: Rabies: valid rabies vaccination certificate required (timing not specified).
documents: Valid health certificate issued in the country of origin
Valid rabies vaccination certificate
Customs declaration of the pet on arrival

countries.name: Saint Lucia
countries.summary: Get a Veterinary Import Permit (EC$45, about 2 business days). Pets need an ISO microchip, rabies vaccination at least 30 days before export, and a FAVN of at least 0.5 IU/ml. Entry is not allowed until 3 months after the successful blood draw. Pets also need a vet exam within 14 days, an APHIS-endorsed certificate, and 3 days' notice of arrival.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785 microchip, or a non-ISO chip with the owner providing a reader. Implanted before rabies vaccination.
countries.rabies_titer: FAVN at an approved lab, blood drawn at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml. Entry not allowed until 3 months after the successful blood draw. The original lab report accompanies the certificate.
countries.parasite_treatment: Endoparasites (including tapeworm) and ectoparasites (including ticks) treated 'not less than 14 days prior to export', per the US certificate wording, so confirm the exact window with VLSD. The pet must be free of external parasites at the exam.
countries.import_permit: Required. Email the application form and documents to vlsdsec.agriculture@govt.lc. Processing about 2 business days; fee EC$45 paid on entry. Animals without a permit are refused or euthanized.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–5 months before travel: microchip, rabies, FAVN at least 30 days later, then a 3-month wait. In parallel, get the permit; vaccines and tests within 14 days; give 3 days' notice.
countries.restricted_breeds: Saint Lucia publishes a separate 'Prohibited Dog Breeds' list (govt.lc). Check it before booking.
countries.private_aviation: Notify the Veterinary and Livestock Services Division of the port of entry (Hewanorra UVF or George F.L. Charles SLU), date, time and flight at least 3 days before arrival. Office hours are 8:00 am–4:30 pm. Pets must travel directly and not contact other animals on the flight.
countries.authority: Veterinary and Livestock Services Division, Ministry of Agriculture, Saint Lucia
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated and adjuvanted, at 12 weeks or older, after the microchip, no less than 30 days before export.
Dogs: distemper, leptospirosis, hepatitis/adenovirus, parainfluenza and parvovirus at least 14 days before export.
Cats: FeLV, rhinotracheitis, calicivirus, panleukopenia and pneumonitis at least 14 days before export.
documents: Veterinary Import Permit.
US health certificate for Saint Lucia (exam within 14 days before export), endorsed by APHIS (digital via VEHCS).
Dogs: negative heartworm and Lyme tests sampled within 14 days before export.

countries.name: Liechtenstein
countries.summary: Liechtenstein is an EU Annex I listed territory with an open border to Switzerland and no airport; pets in practice arrive via Switzerland (or Austria) and must meet the rules of that entry country (Swiss rules: microchip, rabies vaccination, pet passport or health certificate).
countries.microchip: Microchip required before rabies vaccination (Swiss/EU rules).
countries.rabies_titer: Per Swiss rules: required only from rabies high-risk third countries.
countries.import_permit: See Switzerland (FSVO authorisation for direct flights from high-risk countries).
countries.quarantine: None if requirements met (Swiss/EU rules).
countries.timeline: As for Switzerland: at least 4 weeks from EU/low-risk origin; 4+ months from high-risk origin.
countries.restricted_breeds: Liechtenstein-specific breed rules not verified.
countries.private_aviation: No airport in Liechtenstein. Private jets land in Switzerland (e.g. Zurich, Basel, Geneva are the Swiss pet entry airports for third-country arrivals) or Austria/Germany; the landing country's entry rules apply.
countries.export: EU treats Liechtenstein as an Annex I listed territory (pet passport, no titer). Liechtenstein-specific export procedure not verified.
countries.authority: Office of Food Safety and Veterinary Affairs (ALKVW), Liechtenstein; Swiss FSVO for border controls
vaccinations: Rabies: pet >=12 weeks at vaccination, valid 21 days after primary vaccination (Swiss/EU rules).
documents: EU/Swiss pet passport (from EU/CH), or health certificate meeting Swiss rules from third countries.

countries.name: Sri Lanka
countries.summary: A DAPH import permit is required. Under rules in force since 1 January 2026, dogs and cats need an ISO microchip, up-to-date core and rabies vaccinations, parasite treatment within 14 days, and an official health certificate within 10 days of export. Dogs also need negative leishmaniasis and heartworm tests within 1 month of departure.
countries.microchip: ISO-compliant microchip, number shown on all documents (vaccination records, blood test reports).
countries.parasite_treatment: Ecto- and endoparasite treatment within 14 days before departure, certified in writing by a registered vet.
countries.import_permit: Yes. Import permit from the Director General, Department of Animal Production and Health (Animal Diseases Act No. 59 of 1992).
countries.quarantine: The permit application commits the importer to quarantine and inspection or sampling by DAPH. The length is not stated in the 2026 requirements, so confirm with DAPH.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6–8 weeks before travel: vaccinations up to date → apply for the DAPH permit → dog blood tests within 1 month of departure → parasite treatment within 14 days → health certificate within 10 days → fly.
countries.private_aviation: No private-aircraft-specific rule found. Arrange the DAPH quarantine officer inspection at the arrival airport in advance.
countries.authority: Department of Animal Production and Health (DAPH)
vaccinations: Dogs: rabies, canine distemper, parvovirus, infectious hepatitis, leptospirosis (fully vaccinated and up to date)
Cats: rabies, feline calicivirus, feline herpesvirus 1, feline panleukopenia
Under 3 months old: the dam must be fully vaccinated. Minimum import age 1.5 months.
documents: DAPH import permit (application via the DAPH Google form; enquiries vraanim@gmail.com)
Vaccination records (submitted with the permit application)
Dogs only: negative leishmaniasis (PCR/ELISA/IFAT), heartworm antigen and microfilaria tests within 1 month of departure. Waived for a disease the exporting country is officially free of.
International Veterinary Health Certificate from the exporting country's competent authority, issued within 10 days before export

countries.name: Liberia
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.import_permit: Non-official sources say an import permit from the Ministry of Agriculture is required, but others disagree. Not confirmed officially.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel: obtain written confirmation of requirements from Liberia's Ministry of Agriculture before booking.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture (Liberia) – not verified from an official source

countries.name: Lesotho
countries.summary: Pets need a live-animal import permit from Lesotho's Ministry of Agriculture, Food Security and Nutrition. The fee is M200 and processing takes 3–5 days. The official listing names the documents (application, lab reports, vaccination history) but gives no pet-specific health rules, so confirm vaccination and certificate details with the Ministry.
countries.import_permit: Required: 'Import and export of live animals' service, Ministry of Agriculture, Food Security and Nutrition. Fee for pets M200; processing 3–5 days; apply online via gov.ls e-service. Contact: +266 8001 0100, contact.centre@gov.ls.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3–4 weeks before travel: confirm health requirements with the Ministry → gather vaccination history/lab reports → apply for permit (3–5 days) → origin health certificate shortly before departure.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Food Security and Nutrition (Lesotho) – livestock/veterinary services
vaccinations: Vaccination history required with the permit application (official gov.ls listing); specific vaccines/timing not stated officially
documents: Completed import application form
Laboratory reports for the animal(s)
Vaccination history
Proof of registered establishment (as listed generically for live animals)
Transit/removal permit if passing through a third country

countries.name: Lithuania
