countries.authority: Direcção da Pecuária (Livestock Directorate), São Tomé and Príncipe

countries.name: El Salvador
countries.summary: Pets need a licensed-vet health certificate (exam within 30 days, no USDA endorsement or consular stamp) and rabies vaccination no more than 365 days before embarkation for animals over 2 months. A MAG import permit (before travel or on arrival) and a quarantine permit at the port are required.
countries.parasite_treatment: Treated for endo- and ectoparasites with approved products (no timing stated).
countries.import_permit: Required, from the Dirección General de Sanidad Vegetal y Animal (MAG). Can be obtained before travel or on arrival at the port of entry. A quarantine permit is also obtained at the port on arrival.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2 weeks before travel: rabies (within 365 days), vet exam within 30 days.
countries.export: Return to the US: El Salvador IS a CDC high-risk dog-rabies country (USDA-endorsed CDC certification before leaving the US, or arrival at a CDC-registered facility airport). A screwworm certificate is also needed.
countries.authority: Ministerio de Agricultura y Ganadería (MAG) – Dirección General de Sanidad Vegetal y Animal
vaccinations: Rabies: animals over 2 months, vaccinated no more than 365 days before embarkation. The certificate states the date and product.
documents: Health certificate by a licensed vet, exam within 30 days of departure, in at least duplicate. No USDA endorsement, notary or consular stamp.
Rabies vaccination certificate.

countries.name: Sint Maarten (Dutch part)
countries.summary: Get an Animal Movement/Import permit from Inspectorate TEATT (Unit LVV), valid for entry within 30 days, plus an endorsed international health certificate. Pets must be 15 weeks or older, microchipped, rabies-vaccinated at least 21 days before departure and parasite-treated. Dogs and cats from South and Central America (except Suriname) are prohibited.
countries.microchip: ISO microchip, or a readable tattoo applied before July 2011. The number must be on the certificate.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal: negative fecal flotation, or if positive, treatment 21 days before departure. External: parasiticide (e.g. Frontline, NexGard, Bravecto) 7–14 days before departure; free of Amblyomma and Boophilus ticks.
countries.import_permit: Required. Apply to Inspectorate TEATT – Unit LVV (LVV@sintmaartengov.org) via sintmaartengov.org.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–5 weeks before travel: rabies at least 21 days before departure, fecal test and deworming, permit, tick treatment 7–14 days before departure, APHIS endorsement.
countries.restricted_breeds: Pit bull terrier types are permitted only if neutered or spayed (stated on the certificate).
countries.private_aviation: No private-aviation specifics are published. The USDA-hosted version mentions inspection by a licensed vet within 24 hours of arrival, which isn't in the 2022 conditions, so confirm with LVV.
countries.authority: Ministry of Tourism, Economic Affairs, Transport & Telecommunication (TEATT) – Inspectorate, Unit LVV
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 21 days and no more than 1 or 3 years (per the vaccine) before departure.
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis, Bordetella and parvovirus.
Cats: FeLV, rhinotracheitis, calicivirus, panleukopenia and pneumonitis.
documents: Sint Maarten import permit (valid 30 days from issue).
International health certificate in English or Dutch, from an accredited vet and endorsed by the exporting country's Chief Veterinary Officer (APHIS, via VEHCS). EU pet passports are NOT accepted.
Copy of the owner's passport; Animal Movement Authorization Form if the owner isn't travelling.

countries.name: Syria
countries.summary: According to IATA Traveldoc, pets must have a health certificate in English authenticated in the origin country, and cats and dogs need a rabies vaccination certificate. No official Syrian veterinary source was found.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month before travel. Verify the current situation and requirements with operations, as the administrative situation may have changed.
countries.authority: Unknown (Syrian Ministry of Agriculture / Syrian Customs)
vaccinations: Rabies: vaccination certificate required (timing not specified).
documents: Health certificate in English, authenticated in the origin country
Rabies vaccination certificate

countries.name: Eswatini
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.import_permit: Not confirmed from an official source. Non-official guides conflict on whether a veterinary import permit is needed (some say only for high-rabies-risk origins). The government site (gov.sz) was unreachable. Most routings transit South Africa, which requires its own veterinary import permit for dogs and cats.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 8–12 weeks before travel: confirm with Eswatini Ministry of Agriculture, Veterinary Services whether an import permit is needed for the pet's origin; check South African transit rules if routing via South Africa.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Department of Veterinary and Livestock Services, Eswatini

countries.name: Turks and Caicos Islands
countries.summary: An import permit from the Department of Agriculture (Animal Health Services) is required, applied for with an APHIS-endorsed international health certificate that is valid 10 days from issue. The US and Canada are treated as NOT rabies-free. Several dog breeds are banned.
countries.import_permit: Required for all pets. Email, fax or post the application to the Department of Agriculture, Animal Health Services Division, Providenciales (agriculture@gov.tc, +1 649 946 5801).
countries.quarantine: No standard quarantine is published. Non-compliant animals may be held, deported within 48 hours at the owner's expense, or euthanized.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3–4 weeks before travel: vet certificate and APHIS endorsement, then the permit application within the 10-day certificate validity, then at least 48 hours' notice of arrival.
countries.restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Dogo Argentino, American Pit Bull Terrier, American Bulldog, American Staffordshire Terrier, Japanese Tosa, Perro de Presa Canario, Fila Brasileiro. Restricted (contact TCI first): Appenzeller, Aryan Molossus, Bandog, Beauceron, Belgian Mastiff, Bull Mastiff, Danish Broholmer, Dogue de Bordeaux, Great Swiss Mountain Dog, Korean Jindo, Kuvasz, Leonberger, Moscow Watchdog, Neapolitan Mastiff, Perro de Presa Mallorquin, Boerboel, Tibetan Mastiff.
countries.private_aviation: Must enter through an official port of entry. Give at least 48 hours' notice to the Inspection Unit of the confirmed arrival date, time, aircraft/flight and port of entry.
countries.authority: Turks and Caicos Islands Department of Agriculture – Animal Health Services Division
vaccinations: Rabies and other conditions are set out on the TCI import application and permit. The APHIS page doesn't state the timing, so confirm with the Department of Agriculture.
documents: TCI import permit.
International health certificate by a USDA-accredited vet, signed in non-black ink, endorsed by APHIS (original ink endorsement) BEFORE submitting the permit application. Valid 10 days from issue.
If the pet stays 24 hours or more in a transit country: a vet certificate covering that stay.

countries.name: Chad
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2 months before travel: obtain written requirements from Chad's ministry in charge of livestock (veterinary services) or embassy, then vaccination and certificate as instructed.
countries.authority: Ministère de l'Élevage et des Productions Animales — veterinary services (to be confirmed)
documents: For US-origin pets (APHIS): no Chad pet page; APHIS 'Unknown Requirements' guidance advises a vet-issued health certificate (e.g. APHIS Form 7001, preferably USDA-endorsed) and proof of current rabies vaccination.

countries.name: Togo
countries.summary: For US-origin pets (APHIS): microchip, current rabies vaccination, and a Togo-specific health certificate that USDA must ink-sign and emboss (no digital endorsement). No official rules were found for other origins or for an import permit.
countries.microchip: Required (US-origin certificate lists the microchip number as required and the vet must verify the chip).
countries.timeline: Plan at least 3-4 weeks before travel: microchip and rabies vaccination, then an accredited-vet health certificate, then USDA ink endorsement (allow time for mail or appointment).
countries.authority: Togolese veterinary authority (not named by APHIS); USDA APHIS for US-origin certification
vaccinations: Rabies: current at the time of export; the certificate records vaccine name, batch number and validity end date (APHIS, US-origin)
documents: Veterinary Health Certificate for Export of Dogs and Cats from the USA to the Togolese Republic (AUG 2025 form), signed by an accredited vet (electronic signature accepted) and ink-endorsed and embossed by USDA; the original must travel with the pet

countries.name: Thailand
countries.summary: Apply to the Animal Quarantine Station (AQS) at the arrival airport for a DLD import permit, at least 7 and no more than 60 days before departure (30 days recommended). The pet needs a government-endorsed health certificate and is inspected at the AQS on arrival. There is no titre test and normally no quarantine when documents are complete.
countries.microchip: Microchip number required on the application and records. The DLD advises implanting it before or on the same day as the rabies vaccination.
countries.import_permit: Yes: DLD import permit, emailed by the AQS at the port of entry. Processing takes 5-7 Thai business days and the permit is valid 60 days. Owners travelling with their pet may apply on arrival if all originals are ready, but airlines may refuse boarding without a permit.
countries.quarantine: No fixed quarantine when documents are complete. The pet is inspected at the AQS on arrival. If documents are incomplete, the pet may be held at the quarantine station.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 5-6 weeks: microchip, vaccines (21+ days before applying), permit request 30 days before departure, health certificate and endorsement within 10 days of arrival. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~14 days: apply for the import permit at least 7 days before (5-7 business days processing; 30 days recommended), certificate endorsed within 10 days of arrival.
countries.restricted_breeds: The Thai Embassy (Washington) says no dog breeds are banned, but airlines may restrict some. Minimum age 4 months (USDA summary).
countries.private_aviation: AQS offices are at Suvarnabhumi, Don Mueang, Chiang Mai, Phuket, Samui and Krabi (all 24 hours for hand-carried pets; the Suvarnabhumi cargo AQS is open 08:30-16:30 Mon-Fri). The permit names the port of entry. No rule specific to private jets was found. Coordinate the arrival airport's AQS inspection and the FBO in advance.
countries.export: DLD: the microchip must be implanted before or on the same day as the rabies vaccine. Present the pet and documents at the departure port's quarantine station, ideally 2-3 days before departure, to get the export certificate.
countries.authority: Department of Livestock Development (DLD), Animal Quarantine Stations
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 21 days before departure for a primary vaccine, given at 12 weeks of age or older. Boosters need no wait. Pets from rabies-free countries may be exempt.

Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, leptospirosis. If the leptospirosis vaccine is not valid or not 21+ days old, a negative leptospirosis test within 30 days before departure is accepted instead.
Cats: feline panleukopenia.
documents: Application Form R.1/1 with pet details and microchip implantation certificate
Copy of owner's passport and flight itinerary
Colour photo of the pet
English vaccination certificates
Official health certificate endorsed by the exporting country's veterinary authority (US: valid 10 days from USDA endorsement; originals only)
Printed import permit; Form R-6 and Import License R-7 issued at the AQS on arrival (500 THB per animal)

countries.name: Tajikistan
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.timeline: Contact the Tajik veterinary authority / embassy at least 2 months before travel
countries.authority: Veterinary authority of Tajikistan (Committee for Food Security under the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan) — not verified

countries.name: Timor-Leste
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries and Forestry (quarantine/biosecurity services)

countries.name: Turkmenistan
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.quarantine: Pets are subject to veterinary inspection on arrival (IATA Timatic). Quarantine rules not published.
countries.timeline: Contact the Turkmen embassy / State Veterinary Service at least 2 months before travel
countries.authority: State Veterinary Service of Turkmenistan (Ministry of Agriculture) — not verified

countries.name: Tunisia
countries.summary: Dogs and cats need an official health certificate (good health, no clinical signs of species-specific diseases) and a valid rabies vaccination given at least 30 days and at most 12 months before entry (Belgian foreign ministry). The certificate is checked at the border (IATA Timatic). Dangerous dogs such as pit bulls are prohibited. No Tunisian official page found.
countries.timeline: If the last rabies vaccination is more than 12 months old: revaccinate ≥30 days before entry. Then get the official health certificate shortly before travel (validity not published).
countries.restricted_breeds: Dangerous dogs such as Pit Bulls are prohibited (full list not published).
countries.export: For return to the EU: Tunisia is not EU-listed, so a rabies titer is needed (ideally done before leaving the EU).
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries – Direction Générale des Services Vétérinaires (DGSV); Tunisian Customs
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 30 days and no more than 12 months before entry. A multi-year vaccine given more than 12 months ago would not qualify, so revaccinate.
documents: Official veterinary health certificate attesting good health and no clinical signs of species-specific diseases
Valid rabies vaccination certificate

countries.name: Tonga
countries.summary: Tonga needs an import permit from MAFF, a signed owner/exporter declaration (identification, history, origin) and an international health certificate from the exporting country's official vet. On arrival, animals go straight into veterinary control at an approved quarantine ground or premises until released by a veterinary officer. Detailed conditions are set per permit; only Australian-origin permits (2019) are published, e.g. a cat exam within 24 hours of shipment.
countries.import_permit: Yes. Ministry of Agriculture and Food, Forests and Fisheries (info@mafff.gov.to).
countries.quarantine: On arrival, held under veterinary control at an approved quarantine ground or premises until released by a veterinary officer. Duration is per permit.
countries.private_aviation: No private-aircraft rule found. Post-arrival veterinary control and quarantine premises must be arranged.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture and Food, Forests and Fisheries (MAFFF), Quarantine Division
documents: MAFF import permit
Signed owner/exporter declaration (identification, history, origin)
International animal health certificate, signed and stamped by the exporting country's official vet (cats: exam within 24 hours of shipment, per the 2019 Australian-origin permit)

countries.name: Turkey
countries.summary: Max 2 pets per passenger. Each needs a microchip (before rabies vaccination), rabies vaccination, a rabies titer of at least 0.5 IU/ml (blood drawn 30+ days after vaccination, then a 90-day wait) and a health certificate issued within 2 days of travel. Several dog breeds are banned from entry.
countries.microchip: Required: ISO 11784/11785 microchip (or legible tattoo) applied before rabies vaccination; owner must supply reader if non-ISO
countries.rabies_titer: Required: at least 0.5 IU/ml at an accredited (EU-approved) lab, blood sampled at least 30 days after vaccination. Waiting period: 90 days counted from the date of the test RESULT (Istanbul Airport veterinary border post page); not required on later trips if the rabies vaccination is kept valid. No country exemption is stated on the official page (APHIS mentions a 21-day quarantine with on-arrival testing if the titer is missing).
countries.parasite_treatment: APHIS guidance (US origin): tick (ectoparasite) treatment and Echinococcus (tapeworm) treatment within 30 days before travel, signed by vet
countries.quarantine: None if compliant; 21 days possible if titer missing or for young unvaccinated pets
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 months for a first titer: microchip, rabies vaccine, titer blood draw 30+ days later, wait 90 days from the result, tick and tapeworm treatment within 30 days (APHIS, US origin), health certificate within 2 days of travel. Return to EU/GB: Türkiye is not EU-listed, so do the titer before leaving the EU. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~110 days if no previous titer (US or EU origin); ~7 days if a prior valid titer exists and rabies boosters never lapsed.
countries.restricted_breeds: Import banned (Law 5199 Art. 14(1)(l) and Ministry dangerous-animals circular): American Pit Bull Terrier, Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, American Staffordshire Terrier, American Bully, and their crosses (list per Ministry; may change)
countries.private_aviation: Pets must enter through Ministry-approved veterinary border posts (only Istanbul Airport is confirmed on the official page reviewed; APHIS links a list of approved ports). Not verified whether business-aviation terminals at e.g. Bodrum, Dalaman or Antalya have a veterinary border post on duty: confirm with the handler. Since 17 Jul 2026 Türkiye restricts dogs/cats from Texas and New Mexico (New World screwworm).
countries.export: Pet must be microchipped and registered in PETVET with a Turkish pet passport (foreign pets keep existing chip/passport). Rabies vaccine at ≥12 weeks, on/after chip date. FAVN titer (Etlik VKMAEM, ≥30 days after vaccination) if destination requires. Veterinary Health Certificate from the Provincial/District Directorate of Agriculture within 48 hours before departure. Protected native breeds (Kangal, Akbaş, Kars dog, Çatalburun, Zağar, Ankara cat, Van cat) need prior permission to leave; passports listing breed/colour only as 'mix' are rejected. Banned dangerous breeds may leave only if registered and destination accepts
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry of the Republic of Türkiye (General Directorate of Food and Control; Veterinary Border Control Posts)
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated or recombinant vaccine (not modified live), given on/after microchip date; booster after lapse counts as primary. Canada's CFIA notes Türkiye does not accept 3-year vaccine validity
Pets <3 months unvaccinated: admitted only under Ministry conditions (APHIS: 21-day home quarantine, or no-wildlife-contact declaration, or accompanied by vaccinated mother)
documents: Veterinary Health and Origin Certificate for cats/dogs/ferrets with passenger (one certificate per pet), issued by origin competent authority within 2 days before travel (US: APHIS endorsement ≤2 days before departure)
Pet passport or ID showing ownership
Original rabies titer report
Rabies vaccination certificate

countries.name: Trinidad and Tobago
countries.summary: Apply for an import permit from the Chief Veterinary Officer at least 1 month ahead. Pets need an ISO microchip before rabies vaccination, a FAVN/RFFIT drawn at least 1 month after vaccination (lab emails results directly), a Brucella test for intact dogs, parasite treatment, a USDA-endorsed certificate within 7 days of arrival, and 2 working days' notice.
countries.microchip: ISO 11784 / 11785 Annex A, implanted before rabies vaccination.
countries.rabies_titer: FAVN or RFFIT at an approved lab, at least 1 month after vaccination. The lab emails original results to aphmalmr@gmail.com. No post-test waiting period is stated, so confirm with the CVO.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatment before export (timing not stated).
countries.import_permit: Required, held before entry. Apply to the Office of the Chief Veterinary Officer, 80 Abercromby Street, Port of Spain (aphmalmr@gmail.com, 868-625-5997) at least 1 month before travel.
countries.quarantine: Not stated on the APHIS page. Confirm with the CVO whether home or facility quarantine applies.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2–3 months before travel: microchip, rabies, FAVN (1 month later, plus lab time), permit at least 1 month ahead, health certificate and endorsement within 7 days, 2 working days' notice.
countries.private_aviation: Notify the Veterinary Officer, Quarantine (868-693-2910, nadcaph2013@gmail.com) at least 2 working days before the scheduled arrival.
countries.export: Return to the US: Trinidad and Tobago is NOT on the CDC high-risk list, but it is on APHIS's screwworm-affected list, so dogs need a screwworm certificate.
countries.authority: Office of the Chief Veterinary Officer, Ministry of Agriculture, Land and Fisheries
vaccinations: Rabies: required (timing beyond the FAVN rule isn't stated).
documents: Import permit ('Application for a permit to import dogs and cats').
Health certificate by a USDA-accredited vet, endorsed by USDA within 7 days of arrival (digital VEHCS accepted), listing all countries of residence in the past 6 months.
Intact dogs: negative Brucella canis test.

countries.name: Tuvalu
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.authority: Department of Agriculture, Tuvalu

countries.name: Taiwan
countries.summary: An import permit is required, and post-entry quarantine space must be reserved at least 20 days before shipment. From non-rabies-free countries: microchip, rabies vaccination, a titer of at least 0.5 IU/ml (sample 90 days to 1 year before shipment), and 7 days of post-entry quarantine with a re-test. Rabies-free origins (e.g. Hawaii, Guam) have no titer, but require 180 days of residence.
countries.microchip: Required. Pet must be at least 90 days old. No microchip means refusal, return, euthanasia or quarantine.
countries.rabies_titer: Non-rabies-free origins: at least 0.5 IU/ml, sample taken 90 days to 1 year before shipment, at a WOAH reference lab or an APHIA-designated lab. Not required for recognised rabies-free origins (APHIS lists Hawaii and Guam).
countries.import_permit: Yes. Apply and reserve post-entry quarantine space at least 20 days before shipment.
countries.quarantine: Non-rabies-free origins: 7 days at a designated post-entry quarantine station, with a rabies antibody re-test (revaccinated if below 0.5 IU/ml). Rabies-free origins: reduced or no quarantine if compliant (confirm with APHIA).
countries.timeline: An already chipped and vaccinated pet needs at least 90 days: titer blood draw at a WOAH or APHIA-designated lab (US: KSU, DoD Texas, Auburn or Missouri FAVN) at least 90 days before shipment → import permit and quarantine booking at least 20 days before → Taiwan-form certificate, endorsed; arrival within 30 days of endorsement → 7-day quarantine. If shipped more than 1 year after the first titer test, a second test is needed.
countries.restricted_breeds: Pit Bull Terrier types (incl. American Pit Bull Terrier and American Staffordshire Terrier) banned from import and breeding since 1 March 2022 (reported by Taiwan News; confirm scope for mixes with APHIA).
countries.private_aviation: No private-aircraft-specific rule found. Transshipment through countries Taiwan does not recognise as rabies-free is not allowed for rabies-free-origin pets. The APHIA airport branch inspection and the quarantine booking apply as for any arrival.
countries.export: APHIA branch offices issue export animal health certificates based on the destination's requirements. Apply in advance.
countries.authority: Animal and Plant Health Inspection Agency (APHIA, formerly BAPHIQ), Ministry of Agriculture
vaccinations: Rabies (inactivated only; Merial Purevax accepted): given at 90 days of age or older, 30 days to 1 year before import.
documents: Import permit from APHIA (apply with the rabies vaccination certificate, the importer's ID or passport, and the titer report)
Official veterinary health certificate on Taiwan's required form, government-endorsed. Original required. A non-compliant certificate means refusal of entry or destruction of the animal.
Rabies-free origin: statement of 180 days' continuous residence (or since birth) and no third-country visit

US form (version 20250228): pregnant dogs and cats are allowed only if under 4 weeks pregnant. The pet must arrive within 30 days of the USDA endorsement. A second titer is needed if export is more than 1 year after a satisfactory test.

countries.name: Tanzania
countries.summary: Get an import permit by writing to the Director of Veterinary Services, then travel with an official health certificate and vaccination records (rabies given at least 1 month and no more than 3 years before entry). For US-origin pets (APHIS), the certificate must be USDA-endorsed and is valid 30 days.
countries.microchip: Not explicitly required. The APHIS US-origin certificate accepts either a microchip number or the animal's name; a microchip is still recommended.
countries.parasite_treatment: Embassy advice: deworm every 3 months (or worm tablets every 45 days). No pre-entry treatment window is stated in the official sources reviewed.
countries.import_permit: Required. Send a letter of request to the Director of Veterinary Services (Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries; the embassy page still uses the old ministry name) stating type/breed, age and port of entry, with vaccination certificates attached. APHIS directs US applicants to the Veterinary Investigation Centre (VIC). Embassy contacts: zoosanitary@mifugo.go.tz, epid1@mifugo.go.tz, +255 22 2862592.
countries.quarantine: No routine quarantine is stated. Animals are examined by a veterinarian at the port of entry and may be quarantined if needed.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6 weeks before travel: vaccinations at least 1 month before entry, then apply for the import permit, then a health certificate within 30 days of travel (US: USDA endorsement).
countries.private_aviation: No private-aviation-specific rules found. Animals may enter only through designated ports. Zanzibar may have separate rules; no official Zanzibar pet-import information was found.
countries.export: An export permit is required to take the pet back out of Tanzania (Tanzania Embassy).
countries.authority: Director of Veterinary Services, Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries (Veterinary Investigation Centre, Dar es Salaam)
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 1 month and no more than 3 years before entry (Tanzania Embassy); US-origin certificate: current at export, or for animals under 3 months the dam was vaccinated when they were born
Dogs: distemper, parvovirus, infectious hepatitis (adenovirus) and leptospirosis more than 1 month before export (APHIS US-origin certificate; the embassy lists DHLP as recommended)
Cats: panleukopenia, feline herpesvirus-1 and calicivirus (APHIS US-origin certificate)
documents: Import permit from the Director of Veterinary Services

Veterinary health certificate from the exporting country (US: Tanzania-specific APHIS certificate, NOV 2024 form, signed by an accredited vet and endorsed by USDA; can be endorsed digitally via VEHCS; valid 30 days after issue)
Vaccination certificates

UK model certificate 3129 (NFG revised 09/2024): exam within 10 days of export, valid 10 days; dogs fully vaccinated against parvovirus and distemper, cats against panleukopenia. The UK guidance notes rabies vaccination may be required on arrival.

countries.name: Ukraine
countries.summary: International certificate for non-commercial movement (up to 5 pets): ISO microchip, current rabies vaccination, and, per the US-origin model certificate, a rabies titer test. Ukrainian airspace is closed to civil flights, so entry is overland only.
countries.microchip: Required: ISO microchip, or tattoo applied before 3 July 2011
countries.rabies_titer: US origin (APHIS): required, ≥0.5 IU/ml at an approved lab, sample >3 months before export; remains valid if no vaccination lapse. Model certificate wording also references 'not more than 12 months' — confirm with Ukrainian authority. Whether a titer is required from EU/other countries could not be verified (Order No. 553 of 16.11.2018 governs)
countries.parasite_treatment: Model certificate includes an anti-Echinococcus treatment section; APHIS page does not list it as mandatory — confirm
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 months: microchip → rabies → titer → 3-month wait → certificate
countries.private_aviation: Ukrainian airspace closed to civil aviation since 24 Feb 2022 (martial law); no flights possible — reach via neighbouring country (e.g. Poland, Moldova) and cross by land at a border post with veterinary control
countries.authority: State Service of Ukraine on Food Safety and Consumer Protection (Derzhprodspozhyvsluzhba / DPSS)
vaccinations: Rabies: over 12 weeks must be current (US-licensed vaccine for US origin); ≥21 days after primary vaccination or after a booster given outside the validity period
Pets under 12 weeks: must NOT have been vaccinated; 12–16 weeks unvaccinated/<21 days: allowed only with no-wildlife-contact declaration or vaccinated mother
documents: International certificate for introduction into Ukraine of dogs, cats and ferrets for non-commercial movement (issued by accredited vet, endorsed by competent authority)
International pet passport with rabies vaccination
Original rabies titer lab report

countries.name: Uganda
countries.summary: Apply in writing to MAAIF's Commissioner for Animal Health for an import permit at least 7 days before arrival. Travel with an official English-language health certificate and vaccinations done at least 30 days before arrival; imported animals may be held in quarantine for 21-30 days.
countries.import_permit: Required. Written application to the Commissioner for Animal Health at least 7 days before import, stating country of origin, supplier, and animal type, breed, sex and quantity. The permit is then sent to the origin veterinary authority for inspection and certification. It may be refused if the disease risk is unmanageable.
countries.quarantine: MAAIF's general post-import procedure (which its dogs-and-cats page says applies) puts imported animals in quarantine or holding for 21-30 days, with release after tests. The page does not state this specifically for pets accompanying their owners, so confirm with MAAIF.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 5 weeks before travel: vaccinations at least 30 days before arrival, then the permit application at least 7 days before, then a health certificate within 10 days of shipment, then confirm arrival with the port veterinary officer at least 3 days before.
countries.private_aviation: No private-aviation-specific rules found. Confirm the arrival date with the port-of-entry veterinary official at least 3 days before arrival; pets must be crated individually with no contact with other animals.
countries.export: Apply to the Commissioner for Animal Health at least 15 days before export for a veterinary health certificate. Dogs need records of vaccination against rabies, distemper, parvovirus, infectious hepatitis, parainfluenza and tracheobronchitis. The destination country's import permit is also required.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Industry and Fisheries (MAAIF), Commissioner for Animal Health
vaccinations: Dogs: rabies, distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis, parvovirus, at least 30 days before arrival (Uganda Embassy Washington)
Cats: rabies and feline enteritis (panleukopenia), at least 30 days before arrival (Uganda Embassy Washington)

UK official guidance (NFG 3925, revised 12/2023): rabies, and for dogs distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis and parvovirus, or for cats feline enteritis, each at least 30 days and at most 12 months before export
documents: Import permit from the Commissioner for Animal Health (MAAIF)

Official veterinary health certificate from the origin country's veterinary authority, in English or with an English translation (the embassy says signed and stamped within 10 days of shipment, stating the pet is free from disease)
Movement permit from the veterinary authority of the area of origin (embassy)
Certificate or letter from the local veterinary authority that the area of origin is rabies-free (embassy)
Invoice or price list, packing list, and air waybill (MAAIF general procedure)
UK model certificate 3925: exam within 48 hours, valid 7 days, microchip number recorded, owner declaration of 6 months' residence

countries.name: United States
countries.summary: Dogs (CDC, since 1 Aug 2024) need a CDC Dog Import Form receipt, must be at least 6 months old and microchipped; dogs that were in a CDC high-risk dog-rabies country in the past 6 months have extra rabies paperwork and port rules. Cats have no federal USDA requirements, but state rules apply. Dogs from screwworm-affected regions also need a USDA screwworm certificate.
countries.microchip: Dogs: required, readable by a universal scanner. For the high-risk-country routes it must be implanted before the rabies vaccine, or the vaccine is invalid. Cats: no federal requirement.
countries.rabies_titer: Only for foreign-vaccinated dogs from high-risk countries: serology at a CDC-approved lab, drawn at least 30 days after the first valid vaccine and at least 28 days before entry. It stays valid as long as vaccination doesn't lapse. Without a valid titer, the dog does a 28-day quarantine at a CDC-registered animal care facility.
countries.import_permit: None for personal pets. Dogs imported for resale or adoption have additional USDA APHIS Animal Care permit and health requirements.
countries.quarantine: None for compliant dogs. Foreign-vaccinated high-risk-country dogs without a valid titer: 28 days at a CDC-registered facility. HAWAII (state rule): up to 120 days' quarantine unless the 5-Day-Or-Less program is met: 2 rabies vaccinations (latest at least 30 days before arrival), a passing FAVN with arrival at least 30 days after the test, tick treatment, and documents received at least 10 days before arrival. Hawaii certificates also need a New World screwworm statement.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 week before travel for a dog from a low-risk country (CDC form, microchip). For a high-risk country, plan at least 2 months: microchip, rabies vaccine at 12 weeks or older, titer at least 30 days later, facility reservation at least 30 days before travel. Hawaii direct release: plan 3–4+ months, because FAVN results can take 1–2 months. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~7 days for a dog from the EU/UK or another low-risk country (CDC Dog Import Form, age 6+ months, microchip; cats: no federal paperwork). Dogs vaccinated abroad that were in a CDC high-risk country (e.g. UAE) need a CDC-approved titer at least 28 days before entry plus a facility reservation: plan 2+ months. Hawaii: 3-4+ months.
countries.private_aviation: CDC rules apply equally to private and charter flights; the arrival airport must match the CDC Dog Import Form. Dogs from low-risk countries and US-vaccinated dogs returning from high-risk countries may use any airport, land border or seaport. FOREIGN-VACCINATED dogs that were in a CDC high-risk country in the past 6 months (list of 15 Apr 2026 includes the UAE, Qatar, Türkiye, Israel, Morocco, Thailand and South Africa; not Saudi Arabia, Mexico, Bahamas, Japan, Singapore or Hong Kong) may enter ONLY through an airport with a CDC-registered animal care facility: ATL, DFW, LAX, MIA, JFK (not Teterboro, Newark or LaGuardia), PHL, SEA, IAD (CDC list updated 1 Sep 2026). Some facilities (SEA, LAX) work cargo-only or prefer cargo. This rules out typical FBO airports such as Teterboro, Van Nuys or Opa-locka for Dubai-vaccinated dogs. Hawaii: HNL direct airport release 8:30 am-4:30 pm daily; neighbor-island arrivals need a permit 30 days ahead; HDOA does not address private aircraft, so contact the Animal Quarantine Station.
countries.export: Leaving the US: a USDA-accredited vet issues the destination-specific health certificate, preferably in VEHCS, and APHIS endorses it. Most endorsements are digital, but some destinations still require an original ink signature and embossing; a few (e.g. Bermuda, Belize, El Salvador, Honduras) need no APHIS endorsement. Before taking a dog to a CDC high-risk country, get the USDA-endorsed Certification of U.S.-issued Rabies Vaccination; otherwise re-entry requires the foreign-vaccinated route.
countries.authority: CDC Division of Global Migration Health (dogs); USDA APHIS Veterinary Services; state veterinarians (Hawaii Department of Agriculture & Biosecurity, Animal Quarantine Station)
vaccinations: Dogs only in dog-rabies-free/low-risk countries in the past 6 months: no federal rabies certificate required (CDC recommends vaccination; states and airlines may require it).

Dogs in a CDC high-risk country in the past 6 months: valid rabies vaccination given at 12 weeks (84 days) of age or older, after the microchip. US-vaccinated dogs: a first vaccine must be at least 28 days old when the CDC certification form is completed.
Cats: no federal USDA/APHIS requirement. Many states require rabies vaccination.
documents: CDC Dog Import Form receipt for every dog. Free, online, one per dog. Low-risk route: receipt valid 6 months. High-risk routes: single entry on the listed date and port.

US-vaccinated dogs returning from a high-risk country: Certification of U.S.-issued Rabies Vaccination, completed in USDA's system by a USDA-accredited vet and endorsed by USDA BEFORE the dog leaves the US.

Foreign-vaccinated dogs from a high-risk country: Certification of Foreign Rabies Vaccination and Microchip, endorsed by an official government vet and completed no more than 30 days before travel; titer report; reservation at a CDC-registered animal care facility (exam and US revaccination on arrival).

Dogs from screwworm (NWS)-affected regions, including US dogs returning from Mexico: certificate signed by a full-time official government vet of the region (Mexico: a SENASICA-authorized vet may sign) stating the dog was inspected within 5 days of shipment and is free of screwworm. APHIS's affected list includes most of Central America, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Haiti, Jamaica, Trinidad and Tobago, Aruba and the UAE; Mexico is under a separate temporary restriction.
Dogs from FMD-affected countries: no document, but coat and bedding must be free of excess dirt or straw, bathe on arrival, and keep away from livestock for 5 days.

countries.name: Uruguay
countries.summary: Dogs and cats need a CVI (Mercosur model) or validated official passport from the origin country's veterinary authority; dogs additionally need an ISO microchip, praziquantel deworming and (from non-free countries) a negative leishmaniasis test within 60 days. No MGAP entry authorization if travelling with the pet; no fee.
countries.microchip: Dogs: mandatory ISO 11784/11785 microchip (MGAP Res. 273/2018), with implantation or reading certificate. Cats: not listed.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external deworming within 15 days before CVI issue/passport endorsement (date and product recorded); for dogs the internal product must contain praziquantel.
countries.import_permit: Not required for dogs and cats travelling with owner. Pets arriving as cargo at Carrasco: notify aeropuertoic@mgap.gub.uy at least 72 working hours before arrival with scanned documents.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4–6 weeks before travel: microchip (dogs) → rabies (≥21 days if first) → leishmaniasis test (dogs, within 60 days) → deworming within 15 days of CVI (praziquantel for dogs) → vet exam within 10 days of CVI → official CVI → MGAP check at entry.
countries.private_aviation: No prior MGAP authorization for accompanied pets; documents checked at the border point. For Carrasco cargo arrivals, 72 working hours notice to MGAP airport office.
countries.export: Leaving Uruguay: MGAP issues the CVI. Mercosur destinations: digital only via VUCE (since 04/01/2025) through an accredited private vet. Other destinations: accredited vet health certificate within 10 days of travel, dog microchip + INBA registration, pre-filled CVI, payment (UYU 666 per page), at an MGAP Sanidad Animal office by appointment (Montevideo, Carrasco cargo terminal). Mercosur CVI valid 60 days, multiple trips.
countries.authority: MGAP (Ministerio de Ganadería, Agricultura y Pesca) – Dirección General de Servicios Ganaderos
vaccinations: Rabies: current, origin-approved vaccine; CVI states date, type, serial, brand; first vaccination at least 21 days before entry.
Under 3 months: age and no exposure to urban rabies in the 90 days before shipment certified.
Animals from WOAH rabies-free countries may enter unvaccinated if certified.
documents: CVI from origin official authority (Mercosur model, valid 60 days) or official passport validated by the official authority (unvalidated passports refused)
Clinical exam by registered vet within 10 days before CVI issue

Dogs (over 90 days) from countries not WOAH-free of leishmaniasis: negative test (IFAT, ELISA, direct agglutination or molecular) within 60 days before entry; dogs diagnosed/under treatment not admitted

countries.name: Uzbekistan
countries.summary: For US origin: a microchip, a current rabies vaccination, and a veterinary health certificate issued by an accredited vet and APHIS-endorsed (valid 30 days after issuance). Rules for other origins were not verified.
countries.microchip: Required (microchip number verified on certificate)
countries.timeline: Plan at least 1 month: microchip → rabies vaccination (current) → certificate within 30 days of arrival
countries.authority: Committee for Veterinary and Livestock Development of the Republic of Uzbekistan
vaccinations: Rabies: current at time of export (vaccine name, batch and validity recorded)
documents: Veterinary Health Certificate for Export of Dogs and Cats to Uzbekistan (US: accredited vet + APHIS endorsement; valid 30 days after issuance)

countries.name: Vatican City
countries.summary: Vatican City is an EU Annex I listed territory (pets from it enter the EU without titer test or point-of-entry check). No dedicated official import page was found; in practice pets arrive via Italy (Rome), so that country's EU entry rules apply (microchip, rabies vaccination, EU pet passport or EU health certificate; titer test from unlisted countries).
countries.microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid. (as required by the EU country of arrival)
countries.rabies_titer: Per EU rules of the arrival country: required only from unlisted third countries.
countries.parasite_treatment: None identified (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland).
countries.quarantine: None identified if EU requirements are met.
countries.timeline: As for the EU arrival country: at least 4 weeks from EU/listed origin; 4+ months from unlisted origin.
countries.restricted_breeds: Not verified.
countries.private_aviation: No airport in Vatican City. Private jets land in Rome: Fiumicino and Ciampino are both on Italy's September 2026 list of pet points of entry for third-country arrivals.
countries.export: Leaving: EU treats this territory as Annex I listed (pet passport/certificate, no titer, no point-of-entry requirement). Local export procedure not verified.
countries.authority: Governorate of Vatican City State; Italian Ministry of Health at entry - not verified
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
documents: EU pet passport (from EU) or EU animal health certificate + non-commercial declaration (from third countries), as required by the EU arrival country.

countries.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
countries.summary: An import permit is required, issued only after a protective FAVN result reaches the veterinary office. Pets need a microchip before rabies vaccination, US residence for 6 months, vaccines, a heartworm test and parasite treatment within 7 days, an APHIS-endorsed certificate (original ink), and 48 hours' notice.
countries.microchip: ISO microchip implanted before rabies vaccination.
countries.rabies_titer: FAVN at an approved lab (e.g. Kansas State), blood drawn at least 3 weeks after rabies vaccination, result above 0.5 IU/ml. Results must reach the office before the permit is issued; no further waiting period is stated.
countries.parasite_treatment: External and internal (broad-spectrum anthelmintic) treatment within 7 days before export. Dogs: negative heartworm test within 7 days before export.
countries.import_permit: Required. Apply to the SVG veterinary authorities; the permit is issued only after FAVN results are received and confirmed.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6–8 weeks before travel: microchip, rabies, FAVN at least 3 weeks later, results to SVG, then the permit; vaccines, heartworm test and parasite treatment within 7 days; APHIS endorsement; 48 hours' notice.
countries.private_aviation: Give 48 hours' notice of arrival (784-456-1111 ext 326, 784-457-2452 or 784-493-1749). Inspection fee EC$55 / US$20 per animal on arrival; landing after 4:00 pm Mon–Fri, on weekends or on public holidays carries separate (overtime) fees.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture, St. Vincent and the Grenadines – Veterinary Services
vaccinations: Rabies: inactivated adjuvanted vaccine given at 12 weeks or older, after the microchip.
Dogs: distemper, parvovirus, leptospirosis, hepatitis and parainfluenza at least 7 days before export.
Cats: rhinotracheitis, panleukopenia, FeLV, calicivirus and Chlamydophila.
documents: Import permit (exporter's responsibility).
US veterinary health certificate for SVG, endorsed by APHIS (original ink signature and embossing).
Animal born in or resident in the US for the previous 6 months.

countries.name: Venezuela
countries.summary: Dogs and cats need an official international veterinary certificate from the origin country with rabies and core vaccinations and deworming; INSAI is the competent authority. No official Venezuelan source could be verified — details below come from SENASA Argentina's destination page; confirm with INSAI.
countries.microchip: Not mentioned in available official sources.
countries.parasite_treatment: Internal and external deworming within 3 months before entry (per SENASA Argentina destination page).
countries.import_permit: Unclear — an INSAI import permit may be required; not verifiable from official sources.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 6 weeks before travel: confirm INSAI requirements → vaccinations → deworming → health certificate and official CVI → INSAI inspection on arrival.
countries.export: No reliable official information found — INSAI issues zoosanitary certificates for departure; check with Elysium Jet operations.
countries.authority: INSAI (Instituto Nacional de Salud Agrícola Integral)
vaccinations: Rabies: current, valid 1 year from application (under 3 months may enter unvaccinated if age certified) — per SENASA Argentina destination page.
Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, coronavirus, leptospirosis, parainfluenza (valid 1 year).
Cats: panleukopenia, calicivirus, rhinotracheitis (valid 1 year).
documents: Official CVI from origin authority (SENASA Argentina states validity 30 calendar days from issue to entry check)
Vet health certificate within 30 days before entry
Vaccination certificates; copy of traveller's ID/passport

countries.name: British Virgin Islands
countries.summary: Rabies-free. From rabies-endemic countries (including the US), pets need a BVI import permit, 2 rabies vaccinations, a FAVN titer at least 1 month after the second dose, and an APHIS-endorsed health certificate obtained BEFORE applying for the permit.
countries.microchip: Permanent ID: microchip or tattoo.
countries.rabies_titer: FAVN at least 1 month after the second or later rabies vaccine, more than 0.5 IU/ml, before departure. Valid 12 months for re-entry.
countries.parasite_treatment: Treated against internal and external parasites (no timing stated).
countries.import_permit: Required. Apply to the Veterinary Division, Department of Agriculture (Paraquita Bay, Tortola) with the endorsed certificate, rabies certificates and FAVN results. Allow at least 48 hours (2 working days) for processing.
countries.quarantine: No routine quarantine is stated. Non-compliant animals may be held in a facility, deported or euthanized.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 7–8 months before travel for an unvaccinated pet (2 rabies doses 6 months apart, then FAVN); otherwise about 6 weeks: FAVN, then health certificate and APHIS endorsement, then the permit, then 24 hours' notice.
countries.private_aviation: Give the Veterinary Division at least 24 hours' notice of the confirmed arrival date, time, aircraft and port of entry. Agricultural officers handle animal clearance at Terrance B. Lettsome Airport (EIS). Keep the pet in its carrier until entry is granted.
countries.authority: BVI Department of Agriculture – Veterinary Division
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 2 inactivated vaccines, the first at 3 months of age or older and the next at least 6 months later (1- and 3-year vaccines accepted).
Dogs: parvovirus, distemper, hepatitis/adenovirus, parainfluenza, leptospirosis and Lyme disease.
Cats: calicivirus, panleukopenia, rhinotracheitis and FeLV.
documents: Health certificate by an accredited vet, endorsed by APHIS (original ink endorsement), with lab results and rabies certificates attached.
BVI import permit (US$10 per animal).
Residence: in the US and/or BVI for at least 6 months before import; area of origin not under rabies quarantine.

countries.name: US Virgin Islands
countries.summary: From the US or Puerto Rico: no permit (interstate), but a health certificate by an accredited vet within 10 days of arrival, current rabies vaccination, and an emailed certificate at least 1 business day before arrival are needed. From abroad: USVI rules plus federal CDC/USDA rules.
countries.rabies_titer: Optional alternative: adequate FAVN titer within 12 months of travel.
countries.import_permit: Not required from the US or Puerto Rico (interstate). For foreign origins, contact USVI Veterinary Services.
countries.quarantine: Non-compliant animals are confiscated and quarantined for at least 10 days at the owner's expense.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2 weeks before travel: rabies (10 days if first dose), health certificate within 10 days, email at least 1 business day before arrival.
countries.private_aviation: Arrivals by cruise ship or private boat need a separate inquiry. Foreign-vaccinated dogs from CDC high-risk countries cannot enter via US territories.
countries.authority: USVI Department of Agriculture – Veterinary Services
vaccinations: Rabies: currently vaccinated (or an adequate FAVN titer within 12 months of travel). First-time vaccination must be at least 10 days before arrival; boosters have no wait. 3-year vaccines are accepted if labelled. Animals too young for rabies vaccination are not admitted.
Recommended (not required): leptospirosis vaccine for dogs; flea, tick and heartworm prevention.
documents: Health certificate (APHIS 7001, official state CVI or NASAHO-approved eCVI) with the vet's accreditation number, issued within 10 days of arrival, including rabies date, product and lot. Business-specific certificates are not accepted.
Email the certificate to veterinaryservices@doa.vi.gov at least 1 business day before arrival.

countries.name: Vietnam
countries.summary: Vietnam needs a health certificate from the exporting country (for US pets: a USDA-endorsed, Vietnam-specific certificate stating current rabies vaccination, valid 30 days). Up to 2 pets travelling with their owner are cleared directly by the airport animal quarantine office on arrival, with no prior permit. 3 or more need prior quarantine registration with the Department of Livestock Production and Animal Health. No titer and no routine quarantine.
countries.microchip: Microchip number required on the USDA Vietnam certificate, and the vet verifies the chip. Vietnamese law sets no separate chip standard; ISO 11784/11785 is advised.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required (no titer on the USDA Vietnam certificate or in Circular 25/2016).
countries.parasite_treatment: None specified.
countries.import_permit: Not needed for up to 2 animals carried by a person for pet/household use, travel or transit: register directly with the border-gate animal quarantine office (Circular 25/2016/TT-BNNPTNT, Art. 10.1). For more than 2 animals, file prior quarantine registration with the Department of Livestock Production and Animal Health (Cục Chăn nuôi và Thú y) via the National Single Window, then declare at the border (Art. 8 and 10.3).
countries.quarantine: No fixed quarantine for compliant pets: clinical inspection at the border only. Animals with a dangerous infectious disease are destroyed near the border gate. An invalid export certificate means the pet is held and dealt with under the regulations (Art. 10.2).
countries.timeline: An already chipped and vaccinated pet needs about 1 week: accredited-vet exam and Vietnam certificate → USDA (or EU official) endorsement → fly within 30 days of issue. For 3 or more animals, add time for Department registration.
countries.restricted_breeds: No breed ban found in the national quarantine rules.
countries.private_aviation: No private-aircraft rule found. The 2-animal 'carried by a person' route matches owner-accompanied pets on a private jet. Arrange in advance for the airport animal quarantine office (regional Sub-Department of Livestock Production and Animal Health) to inspect at the GA/FBO arrival point.
countries.authority: Department of Livestock Production and Animal Health (Cục Chăn nuôi và Thú y, formerly Department of Animal Health), Ministry of Agriculture and Environment. Border work is done by regional sub-departments / border-gate animal quarantine offices.
vaccinations: Rabies: current at time of export (USDA Vietnam certificate, Sept 2025). Vaccine name, batch and validity end date must be listed. No minimum wait is stated on the certificate.
At the border, Vietnamese quarantine officers vaccinate animals not already vaccinated against dangerous infectious diseases (Circular 25/2016, Art. 10).
documents: Health/quarantine certificate issued by the exporting country. For the USA: the Vietnam-specific USDA certificate (Sept 2025 version), signed by an accredited vet and USDA-endorsed (digital endorsement accepted). It covers the microchip check, a clinical exam on the day of issue, origin outside rabies-quarantined areas, and current rabies vaccination. Valid 30 days from issue to departure.
On arrival: import quarantine registration at the border-gate animal quarantine office. The office checks the certificate and examines the pet, then issues a Vietnamese import quarantine certificate.

countries.name: Vanuatu
countries.summary: Biosecurity Vanuatu import permit required, using the health certificate attached to the permit (new conditions since 30 May 2024). Per Australian MICoR guidance, dogs must arrive by air as manifested cargo. Transit or offloading is allowed only in Australia, New Zealand or New Caledonia, and flight details must reach the Principal Veterinary Officer at least 1 working day before. Pregnant or nursing females and pups under 16 weeks are not eligible. Direct private-jet arrival from the US or EU is not compatible with these rules.
countries.import_permit: Yes. Biosecurity Vanuatu (biosecurity@vanuatu.gov.vu, +678 33580 / 23519). The permit carries the applicable conditions and certificate.
countries.quarantine: On arrival a Veterinary Officer checks documents and inspects or treats the dog. The dog stays in the airport quarantine area until a Permit to Land is issued. Non-compliant dogs may be seized, destroyed or re-exported at the owner's cost.
countries.timeline: Not determinable for US/EU origin without the permit conditions. Origin and transit are restricted to Australia, NZ or New Caledonia routing.
countries.private_aviation: Dogs must travel as manifested air cargo, transiting or offloading only in Australia, NZ or New Caledonia, in line with IATA live animal rules. Yacht arrivals have a separate schedule (4Y).
countries.authority: Biosecurity Vanuatu
documents: Biosecurity Vanuatu import permit
Health certificate attached to the permit (new format since 30 May 2024)
Flight details to the Principal Veterinary Officer at least 1 working day before embarkation

countries.name: Wallis and Futuna
countries.summary: Dogs and cats need a Wallis import permit from BIVAP (agricultural and veterinary inspection service). Imports come via New Caledonia on a DAVAR export certificate (E.CD.WF.10/17). Pets from metropolitan France must first do quarantine in New Caledonia. Category 1 and 2 dogs (Pit Bull, Mastiff, Tosa, American Staffordshire, Rottweiler types) are banned from transport. US/EU pets cannot fly direct to Wallis.
countries.microchip: Microchip or tattoo matching the import permit (DAVAR certificate).
countries.parasite_treatment: Two internal treatments (nematodes and cestodes, incl. Echinococcus for dogs) and two external treatments (long-acting, fleas and ticks), at least 15 days apart: the first within 30 days, the second within 3 days of departure.
countries.import_permit: Yes. BIVAP Wallis (bivap@agripeche.wf).
countries.quarantine: Pets from metropolitan France must complete quarantine in New Caledonia before entry. Other origins: not published.
countries.restricted_breeds: Category 1 and 2 dogs (Pit Bull, Mastiff, Tosa, American Staffordshire, Rottweiler and similar) are banned from transport.
countries.private_aviation: Entry goes through New Caledonia (DAVAR certificate, NC quarantine for pets from metropolitan France). A direct private flight with a pet from outside New Caledonia is not supported by the published procedure.
countries.export: New Caledonia lists Wallis and Futuna as a rabies-free Pacific origin with its own dog/cat health certificate, so pets can move from Wallis and Futuna to New Caledonia under DAVAR conditions.
countries.authority: BIVAP – Bureau d'inspection vétérinaire, alimentaire et phytosanitaire (Service territorial des affaires rurales et de la pêche, Wallis and Futuna)
vaccinations: Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, kennel cough (parainfluenza), leptospirosis. Cats: coryza, panleukopenia. Booster more than 14 days and less than 12 months before export (DAVAR certificate).
documents: BIVAP import permit (owner application form, version 06/09/2019)
DAVAR health certificate E.CD.WF.10/17: exam within 3 days of departure, countersigned by an official vet and emailed to BIVAP Wallis (bivap@agripeche.wf) before export

countries.name: Samoa
countries.summary: Samoa import permit (Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries) required, and dogs are subject to quarantine inspection on arrival. Conditions are set per permit and published only for Australian-origin dogs (Feb 2021 permit): tapeworm treatment (praziquantel) within 21 days, roundworm and long-acting tick/flea/lice treatment within 4 days, current distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis and parvovirus vaccination, and a government vet certificate within 4 days of departure. Conditions for US/EU origin are not published.
countries.parasite_treatment: Dogs (Australia-origin permit): praziquantel within 21 days before transport; roundworm treatment (e.g. pyrantel pamoate) and long-acting topical tick/flea/lice treatment within 4 days before transport.
countries.import_permit: Yes. Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries (maf.info@maf.gov.ws; Biosecurity: biosecurity.info@maf.gov.ws, +685 22561/22562).
countries.quarantine: Quarantine inspection on arrival. The importing country may set further pre- and post-arrival quarantine.
countries.private_aviation: No private-aircraft rule found. The MAF permit sets the conditions, and US/EU-origin eligibility is unconfirmed.
countries.authority: Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries (MAF), Samoa Quarantine Service (biosecurity.info@maf.gov.ws)
vaccinations: Dogs (Australia-origin permit): current distemper, infectious canine hepatitis, leptospirosis and parvovirus.
documents: Samoa import permit
International Animal Sanitary Certificate signed and stamped by a Government Veterinarian within 4 days of departure, recording treatments, doses and dates

countries.name: Kosovo
countries.summary: Kosovo's Administrative Instruction 02/2009 on non-commercial movement of pets (still published by the Food and Veterinary Agency) mirrors the old EU pet scheme. Pets from EU/listed countries, including the USA, need an ISO microchip, valid rabies vaccination and a passport or veterinary certificate. Pets from unlisted countries also need a rabies titer (≥0.5 IU/ml, ≥30 days after vaccination and 3 months before entry) and echinococcus treatment. IATA Timatic adds a ≥30-day wait after rabies vaccination and echinococcus treatment for dogs and cats.
countries.microchip: Required: electronic identification (ISO 11784 / Annex A ISO 11785). Tattoos were accepted only during the 4-year transitional period after 2009. If the chip is not ISO-compliant, the owner must provide a reader.
countries.rabies_titer: Not required from EU/listed countries (Annex II Parts A–C, which include the USA, Canada, UAE, Bahrain, Japan, Russia, Belarus, Australia, etc.). Required from unlisted countries: ≥0.5 IU/ml, sample ≥30 days after vaccination and ≥3 months before entry (waived on re-entry if the titer was done before leaving).
countries.parasite_treatment: Echinococcus treatment for dogs and cats (praziquantel or epsiprantel), documented in the certificate/passport. Under AI 02/2009 it applies to animals from unlisted countries, '30 days before the import'. IATA Timatic lists it for all pet entries; treat and document to be safe.
countries.import_permit: Not mentioned for non-commercial pets.
countries.quarantine: Not mentioned for compliant pets.
countries.timeline: EU/listed origin (incl. USA): microchip → rabies vaccination ≥30 days before travel → vet certificate/passport (+ echinococcus treatment, documented). Unlisted origin: add titer ≥30 days after vaccination, then wait 3 months.
countries.private_aviation: IATA Timatic gives no airport restriction. Pristina International Airport is the international entry point.
countries.authority: Kosovo Food and Veterinary Agency (AUV/AUVK), Fushë Kosovë/Prishtinë, infoauv@rks-gov.net
vaccinations: Rabies: valid vaccination per manufacturer's recommendations, certified in a passport/veterinary certificate. IATA Timatic: at least 30 days before departure. Unvaccinated pets under 3 months only under specific conditions (passport, raised with mother, no wild-animal contact).
documents: Pet passport or veterinary certificate issued by an authorised veterinarian, certifying identification and valid rabies vaccination (plus titer and echinococcus treatment where applicable)

countries.name: Yemen
countries.summary: No reliable official information found — check with Elysium Jet operations before booking.
countries.authority: Unknown (Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation – veterinary services)

countries.name: Mayotte
countries.summary: Mayotte is a French department in the EU, and the EU non-commercial pet rules apply (Reg. (EU) 576/2013), as confirmed by the DAAF de Mayotte information sheet. From mainland France or the DOMs, a microchip and EU pet passport are enough. From another EU state, the pet also needs a valid rabies vaccination. From third countries (including the USA), the pet needs a microchip, valid rabies vaccination and an EU health certificate signed by an official vet of the origin country, plus a rabies titer unless the country is on the exempt list (the USA is exempt). Category 1 'attack' dogs are banned, and category 2 dogs need prefectoral authorisation.
countries.microchip: Required for all origins. Tattoos are accepted only if clearly legible and applied before 3 Jul 2011 (DAAF Mayotte).
countries.rabies_titer: Required only from third countries not on the exempt list (I-CAD/EU list; the USA, UK and other EU-listed countries are exempt). Sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after vaccination and at least 3 months before travel, tested at an approved lab (EU threshold ≥0.5 IU/ml). Valid for life while vaccination is kept current.
countries.import_permit: Not required for ordinary dogs and cats. A DAAF prior-introduction authorisation form (alimentation.daaf976@agriculture.gouv.fr) is required for category 2 dogs and for exotic pets (NAC).
countries.quarantine: None for compliant animals. Non-compliant animals may be refused, returned or isolated at the owner's expense.
countries.timeline: EU/France origin: no lead time beyond a valid passport and vaccination. USA (exempt from titer): EU health certificate issued by an accredited vet and endorsed by USDA APHIS within 10 days before arrival. Non-exempt third countries: plan at least 4 months (vaccination → titer at 30+ days → wait 3 months → certificate).
countries.restricted_breeds: Category 1 dogs (non-pedigree American Staffordshire terrier/'pit-bull', Mastiff/'boerbull' and Tosa types) may not be introduced, and air transport of them is prohibited. Category 2 dogs (pedigree American Staffordshire terrier and Tosa; Rottweiler and Rottweiler types) are allowed only if sterilised and with prefectoral authorisation under Arrêté 2014-6571.
countries.private_aviation: Pets from third countries must be checked at an EU travellers' point of entry. Confirm with DAAF Mayotte / customs that Dzaoudzi-Pamandzi can carry out the check for a private flight. Category 1 dogs cannot be carried by air.
countries.authority: DAAF de Mayotte (Service Alimentation), French Ministry of Agriculture; alimentation.daaf976@agriculture.gouv.fr
vaccinations: Rabies: required from EU states and third countries. Given at 12 weeks of age or older and kept valid (primary dose and boosters). Primary vaccination valid from 21 days (EU rule). Unvaccinated dogs and cats under 3 months cannot enter, except by DAAF derogation.
documents: From mainland France/DOM: EU pet passport
From another EU state (or New Caledonia, French Polynesia, Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, Wallis-et-Futuna): EU pet passport with valid rabies vaccination
From third countries: EU-model health certificate issued and signed by an official vet of the origin country (valid 10 days to the entry check), plus the owner's non-commercial declaration
Titer lab report (non-exempt third countries only)

Category 2 dogs: prefectoral authorisation (Arrêté préfectoral 2014-6571), DAAF prior-introduction form (Annex 1), identification, valid rabies certificate, sterilisation certificate, liability insurance, owner's aptitude certificate and behavioural assessment
Maximum 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per non-commercial movement

countries.name: South Africa
countries.summary: A veterinary import permit from the Department of Agriculture (Food Import & Export Standards / Animal Health) is required for every dog and cat. The permit, which lists the exact conditions and the authorised port of entry, must be in place before departure. Pets must arrive as manifested cargo at an airport with state veterinary inspection (Johannesburg O.R. Tambo, Cape Town, Durban King Shaka). Dogs need a series of pre-import blood tests.
countries.microchip: Mandatory for all dogs and cats; must be readable by ISO 11784/11785 scanners (tattoos not accepted). The microchip number must appear on all lab reports.
countries.rabies_titer: Not on the US-origin dog certificate (APHIS guidance). Requirements for other origins are set on the permit; confirm with the Permit Office.
countries.parasite_treatment: Dogs (US-origin certificate): heartworm (D. immitis) preventive given at least once after the negative heartworm test and before certificate issue. Effective acaricide plus insect repellent within 30 days before departure, recorded on the certificate.
countries.import_permit: Required for ALL dogs and cats. Apply at least 4 weeks before arrival (separate forms: domestic cats; dogs not subject to quarantine; dogs subject to quarantine). Proof of payment is required. Issued 3-5 working days after approval. Valid for a limited period (stated on the permit) and for one consignment only. Fees are set in the annual tariff list (2026/27 list published by DoA).
countries.quarantine: Cats are generally not quarantined. Dogs from some origins are subject to quarantine at state stations (Kempton Park/Johannesburg or Cape Town), which must be booked in advance using the 'subject to quarantine' application. APHIS lists no quarantine for US-origin dogs. Non-compliant dogs face a high risk of return or euthanasia: DoA has told APHIS they will no longer be placed in quarantine.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 8 weeks (more for dogs): apply for the permit 4+ weeks ahead → receive permit and model certificate → dog blood tests within 30 days of arrival (surra samples go abroad) → parasite treatments → vet exam, certificate and government endorsement within 10 days of travel → notify the port of entry. LEAD TIME (lead_days): ~45 days from the USA: permit at least 4 weeks ahead, dog blood tests within 30 days of arrival (surra samples sent to Belgium or Japan), certificate and APHIS endorsement within 10 days.
countries.private_aviation: High impact. DoA information document (06-2022) and SAA: dogs and cats must be registered as manifested cargo, not excess baggage. No state veterinarians at passenger terminals, so pets clear only via the cargo terminal at O.R. Tambo, Cape Town or King Shaka (Durban, depending on the permit). On a private jet, the pet must be on the cargo manifest/air waybill, the aircraft should land at the airport named on the permit, and inspection must be arranged with the port's state vet/cargo handler. Do not plan an arrival at Lanseria or other private/regional airports unless DoA confirms it in writing on the permit.
countries.export: Exports follow the destination country's rules. South African state veterinarians endorse export health certificates. Movement to Namibia uses an inter-territorial movement permit from a local state vet.
countries.authority: Department of Agriculture (formerly DALRRD/DAFF), Directorate Animal Health – Import Export Policy Unit / Food Import & Export Standards (VetPermits@daff.gov.za)
vaccinations: Rabies (US-origin, per APHIS guidance Sept 2024): vaccinated within 12 months before export, and more than 30 days before export for a primary vaccination. The 30-day wait does not apply if the booster was given before the previous vaccination expired.
Other origins: as stated on the import permit / South African model health certificate.
documents: Original South African veterinary import permit (DoA, VetPermits@daff.gov.za)

Original veterinary health certificate on the South African model (dogs: IMP. DOG. GEN 05/22 CG), issued and endorsed by the exporting country's veterinary authority within 10 days of travel (US: USDA APHIS ink-signed and embossed)
Rabies vaccination certificate (original or copy)

Dogs: English lab reports, all within 30 days of import and all negative: Brucella canis, Trypanosoma evansi (CATT plus Giemsa smear at a WOAH reference laboratory), Babesia gibsoni (two tests), Dirofilaria immitis (microfilarial filtration only), Leishmania
Indemnity declaration where specified (e.g. dogs entering quarantine)
sources: https://old.dalrrd.gov.za/vetweb/ImportExport/Information document for import of dogs and cats to RSA 06-2022.pdf

countries.name: Zambia
countries.summary: A veterinary import permit from the Department of Veterinary Services, Lusaka, is required and must accompany the pet; its conditions depend on origin. UK official guidance (revised Dec 2023) adds: rabies vaccination no more than 12 months before export, official vet exam within 48 hours, and a certificate valid 7 days. Unvaccinated pets must be vaccinated at a Government Veterinary Station on arrival.
countries.microchip: Not stated in official sources (the UK certificate uses identification marks). Microchip recommended.
countries.parasite_treatment: Exam within 48 hours before export must find the pet free of external parasites including ticks (UK EHC 3928).
countries.import_permit: Required. Issued by the Department of Veterinary Services HQ, Mulungushi House, P.O. Box 50060, Lusaka (UK guidance uses the older name 'Department of Veterinary and Tsetse Control Services'). Must be attached to the consignment and travel with the animal. Conditions vary by species, origin and purpose. A contact person in Lusaka can apply.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 4 weeks: apply for the import permit (no official processing time published) → send it to your vet and the origin veterinary authority → vet exam within 48 hours of export and government endorsement → notify the nearest Zambian Veterinary Officer of the arrival.
countries.private_aviation: No private-aviation-specific rules found. The importer must inform the nearest Veterinary Officer of the arrival so the animal can be inspected.
countries.authority: Department of Veterinary Services, Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock (the embassy page uses an older department name)
vaccinations: Rabies: no more than 12 months before export (UK EHC 3928). If not vaccinated before export, the pet must be presented to the nearest Government Veterinary Station in Zambia for vaccination on arrival.
documents: Zambian veterinary import permit (accompanies the animal)
Official health certificate meeting the permit conditions (UK model: exam within 48 hours, valid 7 days)
Rabies vaccination certificate
Owner declaration of 6 months' residence in the exporting country or since birth (UK)

countries.name: Zimbabwe
countries.summary: UK official guidance (revised Dec 2023) says no dog or cat may enter Zimbabwe except under an import permit from the Director of Veterinary Services, Harare. The pet needs an official health certificate (exam within 48 hours, valid 7 days). Rabies vaccination is not a pre-export condition, but dogs not vaccinated before arrival must be vaccinated by a Government Veterinary Officer, and pre-travel vaccination is advised.
countries.microchip: Not stated in official sources. Microchip recommended.
countries.parasite_treatment: Exam within 48 hours before export must find the pet free of external parasites (UK EHC 3929).
countries.import_permit: Required (UK NFG 3929). Director of Veterinary Services, P.O. Box CY 66, Causeway, Harare (tel +263 4 791 355 per UK guidance; 242-791516 per Wikiprocedure). Non-official sources report a written application stating breed, age and origin with the rabies certificate, a US$150 fee and 3–5 days' processing. Claimed SADC exemptions are unverified.
countries.timeline: Plan at least 2–3 weeks for a vaccinated pet: apply for the import permit (3–5 days reported) → vet exam within 48 hours of export and government endorsement → travel.
countries.authority: Department of Veterinary Services (Ministry of Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development), Harare
vaccinations: Rabies: not mandatory before export per UK guidance. If given, within 12 months before export. All dogs in Zimbabwe must be rabies-vaccinated; unvaccinated dogs must be vaccinated by a Government Veterinary Officer after arrival. Pre-travel vaccination is recommended.
Other vaccinations: the UK OV must be satisfied that 'necessary vaccinations' were done.
documents: Zimbabwe import permit (permit number entered on the certificate)
Official health certificate (UK model: exam within 48 hours, valid 7 days)
Rabies vaccination certificate (if vaccinated)
Owner declaration: not imported into the exporting country in the past 6 months (UK)
